papers.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding (Leviathan et al.)
papers.idea: Original draft-then-verify with rejection sampling that provably preserves the target distribution; small AR drafter proposes gamma tokens, target verifies in one parallel pass.
papers.numbers: 2-3.4x on T5-XXL; speedup formula (1-alpha^(gamma+1))/((1-alpha)(gamma*c+1)) introduced alpha (acceptance) and cost-ratio c.
papers.long_context_behavior: Not evaluated beyond short seq2seq/LM benchmarks (<2K). Drafter carries its own full KV cache, so drafting cost grows with context; no accounting for KV-bound regimes.

papers.title: Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling (Chen et al.)
papers.idea: Independent concurrent discovery of speculative sampling; modified rejection sampling for nucleus/temperature; 4B drafter for Chinchilla-70B.
papers.numbers: 2-2.5x on Chinchilla 70B (XSum, HumanEval) in a distributed TPU serving setting.
papers.long_context_behavior: Not evaluated beyond ~2K contexts; no long-context analysis.

papers.title: SpecTr: Fast Speculative Decoding via Optimal Transport
papers.idea: Formulates multi-draft token selection as discrete optimal transport with membership cost; derives efficiently computable transport plan achieving (1-1/e)-approximation of optimal acceptance probability with K parallel drafts.
papers.numbers: 2.13x wall-clock, 1.37x over single-draft speculative decoding on PALM-2 benchmarks.
papers.long_context_behavior: Pure distribution-level theory; no dependence on context length modeled and no long-context experiments.

papers.title: Blockwise Parallel Decoding for Deep Autoregressive Models (Stern et al.)
papers.idea: k auxiliary output heads propose a block of future tokens verified by the base model in one pass — the ancestor of Medusa-style draft heads and block drafting.
papers.numbers: ~3.3x fewer decoding iterations, ~2x wall-clock on machine translation.
papers.long_context_behavior: Pre-LLM era; sequences of a few hundred tokens only.

papers.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
papers.idea: Multiple independent FFN heads off the last hidden state predict tokens at offsets +1..+k; candidates verified via tree attention; optional 'typical acceptance' relaxation (lossy).
papers.numbers: Medusa-1 (frozen backbone) 2.2x; Medusa-2 (joint finetune) 2.3-3.6x on Vicuna/Zephyr chat benchmarks.
papers.long_context_behavior: Trained and evaluated on short chat data (<4K). Heads condition only on last hidden state so drafter memory is constant, but acceptance degrades on long inputs (documented by SpecExtend/LongSpec follow-ups); tree verification still pays full target KV cost.

papers.title: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty
papers.idea: Single-layer autoregressive head operating at feature (penultimate hidden state) level with token-shift disambiguation; static draft tree; lossless verification.
papers.numbers: 2.7-3.5x on LLaMA2-Chat 70B; ~2x over Lookahead, ~1.6x over Medusa at the time.
papers.long_context_behavior: Draft head keeps its own growing feature-KV cache (adds memory at long context); trained on <4K data. Later studies (LongSpec, OWL, SpecExtend) show acceptance length collapses at 8K-100K+ inputs.

papers.title: EAGLE-2: Faster Inference of Language Models with Dynamic Draft Trees
papers.idea: Replaces EAGLE's static tree with confidence-calibrated dynamic draft trees (drafter confidence approximates acceptance probability), reranking and expanding the tree per step.
papers.numbers: 3.05-4.26x speedup, 20-40% over EAGLE-1; acceptance length ~4-5.5 tokens on MT-Bench/HumanEval.
papers.long_context_behavior: Same short-context training regime as EAGLE; SGLang production data shows throughput drops below 1.0x at batch ~24; long-context acceptance decay inherited from EAGLE-1; not evaluated beyond ~4K.

papers.title: EAGLE-3: Scaling up Inference Acceleration of Large Language Models via Training-Time Test
papers.idea: Drops feature-prediction loss for direct token prediction; fuses low/mid/high-layer target features via 'training-time test' so drafter quality scales with training data.
papers.numbers: Up to 6.5x vs AR, ~1.4x over EAGLE-2; in SGLang on H100 keeps +38% throughput at batch 64 (EAGLE-2 regresses to 0.93x at batch 24). Production default in vLLM/SGLang/TensorRT-LLM by 2026.
papers.long_context_behavior: Still trained on short data. OWL (2510.07535) measures EAGLE-3 on long-context inputs: acceptance collapses and generation can slow to 0.81x of AR; drafter KV grows with context. Long-context is EAGLE-3's known failure mode.

papers.title: OWL: Overcoming Window Length-Dependence in Speculative Decoding for Long-Context Inputs
papers.idea: Length-robust drafting: LSTM drafter conditioned only on the final token's hidden state (no growing drafter KV), a [SPEC] token that enriches verifier representations for the drafter, and hybrid tree/non-tree decoding.
papers.numbers: ~5x higher acceptance length than EAGLE-3 on long-context inputs; introduces LongSpecBench; shows EAGLE-3 dropping to 0.81x on long inputs.
papers.long_context_behavior: Explicitly built for 8K-100K+ inputs: drafter state is O(1) in context length by construction; acceptance roughly length-independent. One of the few papers with a dedicated long-context spec-decode benchmark.

papers.title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Train with layer dropout + early-exit loss so early layers become a competent drafter; self-speculative decoding where draft and verify share weights and KV cache (exit-layer KV reused).
papers.numbers: 2.16x on CNN/DM summarization, 1.82x coding, 2.0x semantic parsing (Llama2 variants).
papers.long_context_behavior: Not evaluated beyond ~4K. Shared KV between draft and verify means no extra drafter KV, which is inherently long-context friendly, but early-layer acceptance at 32K+ is unmeasured.

papers.title: Draft & Verify: Lossless Large Language Model Acceleration via Self-Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Drafter = target model with a Bayesian-optimization-selected static set of skipped intermediate layers; zero extra parameters or memory.
papers.numbers: Up to ~1.99x (CodeLLaMA/LLaMA-2-13B), typically 1.4-1.7x.
papers.long_context_behavior: Short-context benchmarks only (<4K); skipped-layer set is fixed per task, not adapted to context length; drafting still attends over full KV so drafting cost grows with context.

papers.title: SWIFT: On-the-Fly Self-Speculative Decoding for LLM Inference Acceleration
papers.idea: Plug-and-play layer-skipping self-speculation with an online optimization phase that discovers the optimal skipped-layer set per input stream, then an acceleration phase.
papers.numbers: 1.3-1.6x while preserving output distribution; token acceptance rates 98-100% on LLaMA-2/CodeLLaMA.
papers.long_context_behavior: Evaluated on standard <4K benchmarks; no long-context evaluation. Drafting attends over the full (unsparsified) KV, so gains shrink in KV-bound regimes.

papers.title: CLaSp: In-Context Layer Skip for Self-Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Training-free per-step dynamic programming over which layers to skip, using the full hidden states of the last verification step as the objective; layer-skip schedule adapts continuously during generation.
papers.numbers: 1.3-1.7x on LLaMA-3 series, lossless.
papers.long_context_behavior: Not evaluated at long context; DP objective uses last-step hidden states so it adapts to content but the drafter still pays full-KV attention cost at 32K+.

papers.title: QuantSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding with Hierarchical Quantized KV Cache
papers.idea: Drafter = target architecture with 4-bit weights and hierarchical 4-bit KV cache; verification with full-precision KV. Directly attacks the long-context KV-loading bottleneck; custom CUDA kernels for quantized-KV attention.
papers.numbers: >90% acceptance rate; up to ~2.5x end-to-end; ~1.3x memory reduction vs other self-spec baselines; quantized attention kernel up to 2.88x vs FP16 FlashAttention.
papers.long_context_behavior: Designed for long-context edge inference: drafter KV is 4x smaller but still grows linearly with context; acceptance stays >90% at evaluated long-context settings (LongBench-scale, up to ~32K). Nothing shown at 128K+.

papers.title: Vegas: Self-Speculative Decoding with Verification-Guided Sparse Attention
papers.idea: Co-designs sparse attention with self-speculation: critical KV entries are identified for free from attention computed during the verification phase, then reused to sparsify drafting attention — no separate KV-selection pass.
papers.numbers: 1.25-2.81x vs default vLLM; 1.15-1.29x vs SOTA sparse-attention methods; gains from higher acceptance plus near-zero selection overhead.
papers.long_context_behavior: Built for long-context memory-bound decoding; drafter KV budget is sparse and verification stays full-KV (lossless). Exact max context in experiments not stated in abstract; targets vLLM-scale serving contexts.

papers.title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding (SparseSpec-L)
papers.idea: Training-free self-speculation from a dynamically sparsified, recallable KV cache: attention statistics from full-context verification act as importance signals, evicted tokens can be reactivated (nothing permanently dropped), and an entropy-based controller sets speculation length per step.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.79x end-to-end across long-context tasks and model scales; includes a unified analysis showing longer speculation horizons hurt when marginal acceptance falls below relative drafting cost.
papers.long_context_behavior: Long-context-native: addresses the sparse-drafter acceptance drift problem via recallable (not permanent) eviction; verification remains full-KV so lossless. Extreme lengths (256K+) unreported.

papers.title: REST: Retrieval-Based Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Model-free drafting: exact suffix matching against a static datastore builds a draft trie verified by tree attention; no drafter training or extra parameters.
papers.numbers: 1.62-2.36x on HumanEval/MT-Bench (7B/13B models).
papers.long_context_behavior: Drafting cost is independent of context length (no drafter KV), which is length-robust by construction, but retrieval is from an external corpus, not the prompt; not evaluated on long-context inputs.

papers.title: Prompt Lookup Decoding (PLD)
papers.venue: GitHub (apoorvumang); shipped in HF transformers and vLLM (ngram speculator)
papers.idea: Draft by copying the continuation of an n-gram matched inside the prompt itself; zero model, zero memory, verified losslessly.
papers.numbers: 2-4x on input-grounded tasks (summarization, doc QA, code editing); no gain on open-ended generation.
papers.long_context_behavior: Actually improves with longer grounded contexts (more copyable material) and adds zero drafter KV — one of the few methods trivially safe at 1M tokens — but acceptance is task-dependent and there is no formal long-context study.

papers.title: Break the Sequential Dependency of LLM Inference Using Lookahead Decoding
papers.idea: Jacobi-iteration parallel trajectories generate disjoint n-grams cached in a pool; verification branch checks pooled n-grams; drafting FLOPs traded for steps without any draft model.
papers.numbers: Up to 1.8x on MT-Bench; up to 4x with strong scaling across GPUs on code completion.
papers.long_context_behavior: Not evaluated at long context; the extra-wide attention window per step multiplies the already KV-bound attention cost, so the FLOPs-for-steps trade worsens as context grows.

papers.title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications
papers.idea: Model-free drafting from suffix trees built over the current prompt and previous outputs; adaptive speculation length scales to hundreds of tokens when patterns repeat (agentic pipelines, SQL, self-refine loops).
papers.numbers: Up to 5.3x on agentic benchmarks (SWE-Bench, AgenticSQL); 2.8x faster than EAGLE-2/3, 1.9x faster than Token Recycling; shipped in vLLM via ArcticInference.
papers.long_context_behavior: No drafter KV at all and suffix-tree ops are cheap, so drafting is length-independent; verification still pays full target KV cost. Long agentic contexts are the target workload, though no explicit 128K+ ablation.

papers.title: TokenSwift: From Hours to Minutes — Lossless Acceleration of Ultra-Long Sequence Generation up to 100K Tokens
papers.idea: Targets ultra-long GENERATION (not input): multi-token drafting heads + n-gram retrieval + tree verification, with dynamic KV management and anti-repetition handling as the sequence being generated grows to 100K.
papers.numbers: >3x consistent speedup on 1.5B-14B models (MHA and GQA); 100K-token generation cut from ~5 hours to ~90 minutes on LLaMA-3.1-8B (4K prefix).
papers.long_context_behavior: The complement of long-input work: KV growth comes from the model's own output; handles KV cache updates and repetitive-generation collapse across 100K generated tokens losslessly.

papers.title: SpecInfer: Accelerating Generative LLM Serving with Tree-based Speculative Inference and Verification
papers.idea: First token-tree verification system: multiple small drafters propose a speculated token tree, verified in one pass with tree attention against the target; integrated into a serving system (FlexFlow).
papers.numbers: 1.5-2.8x for distributed inference, 2.6-3.5x for offloading-based inference.
papers.long_context_behavior: Not evaluated at long context; tree attention cost multiplies with context length, and later work (LongSpec) shows naive tree attention becomes inefficient on long prefixes.

papers.title: Sequoia: Scalable, Robust, and Hardware-aware Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Dynamic programming finds the optimal speculation tree topology; sampling-without-replacement verification is robust across temperatures; hardware-aware optimizer picks tree size/depth per platform.
papers.numbers: Up to 4.04x (Llama2-7B) / 3.73x (13B) on A100; up to 9.96x with offloading on L40.
papers.long_context_behavior: Tree optimizer models hardware, not context length; experiments at standard short contexts. The DP tree framework is orthogonal to and later reused by long-context systems.

papers.title: SpecExec: Massively Parallel Speculative Decoding for Interactive LLM Inference on Consumer Devices
papers.idea: For offloading regimes where one target pass costs seconds: build a huge (thousands-node) draft tree from a strong drafter's top-probability paths, deterministically 'pre-executing' the likely continuations.
papers.numbers: 4-6 tokens/s for Llama-2-70B (4-bit) on a consumer RTX 4090 with RAM offloading; on the order of 10-18x over offloaded AR decoding.
papers.long_context_behavior: Offloading focus, short contexts; giant trees multiply verification attention cost with context length, so the approach is untested where KV, not weights, dominates.

papers.title: DiffuSpec: Unlocking Diffusion Language Models for Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Repurposes a pretrained diffusion LM as a parallel drafter — multi-token proposals in a single forward pass — with causal-consistency path search and adaptive draft length, verified by a standard AR target.
papers.numbers: Up to 3x wall-clock speedup; positioned as training-free alternative to AR drafters.
papers.long_context_behavior: Not evaluated at long context; DLM drafter has its own bidirectional attention over the context, so drafting cost grows quadratically with input length — unaddressed.

papers.title: DFlash: Block Diffusion for Flash Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Lightweight block-diffusion drafter conditioned on context features extracted from the target model generates an entire draft block in one forward pass, removing the sequential drafting bottleneck of AR/EAGLE drafters.
papers.numbers: >6x lossless acceleration; up to 2.5x higher speedup than EAGLE-3. Spawned a 2026 follow-up wave (DDTree/2604.12989 draft trees, DFlare/2606.02091 draft capacity scaling, D2SD/2606.04446 dual drafters, DeLS-Spec/2607.07409 long-short context experts, Spec-AUF/2607.01893 accept-until-fail training).
papers.long_context_behavior: Short/medium-context benchmarks (math, code, dialogue); conditioning on target features sidesteps some drafter-KV growth but no 32K+ evaluation reported; long-context behavior of diffusion drafters is an open question.

papers.title: TriForce: Lossless Acceleration of Long Sequence Generation with Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Hierarchy attacks both bottlenecks: target model with retrieval-based sparse KV (chunked KV selected by attention) self-drafts against full-KV verification; a tiny StreamingLLM-cache model drafts for the sparse-KV middle layer.
papers.numbers: 2.31x on A100 for Llama2-7B-128K at 128K context; 7.78x with offloading on 2x RTX 4090; Llama2-13B at 128K served at 0.226 s/token offloaded.
papers.long_context_behavior: The canonical long-context result: evaluated AT 128K; retrieval KV selection keeps acceptance high (~constant KV budget ~4K) as context scales; established that at long context the target-with-sparse-KV is a better drafter than a small model.

papers.title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Theory + system showing that in long-context, large-batch regimes decoding is KV-bound, so a StreamingLLM-cache (constant-KV) drafter — even the target itself with sparse KV — yields speedup that GROWS with batch size, inverting conventional wisdom that spec decode dies at large batch.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.51x for LLaMA-3.1-8B at batch sizes 32-256 on sequences in the 8K-32K+ range; provides an analytical model for optimal drafting strategy vs (batch, seqlen).
papers.long_context_behavior: Long-context is the entire premise: draft-to-target cost ratio shrinks as batch/context grow because both are dominated by KV loading; drafter KV is O(1) via attention sink + sliding window. Foundation for production long-context spec decode.

papers.title: LongSpec: Long-Context Lossless Speculative Decoding with Efficient Drafting and Verification
papers.idea: Purpose-built long-context drafter: constant-sized KV (sink + sliding window), Anchor-Offset position indices to fix the train-short/test-long position mismatch, and Hybrid Tree Attention that splits verification into Flash-decoded prefix + dense tree suffix.
papers.numbers: Up to 3.26x over strong FlashAttention baselines across five long-context datasets; 2.25x wall-clock reduction on AIME24 long reasoning with QwQ.
papers.long_context_behavior: Evaluated at 32K-100K+ input scales; explicitly diagnoses the three long-context failure modes (drafter KV memory, short-train/long-test mismatch, tree-attention inefficiency) and fixes each; also covers long-reasoning generation.

papers.title: SpecExtend: A Drop-in Enhancement for Speculative Decoding of Long Sequences
papers.idea: Training-free retrofit for existing draft models: FlashAttention/hybrid tree attention for prefill+verification, plus Cross-model Retrieval — the TARGET model's attention scores select which KV entries the small drafter keeps.
papers.numbers: 2.37x/2.22x over standard SD at 8K/16K inputs; up to 2.84x on 16K summarization and 3.86x on long reasoning; 2.02-2.09x for EAGLE-based frameworks; documents that vanilla SD degrades sharply even at 8K.
papers.long_context_behavior: Directly measures early long-context degradation (acceptance drop at 8-16K) of vanilla and EAGLE pipelines and restores speed without retraining; evaluated to 16K, not 128K.

papers.title: RAPID: Long-Context Inference with Retrieval-Augmented Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: RAG drafter: a drafter (same-size or even LARGER than the target) runs on a retrieval-shortened context and speculates for the long-context target; 'upward speculation' can transfer knowledge so verification also improves quality.
papers.numbers: ~2x speedups on long-context targets (LLaMA-3.1/Qwen-2.5 8B-72B) while IMPROVING generation quality — a lossy-by-design departure from strict losslessness.
papers.long_context_behavior: Long-context native (evaluated at 32K-128K-scale inputs): drafter cost is decoupled from context length via retrieval; acceptance depends on retrieval recall; blurs the acceleration/quality line.

papers.title: BudgetDraft: Acceptance-Aware Multi-View Training for Sparse-KV Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Trains the drafter under MULTIPLE sampled KV budgets simultaneously (multi-view sparse training) with an acceptance-aware loss against a full-cache teacher, yielding one drafter robust across runtime KV budgets set by memory/concurrency/SLO.
papers.numbers: 6.55x / 4.46x / 2.10x vs AR at 4K / 8K / 16K on PG-19, LongBench, LWM.
papers.long_context_behavior: Targets the sparse/full mismatch that grows with context; explicitly shows acceptance recovery across sparsity levels as context lengthens, but evaluation stops at 16K.

papers.title: Dustin: Draft-Augmented Sparse Verification for Efficient Long-Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Flips the sparsity to the VERIFICATION side: draft-model lookahead signals plus target attention history pick the critical KV subset for verification, with importance scoring restricted to a few attention heads to bound overhead.
papers.numbers: 27.85x self-attention speedup and 9.17x end-to-end decoding speedup on Qwen2.5-72B at 32K (PG-19, LongBench), reported with negligible accuracy loss.
papers.long_context_behavior: Evaluated at 32K on a 72B model; sparse verification means the output is no longer bit-exact to full-KV target — trades strict losslessness for attacking the dominant verification-KV bottleneck.

papers.title: SpecKV: Adaptive Speculative Decoding with Compression-Aware Gamma Selection
papers.idea: Studies the spec-decode x KV-quantization interaction: mean acceptance is stable across FP16/INT8/NF4 (~0.70) but acceptance at large draft length degrades differently, so the optimal gamma must adapt to the compression level; proposes compression-aware gamma selection.
papers.numbers: Optimal gamma shifts from 2-4 (FP16) to 6-8 (INT8) to 4-6 (NF4); mean acceptance ~0.69-0.70 across precisions.
papers.long_context_behavior: KV compression is a long-context enabler, but the paper's context-length coverage is modest; its contribution is the first quantified coupling between KV precision and draft length, not a 128K result.

papers.title: Optimizing Speculative Decoding for Serving Large Language Models Using Goodput (SmartSpec)
papers.idea: Under continuous batching, fixed-length speculation can INCREASE latency at high load; SmartSpec picks per-request speculation length by maximizing estimated goodput (accepted tokens/sec given system load and measured acceptance).
papers.numbers: Up to 3.2x average request latency reduction vs non-speculative baselines across request rates; works with model-based, prompt-lookup, and tree speculators; basis for vLLM dynamic speculation.
papers.long_context_behavior: Load-aware, not length-aware: goodput model captures batch occupancy but not KV-boundedness vs context length; combining goodput control with MagicDec-style length-dependent acceptance models remains open.

papers.title: Batch Speculative Decoding Done Right
papers.idea: Shows that batched speculative decoding implementations are subtly WRONG (ragged tensors, padding/alignment cause output divergence from AR baseline) and provides a correctness-first exact batched implementation.
papers.numbers: Correctness audit across open-source implementations; exactness restored with competitive throughput (headline numbers are correctness violations found, not a speedup claim).
papers.long_context_behavior: Correctness issues compound with long, variably-sized contexts in a batch (more raggedness); no explicit long-context study.

papers.title: Speculative Speculative Decoding (Saguaro)
papers.idea: Removes the draft/verify serialization: while verification runs, the drafter predicts the likely verification outcome and pre-drafts for it; on a correct guess the next batch of draft tokens is ready at zero perceived drafting cost.
papers.numbers: ~30% faster than optimized speculative decoding baselines on average; up to 5x vs AR on open-source engines.
papers.long_context_behavior: Scheduling-level idea, orthogonal to context length; long-context regimes where verification latency dominates make outcome-prediction overlap MORE valuable, but this is not separately evaluated.

papers.title: A Theoretical Perspective for Speculative Decoding Algorithm
papers.idea: Abstracts spec decode as a Markov chain; gives exact characterization of the distribution of rejections/output quality, proves optimality properties of the rejection-sampling scheme, and quantifies batched speedup vs draft quality tradeoffs.
papers.numbers: Closed-form expected-rejection formulas in terms of draft-target TV distance; no new system numbers.
papers.long_context_behavior: Distribution-level theory with no context-length dependence; acceptance-vs-length drift observed empirically in long-context work has no counterpart here.

papers.title: Speculative Decoding Speed-of-Light: Optimal Lower Bounds via Branching Random Walks
papers.idea: Connects tree speculation to branching random walks and proves a ceiling on accepted tokens per iteration: E[X] <= (mu + mu_2) log(P) / mu^2 + O(1), where P is verifier capacity (tree size) and mu reflects output-distribution entropy — speculation gains are only LOGARITHMIC in verifier parallelism.
papers.numbers: Tight bounds validated empirically on Llama models; explains diminishing returns of ever-larger draft trees (Sequoia/SpecExec regimes).
papers.long_context_behavior: No explicit context dependence, but the entropy parameter mu is task/context-dependent; long grounded contexts (low-entropy continuations) raise the ceiling, consistent with PLD/SuffixDecoding behavior.

papers.title: When Is a Draft Accepted? A Theory of Acceptance in Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Characterizes rejection regions of common acceptance criteria as lower level sets of the target distribution; exact KL-divergence-to-rejection certificates for strict greedy, additive/multiplicative relaxed, top-m, and tree acceptance rules — a unified lens on lossless vs lossy verification.
papers.numbers: Analytical certificates; no system benchmarks.
papers.long_context_behavior: No context-length dependence analyzed; relevant to long-context work because sparse verification (Dustin) and relaxed acceptance (Medusa typical, RAPID) need exactly these divergence certificates.

trends: The field split into two regimes with opposite physics: short-context weight-bound decoding (EAGLE-3/DFlash arms race chasing 5-7x via better heads and parallel drafting) and long-context KV-bound decoding, where those same SOTA heads actively hurt — OWL measures EAGLE-3 at 0.81x (slower than AR) on long inputs while its acceptance length collapses ~5x.

Long-context spec decode converged on one recipe: constant-or-sparse-KV drafter + full-KV lossless verification (TriForce retrieval-KV, MagicDec StreamingLLM-KV, LongSpec sink+sliding-window, QuantSpec 4-bit KV, BudgetDraft budget-robust training, SparseSpec-L recallable eviction). The 2026 frontier moved sparsity into verification itself (Dustin, Vegas), formally abandoning bit-exactness for the dominant bottleneck.

Speculative decoding and sparse attention are merging into a single co-design problem: verification-phase attention scores are recycled as the drafter's KV-importance oracle (Vegas, SparseSpec-L, SpecExtend's cross-model retrieval), so the target model continuously tells the drafter what to keep — no separate selection pass, no training.

Batch-size folklore was inverted for long context: MagicDec showed draft/target cost ratio FALLS with batch size in KV-bound regimes, so speedup grows with batch — enabling production adoption. By 2026 EAGLE-3, DeepSeek-style MTP heads, ngram/suffix speculators, and goodput-adaptive speculation length are stock features in vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM.

The train-short/test-long mismatch is now treated as a first-class problem: position-index remapping (LongSpec Anchor-Offset), length-independent drafter state (OWL's LSTM on final hidden state), multi-budget sparse training (BudgetDraft), and dedicated benchmarks (LongSpecBench) replaced the old practice of training drafters on <4K chat data and hoping.

Block-diffusion drafting matured from curiosity to SOTA in one year: DFlash (>6x, 2.5x over EAGLE-3, ICML 2026) plus a follow-up wave (DDTree, DFlare, D2SD, Spec-AUF, DeLS-Spec) — single-forward-pass drafting eliminates sequential drafting latency, the last AR bottleneck on the draft side.

Model-free retrieval drafting owns the agentic/repetitive-workload niche: SuffixDecoding (5.3x, 2.8x over EAGLE-3, shipping in vLLM ArcticInference) and PLD have zero drafter KV, making them the only approaches that are trivially length-robust to 1M tokens; TokenSwift extends the same toolbox to 100K-token GENERATION.

Theory caught up to practice: optimal-transport multi-draft verification (SpecTr line), Markov-chain speedup laws (NeurIPS 2024), level-set acceptance certificates (2606.30265), and a log(P) ceiling on accepted tokens per step via branching random walks (2512.11718) — collectively proving that draft length and tree width have sharply diminishing returns, which adaptive-gamma systems (SmartSpec, SpecKV, SparseSpec-L's entropy controller) exploit operationally.

The interaction between KV-cache compression and speculation is now quantified rather than anecdotal: quantized-KV drafters hold >90% acceptance (QuantSpec), the optimal draft length shifts systematically with KV precision (SpecKV), and permanent eviction is understood to cause acceptance drift via saliency shift — motivating recallable/non-destructive sparsity.
open_problems: Nothing is evaluated at 256K-1M tokens: TriForce's 128K (2024) remains the high-water mark; the 2026 wave (BudgetDraft 16K, Dustin/LongSpec 32K-100K) stops far short of the 1M-context models being served, and acceptance/speedup behavior there — especially for hybrid linear-attention/SSM targets whose drafting economics differ — is unmapped.

Acceptance drift over long generations: sparse-KV drafters' importance estimates go stale as decoding proceeds (saliency shift); recallable eviction (SparseSpec-L) is a heuristic fix, and there is no principled online refresh policy with acceptance guarantees, particularly for 100K-token reasoning traces.

Sparse verification breaks losslessness with no certification: Dustin-style sparse-KV verification gives ~9x end-to-end but the output distribution is no longer the target's; level-set acceptance theory (2606.30265) has not been connected to KV-sparsity-induced divergence, so there is no way to certify 'negligible accuracy loss' claims.

Composability is unmodeled: KV quantization, eviction, sparse attention, and speculation each perturb acceptance; SpecKV only covers gamma-vs-precision. No unified roofline/acceptance model predicts end-to-end speedup when stacking all four in one serving engine at a given (batch, context, budget) point.

Long-context + large-batch + tree speculation kernels: tree attention over ragged 100K-context batches is immature (LongSpec's hybrid attention is single-request-oriented), and batched spec decode was shown to be silently incorrect in major implementations as late as 2025 (2510.22876) — correctness plus performance at scale is unsolved.

Draft-head state growth is an uncharacterized Pareto frontier: EAGLE-style heads carry growing feature-KV, while constant-state drafters (OWL LSTM, sliding-window) trade acceptance for O(1) memory; nobody has mapped acceptance-vs-drafter-memory as a function of context length.

Theory has no context-length axis: all acceptance theory (OT, Markov-chain, log(P) bounds) assumes fixed draft/target distributions; empirically acceptance decays with input length and retrieval quality (RAPID), but no theory ties alpha to context length, KV budget, or retrieval recall.

Scheduling speculation under disaggregated prefill/decode serving: goodput-based control (SmartSpec) ignores KV-boundedness vs length, MagicDec's analytical model ignores load; unifying them for SLO-aware speculation at 100K+ contexts, and deciding when to fall back (OWL shows negative speedups exist), is open.

Diffusion drafters at long context: DFlash-class drafters beat EAGLE-3 at short context, but their bidirectional attention over long prompts and their conditioning-feature pipelines have no 32K+ evaluation; whether block-diffusion drafting survives KV-bound regimes is unknown.

Quality-improving ('upward') speculation blurs the contract: RAPID accelerates AND improves outputs by speculating with a larger RAG drafter — once verification is deliberately lossy, the community lacks agreed evaluation for the speed/quality/faithfulness triangle in long-context tasks.

papers.title: LongSpec: Long-Context Lossless Speculative Decoding with Efficient Drafting and Verification
papers.idea: Long-context-native drafter with a constant-sized (sliding/anchor) KV cache, position indices that fix the train-inference mismatch when the drafter window is shorter than the target context, and an attention aggregation scheme combining fast prefix computation with standard tree attention.
papers.long_context_behavior: Explicitly built for long context: drafter KV is O(1) in context length so drafter memory does not grow with 32K-1M contexts; targets the failure mode that SOTA drafters are trained on <4K-token texts.
papers.numbers: Up to 3.26x speedup over FlashAttention baselines on five long-context datasets; 2.34x wall-clock reduction on four math reasoning tasks with QwQ (long-CoT). Source: aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.83 and arxiv.org/abs/2502.17421.

papers.title: OWL: Overcoming Window Length-Dependence in Speculative Decoding for Long-Context Inputs (+ LongSpecBench)
papers.year: 2025 (late-2025; heavily cited by 2026 long-context spec-decode work; no 2026 venue confirmed)
papers.idea: LSTM-based drafter conditioned only on the final token's state so it is context-length-invariant; adds a [SPEC] token to the verifier for richer drafter conditioning; hybrid tree/non-tree decoding. Releases LongSpecBench, the long-context spec-decoding benchmark used by 2026 follow-ups.
papers.long_context_behavior: Directly measures acceptance drift: EAGLE-3 degrades to 0.81x (a slowdown) on long-context inputs because its acceptance collapses beyond the trained context window; OWL's last-token-state conditioning avoids window-length dependence.
papers.numbers: ~5x higher acceptance length than EAGLE-3 on long-context inputs; EAGLE-3 baseline at 0.81x generation speed on long contexts. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2510.07535.

papers.title: Vegas: Self-Speculative Decoding with Verification-Guided Sparse Attention
papers.idea: Self-speculation where the critical KV entries identified as a byproduct of the full-KV verification pass are recycled to define the sparse-attention mask used for drafting the next chunk — no separate KV-selection algorithm and no separate drafter.
papers.long_context_behavior: Designed for the long-context memory-bound regime; drafting loads only the verification-selected sparse KV subset, so drafter-side KV traffic stays roughly constant while the full cache is touched only at verification.
papers.numbers: 1.25x-2.81x throughput over default vLLM; 1.15x-1.29x over SOTA sparsity-based self-speculative methods. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2602.07223.

papers.title: Dustin: Draft-Augmented Sparse Verification for Efficient Long-Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Attacks the verification side: fuses draft-model lookahead attention signals with the target's historical attention into a global importance map, selects a fixed-size KV set, and verifies with only that compressed target KV; importance scoring is restricted to a minimal subset of attention heads.
papers.long_context_behavior: Premise is that KV-cache loading dominates verification latency at long context; evaluated at 32K sequence length with selective token retention across multi-step verification windows.
papers.numbers: 27.85x self-attention speedup and 9.17x end-to-end decoding speedup at 32K with negligible accuracy degradation. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2606.24957.

papers.title: SpecPV: Improving Self-Speculative Decoding for Long-Context Generation via Partial Verification
papers.year: 2025-12 (v1 Dec 2, 2025; part of the 2026 sparse-verification wave)
papers.idea: Self-speculation where most verification steps use partial KV states (fast) and full-KV verification is applied intermittently to bound error accumulation.
papers.long_context_behavior: Identifies verification, not drafting, as the dominant constraint as context grows; NOTE: admits 'minor degradation' in output quality, i.e., not strictly lossless — a key caveat vs Dustin/Vegas.
papers.numbers: Up to 6x decoding acceleration vs autoregressive on LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-series. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2512.02337.

papers.title: BudgetDraft: Acceptance-Aware Multi-View Training for Sparse-KV Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Trains a drafter that is robust across deployment-time KV budgets by exposing it to multiple sampled sparse-KV views during training, each aligned to a shared full-cache teacher, combining acceptance-aware loss (full branch) with multi-view loss (sparse branches).
papers.long_context_behavior: Documents that naive sparse-KV drafting suffers acceptance collapse to near-zero as context grows 4K->16K due to sparse/full mismatch; multi-view training preserves acceptance across budgets, but evaluation stops at 16K — behavior at 32K+ unmeasured.
papers.numbers: 6.55x end-to-end vs autoregressive at 4K, 4.46x at 8K, 2.10x at 16K. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2606.00144.

papers.title: SparseSpec: Accelerating Large-Scale Reasoning Model Inference with Sparse Self-Speculative Decoding (PillarAttn)
papers.venue: MLSys 2026 (arXiv 2512.01278); Zhao, Tang, Kasikci, Han, Stoica et al.
papers.idea: Self-speculation for long-generation reasoning models: the target model drafts using PillarAttn, a sparse attention mechanism selecting critical tokens, co-designed with system machinery — unified batch scheduling, delayed verification for CPU/GPU overlap, and dynamic KV-cache management.
papers.long_context_behavior: Targets long chain-of-thought generations where decoding becomes memory-bound as generated KV grows; drafter reuses the target's own KV cache sparsely, so no separate drafter KV.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.13x throughput vs vanilla decoding for reasoning workloads. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2512.01278, mlsys.org 2026 program.

papers.title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding (SparseSpec-L)
papers.idea: Train-free self-speculation: drafts with a dynamically sparsified but recallable KV cache (dense cache never discarded), recycling per-head attention statistics from full-context verification as the importance signal, plus an entropy-based controller for adaptive speculation length.
papers.long_context_behavior: Built for long-context inference; because the dense KV is retained and tokens are recallable, acceptance can recover from importance-estimation errors that would permanently hurt eviction-based approaches.
papers.numbers: Reports consistent end-to-end acceleration over autoregressive decoding (abstract's specific max figure not machine-readable on fetch). Source: arxiv.org/abs/2607.27735.

papers.title: SSV: Sparse Speculative Verification for Efficient LLM Inference (v1 titled SpecSA: Bridging Speculative Decoding and Sparse Attention)
papers.idea: Resolves the structural mismatch between multi-token speculative verification and query-specific dynamic sparse attention (NSA-style) via overlap-aware grouped-query execution, refresh/reuse NSA kernel fusion, and profile-guided prompt-adaptive orchestration to maximize KV-block reuse across verification queries.
papers.long_context_behavior: Aimed at long-context NSA decoding where each verification query would otherwise trigger its own sparse KV selection; cross-query KV-block reuse keeps sparse verification cost sublinear in draft width.
papers.numbers: 3.49x end-to-end throughput over autoregressive NSA decoding; 6.86x kernel-level speedups on H100. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2605.19893.

papers.title: STS: Efficient Sparse Attention with Speculative Token Sparsity
papers.idea: Training-free: repurposes the draft model's attention scores as a predictor of target-model token importance, dynamically building a token-and-head-wise sparsity mask that prunes target attention — draft model accelerates both drafting and target attention.
papers.long_context_behavior: Evaluated on long-document QA (NarrativeQA); relies on draft-target attention-importance correlation, which is the same signal family whose long-range stability Attention Drift (2605.09992) questions.
papers.numbers: 2.67x speedup at ~90% sparsity with negligible accuracy loss. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2605.15508.

papers.title: Predict, Reuse, and Repair: Accelerating Dynamic Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Decoding
papers.idea: Applies speculation to the KV-block-selection step itself: an EMA-based predictor exploits temporal locality of dynamic sparse attention selections, attention is speculatively computed over predicted blocks while true selection runs, and missed blocks are merged afterwards via an online-softmax FlashAttention repair kernel.
papers.long_context_behavior: Pure long-context decode optimization — removes block-selection latency from the critical path without changing which blocks are attended, so accuracy of the underlying sparse method is preserved at any context length.
papers.numbers: Up to 40% per-token decoding latency reduction with maintained downstream accuracy. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2606.30389.

papers.title: VeriCache: Turning Lossy KV Cache into Lossless LLM Inference
papers.idea: The 'drafter' is the same model running on a compressed KV cache (token dropping or quantization); full-KV verification runs against an off-GPU (CPU/PCIe/network) copy, overlapping compressed-KV decoding (HBM-bound) with full-KV swaps (PCIe-bound).
papers.long_context_behavior: Directly targets the 32K-1M regime where full KV cannot fit in HBM (~327GB at 1M); because compressed-KV outputs stay close to full-KV outputs, drafting horizons are an order of magnitude longer than model-based drafters, amortizing each swap.
papers.numbers: Up to 4x throughput over full-KV inference with bit-identical outputs; sustains 25-40 accepted tokens per verification round vs 2-3 for small-model drafters. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2605.17613.

papers.title: When Hidden States Drift: Can KV Caches Rescue Long-Range Speculative Decoding? (KVShot)
papers.idea: Diagnostic study showing EAGLE-style hidden-state reuse is lossy context compression that suppresses information needed for multi-step drafting; KVShot compares hidden-only, KV-only, and hybrid reuse paradigms for letting the drafter read the target's KV cache.
papers.long_context_behavior: Core finding for KV-aware drafting: KV-reuse improves long-range acceptance but end-to-end speedups remain marginal under current training pipelines — bottlenecks are shallow drafters' poor target-query estimation and sparse gradients into draft-side KV projections; argues for block-wise training.
papers.numbers: Qualitative: KV-reuse improves long-range acceptance; e2e speedup marginal (no headline multiplier claimed). Source: arxiv.org/abs/2604.26412.

papers.title: SpecLA: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Linear-Attention Models
papers.idea: Runtime making chain/tree speculative decoding work on stateful linear-attention targets: topology-aware verification kernels respect recurrent dependencies, and compact factors produced during verification recover the accepted-state trajectory without full recomputation; paired with an EAGLE-style drafter plus confidence pruning.
papers.long_context_behavior: Linear-attention targets have O(1) state instead of growing KV, so context length does not inflate memory — but speedups are well below Transformer-target spec decoding, since verification must serially respect recurrence.
papers.numbers: Up to 1.70x end-to-end over autoregressive on a public GDN-1.3B target (H100). Source: arxiv.org/abs/2607.16673.

papers.title: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding in Hybrid Language Models
papers.idea: Uses the SSM/linear-attention components of hybrid models as internal drafters (no external draft model), and shows that architectural composition — parallel (Mamba-2 + attention in each layer) vs sequential (interleaved layers) — determines speculative viability.
papers.long_context_behavior: Does not evaluate long context, but is the reference point for drafting on the hybrid architectures (Falcon-H1, Qwen3.5-style interleaved) that dominate 2026 long-context model design.
papers.numbers: Parallel hybrid (Falcon-H1): acceptance alpha=0.68 at k=2 greedy; sequential hybrid (Qwen3.5): alpha=0.038 (18x gap); LayerSkip-style early exit recovers ~12x higher acceptance for sequential hybrids; results scale-invariant 0.5B->3B. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2605.01106.

papers.title: Attention Drift: What Autoregressive Speculative Decoding Models Learn
papers.idea: Shows EAGLE-style drafters' attention progressively drifts off the prompt onto their own generated tokens as chain depth grows, because drafter hidden-state magnitude grows monotonically (drafter acts like extra target layers); fixes with post-norm on drafter hidden states and per-hidden-state RMSNorm.
papers.long_context_behavior: Drift explains why draft heads degrade on long contexts and perturbed prompts; the norm fixes let short-training-depth drafters generalize over longer drafting sequences — 1.18x gain specifically on long-context tasks.
papers.numbers: 2x acceptance-length improvement under template perturbation; 1.18x on long-context tasks; 1.10x across seven standard benchmarks. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2605.09992.

papers.title: P-EAGLE: Faster LLM Inference with Parallel Speculative Decoding in vLLM
papers.venue: vLLM blog (2026-03-13), production feature in vLLM; also in SGLang tracking (sgl-project/sglang#23171)
papers.idea: Replaces EAGLE's autoregressive draft loop with a single-forward-pass parallel drafter: a 4-layer head with learnable mask-token embeddings and shared hidden states across positions produces all K draft tokens at once.
papers.long_context_behavior: Serving-grade but trained on <=8K-ish sequences (median 3,891, P90 10,800 on UltraChat) with a sequence-partition trick for training memory; vLLM/SGLang ecosystem consensus in 2026 is that EAGLE-3-family heads still lose acceptance beyond the trained context window (>32K).
papers.numbers: Up to 1.69x over vanilla EAGLE-3 on B200; +55-69% throughput at concurrency 1, +5-25% at concurrency 64; optimal speculation depth K=7 vs K=3 for EAGLE-3; heads released for GPT-OSS 120B/20B, Qwen3-Coder 30B. Source: vllm.ai/blog/2026-03-13-p-eagle.

papers.title: Learning to Draft: Adaptive Speculative Decoding with Reinforcement Learning
papers.idea: Formulates the draft-and-verify loop as an RL environment with two co-adaptive policies controlling drafting and verification scheduling, directly optimizing wall-clock throughput per cycle instead of proxy metrics like acceptance length.
papers.long_context_behavior: Not long-context specific; relevant because static speculation-length policies are exactly what breaks when acceptance drifts with context length.
papers.numbers: 2.24x-4.32x speedups; up to 36.4% over EAGLE-3. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2603.01639, iclr.cc/virtual/2026/poster/10010314.

papers.title: DFlash: Block Diffusion for Flash Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Lightweight block-diffusion drafter generates an entire draft block in one forward pass, conditioned on context features extracted from the target model to keep acceptance high; verified losslessly by the target.
papers.long_context_behavior: Evaluated on standard (short-context) reasoning/coding/chat tasks; drafter conditions on target features so its own context handling is shallow — long-context acceptance behavior unreported.
papers.numbers: Over 6x lossless acceleration across models/tasks; up to 2.5x higher speedup than EAGLE-3. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2602.06036.

papers.title: SpecDiff-2: Scaling Diffusion Drafter Alignment For Faster Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Discrete-diffusion drafter with novel calibration techniques aligning the non-autoregressive drafter's distribution with the autoregressive verifier, attacking both the drafting-parallelism bottleneck and draft-verifier misalignment rejections.
papers.long_context_behavior: Benchmarks are reasoning/coding/math — long-context alignment of diffusion drafters is untested; no drafter-KV analysis given (diffusion drafter re-encodes block context per pass).
papers.numbers: Up to +55% average tokens/sec over previous SOTA baselines; up to 5.5x average over standard decoding, lossless. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2511.00606, mlsys.org/virtual/2026/oral/3755.

papers.title: Fail Fast, Win Big: Rethinking the Drafting Strategy in Speculative Decoding via Diffusion LLMs (FailFast)
papers.idea: Uses off-the-shelf diffusion LLMs as drafters without fine-tuning; because dLLM drafting cost is roughly independent of draft length, it dynamically 'fails fast' (short drafts) in hard regions and extends drafts aggressively in easy regions.
papers.long_context_behavior: Adaptive speculation length is the mechanism most relevant to long-context acceptance variance, but evaluation is on standard benchmarks; long-context untested.
papers.numbers: Up to 4.9x over vanilla autoregressive decoding, 1.7x over naive dLLM drafting, 1.7x faster than EAGLE-3; accepts up to 70 tokens in one round. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2512.20573.

papers.title: Spec-AUF: Accept-Until-Fail Training under Train-Inference Misalignment for Masked Block Drafters
papers.idea: Training objective for masked block drafters (DFlash/Domino-style): truncate cross-entropy supervision at the drafter's first predicted failure, matching inference where everything after the first rejection is discarded; shows position-decay weighting becomes inert once AUF truncates loss support.
papers.long_context_behavior: Training-objective work; no long-context evaluation — but directly addresses the train-inference misalignment class of problems that also underlies long-context acceptance drift.
papers.numbers: DFlash drafter average emitted length 2.40 -> 2.61 tokens; Domino two-branch head 2.56 -> 2.68, gains on every benchmark tested (six). Source: arxiv.org/abs/2607.01893.

papers.title: Draft Less, Retrieve More: Hybrid Tree Construction for Speculative Decoding (Graft)
papers.idea: Prune-then-graft: dynamic-depth pruning removes marginal branches of the dense EAGLE-style draft tree, and retrieved (n-gram) tokens are grafted into the freed positions, so retrieval compensates pruning-induced coverage loss at near-zero overhead.
papers.long_context_behavior: Evaluates short-context, long-context generation, and large-model settings (per abstract); retrieval branch naturally benefits from long inputs (more copyable spans), though no acceptance-vs-context curve is given.
papers.numbers: Up to 5.41x speedup on short-context benchmarks; +21.8% average over EAGLE-3 on Qwen3-235B; preliminary extension to DFlash-style block drafting. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2605.20104.

papers.title: AdaPLD: Adaptive Retrieval and Reuse for Efficient Model-Free Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Model-free (PLD-style) drafting upgraded with lexical + semantic-similarity retrieval and branched multi-hypothesis drafts instead of single copied spans, training-free and drafter-free.
papers.long_context_behavior: Zero drafter KV by construction (no draft model), making it trivially long-context-safe on the draft side; verification cost unchanged, so target KV loading still dominates at 32K+.
papers.numbers: Up to 3.10x decoding speedup, fewer target forward passes. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2606.05742.

papers.title: Speculative Speculative Decoding (Saguaro)
papers.venue: ICLR 2026 (arXiv 2603.03251, v3 May 2026); Kumar, Dao, May
papers.idea: Parallelizes the speculate and verify phases themselves: while verification of draft block t runs, the drafter predicts likely verification outcomes and pre-emptively speculates continuations for them, removing the sequential draft-verify dependency.
papers.long_context_behavior: Orthogonal to context length; at long context where verification latency grows (KV-bound), hiding drafting under verification becomes more valuable, but the paper reports no context-scaling study.
papers.numbers: ~30% faster on average (up to 2x) than optimized speculative decoding baselines; up to 5x over autoregressive in open-source engines. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2603.03251, openreview.net/forum?id=aL1Wnml9Ef.

papers.title: When Is a Draft Accepted? A Theory of Acceptance in Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Acceptance theory beyond distribution-preserving verification: characterizes rejection regions as lower level sets of the target distribution and derives exact KL certificates and sharp margin-based bounds for strict greedy, additive/multiplicative relaxed acceptance, top-m, entropy-thresholded, and tree criteria (when the target greedy token stays covered by the drafter's top-m).
papers.long_context_behavior: No context-length dependence treated — the theory of how acceptance margins evolve with context length remains open.
papers.numbers: Empirical: on Qwen3, relaxed and tree criteria substantially enlarge the certified-acceptance region, especially at low target-margin decoding steps. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2606.30265.

papers.title: ReSpec: Towards Optimizing Speculative Decoding in Reinforcement Learning Systems
papers.idea: Integrates speculative decoding into RL post-training rollouts (75%+ of training time): dynamically tunes speculation config, evolves the drafter online via knowledge distillation as the actor updates, and weights drafter updates by rollout rewards to avoid policy degradation.
papers.long_context_behavior: Long-CoT rollout generation is the target workload; notes speedup diminishes at large batch sizes and drafters go stale under continual actor updates — both worse for long generations.
papers.numbers: Up to 4.5x rollout speedup on Qwen 3B-14B with preserved reward convergence and training stability. Source: mlsys.org/virtual/2026/oral/3836.

trends: Sparse attention and speculative decoding have merged into one design space in 2026: the dominant long-context pattern is 'draft with sparse/compressed KV, verify with (or against) full KV' — Vegas (ICML'26), Dustin (ICML'26), BudgetDraft, SparseSpec (MLSys'26), SparseSpec-L, SpecPV, STS, VeriCache all instantiate it, differing mainly in where the importance signal comes from (verification attention stats, draft attention, EMA of block selections) and whether evicted KV is recallable.

Self-speculation is displacing independent drafters at long context because a separate drafter's KV grows with context; the target model with a sparse view of its own KV is drafter-KV-free by construction. Where a separate mechanism is kept, it is either constant-KV by design (LongSpec's sliding-window drafter, OWL's LSTM last-token-state drafter) or model-free retrieval (AdaPLD).

KV compression as the drafter (VeriCache) changes the acceptance economics: compressed-KV self-drafts sustain 25-40 accepted tokens per verification round vs 2-3 for small-model drafters, because output divergence from lossy KV accumulates slowly — making speculation the mechanism that converts lossy KV compression into lossless inference.

Verification, not drafting, is now identified as the long-context bottleneck (KV loading dominates); 2026 responses are sparse verification (Dustin: 9.17x e2e at 32K), partial verification with periodic full passes (SpecPV, at the cost of losslessness), sparse-computation verification over attention/FFN/MoE (arXiv 2512.21911), and kernel-level co-design with NSA-style sparse attention (SSV: 3.49x over AR NSA).

Block-diffusion drafters are supplanting autoregressive draft heads as the SOTA drafting architecture: DFlash (ICML'26, >6x, 2.5x over EAGLE-3), DFlare (5.5x), SpecDiff-2 (MLSys'26 oral, 5.5x), FailFast (70-token accepts, adaptive length exploiting length-independent dLLM draft cost), with dedicated training objectives emerging (Spec-AUF accept-until-fail loss).

The scheduling layer is being parallelized and learned: SSD/Saguaro (ICLR'26) overlaps speculation with verification; P-EAGLE (vLLM, production) makes EAGLE drafting single-pass and pushes optimal depth from K=3 to K=7; Learning-to-Draft (ICLR'26) replaces static speculation-length heuristics with RL on wall-clock throughput; ReSpec (MLSys'26 oral) brings spec decoding into RL rollout generation with reward-weighted drafter distillation.

A science of drafters is forming: Attention Drift shows EAGLE-style drafters behave like extra target layers whose attention drifts off the prompt with chain depth (norm fixes give 1.18x long-context gains); KVShot shows hidden-state reuse is lossy context compression and KV-reuse helps acceptance but not yet wall-clock; acceptance theory (2606.30265) now gives margin-based certificates for relaxed/top-m/tree criteria; even security enters — adversarial suffixes can collapse acceptance for +62.3% latency (ADSD, arXiv 2607.21804).

Speculative decoding is being ported off the pure-Transformer target: linear-attention targets (SpecLA: topology-aware tree verification with state recovery, 1.70x on GDN-1.3B) and hybrid Mamba-attention models (component-aware self-spec: parallel hybrids draft well at alpha=0.68, sequential interleaved hybrids collapse to alpha=0.038), plus FPGA Mamba verification (SpecMamba lineage).

Long-context spec-decode evaluation is standardizing: OWL's LongSpecBench and the documented failure of EAGLE-3 beyond its trained window (0.81x slowdown; sparse drafting acceptance collapsing to near-zero at 16K in BudgetDraft) are now the shared motivation across the 2026 papers; production stacks (vLLM/SGLang/TensorRT-LLM) shipped EAGLE-3/P-EAGLE but acknowledge >32K degradation.
open_problems: Acceptance drift beyond the drafter's trained window remains unsolved at scale: EAGLE-3 goes sub-1x on long inputs (OWL), and no 2026 paper reports acceptance curves at 128K-1M — the best sparse-KV drafting evaluations stop at 16K (BudgetDraft) or 32K (Dustin); the 100K+ regime is essentially unmeasured.

KV-aware drafting works in principle but not in wall-clock: KVShot (2604.26412) shows KV-reuse improves long-range acceptance yet end-to-end speedup is marginal because shallow drafters cannot estimate target queries and draft-side KV projections get sparse gradients — block-wise training pipelines for KV-reading drafters are an explicitly stated open direction.

Lossless sparse verification is not settled: SpecPV concedes 'minor degradation' (not lossless), Dustin's guarantees are empirical ('negligible' at 32K), and sparse/full acceptance collapse (BudgetDraft: near-zero acceptance at 16K for naive sparse drafting) shows the sparse-view mismatch grows with context — budget-robust drafting past 32K is unproven.

Drafting for sequential hybrid architectures is broken: interleaved linear+full-attention models yield alpha=0.038 self-spec acceptance vs 0.68 for parallel hybrids (2605.01106); since 2026 long-context frontier models are mostly hybrids, a drafting mechanism that survives sequential composition is a major gap.

Speculation on stateful (linear/SSM) targets lags far behind: SpecLA reaches only 1.70x because tree verification must respect recurrent state dependencies and accepted-state recovery is expensive — efficient tree speculation with O(1)-state targets is open.

Long-context behavior of block-diffusion drafters is unknown: DFlash/DFlare/SpecDiff-2/FailFast are evaluated on short-context reasoning/coding; whether single-pass diffusion drafts conditioned on target features hold acceptance at 32K+ inputs, and how their per-block re-encoding cost scales, is untested.

Throughput-regime speculation is still weak: gains shrink at high concurrency (P-EAGLE drops to +5-25% at c=64; ReSpec notes diminishing returns at large batch), and the batch-size x context-length x KV-budget operating surface for when speculation beats plain batching has no accepted theory or scheduler.

Acceptance theory has no context dependence: the 2026 acceptance-certificate framework (2606.30265) covers relaxed/top-m/tree criteria but says nothing about how target-distribution margins — hence certified acceptance — evolve with context length or retrieval position, leaving long-context acceptance prediction empirical.

Robustness and security of speculation are new and unaddressed: adversarial prompt suffixes collapse draft-target alignment for +62.3% mean sample time with quality preserved (ADSD, 2607.21804), a DoS vector for every deployed spec-decode stack with no published defense; relatedly, drafter staleness under continually-updated targets (RL training, online distillation in ReSpec) lacks principled solutions.

Composability of the 2026 stack is unexplored: sparse-KV self-drafting (Vegas), sparse verification (Dustin/SSV), overlap scheduling (SSD/Saguaro), and diffusion drafting each claim 2-9x in isolation, but no work composes them or characterizes interference (e.g., verification-guided sparsity signals disappear once verification itself is sparse).

surveys.theme: Self-speculative decoding and early exit: drafting from within the target model itself (layer-skip subset selection, early-exit heads, shared-weight/quantized/sparse-KV self-drafting) — how the draft path is chosen or trained, KV-cache sharing, acceptance, real speedups, and behavior at 32K-1M context

papers.title: Draft & Verify: Lossless Large Language Model Acceleration via Self-Speculative Decoding (Zhang et al.)
papers.idea: Drafter = target model with a static set of skipped intermediate (attention+FFN) layers found by Bayesian optimization on a calibration set; verification by the full model; zero extra parameters, zero extra memory.
papers.numbers: Up to 1.99x (CodeLLaMA-13B), typically 1.4-1.7x; ~92% token acceptance; skip set fixed per task.
papers.long_context_behavior: Benchmarks <4K only. Skip set is calibrated on short data and never adapted to context length; the draft pass still attends over the FULL KV in every retained layer, so drafting cost converges to the attention-bound cost of retained layers as context grows — speedup ceiling shrinks in KV-bound regimes. No drafter-side KV overhead (shared cache) is the one long-context-friendly property.

papers.title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding (Elhoushi et al.)
papers.idea: Train with layer dropout + early-exit loss (shared LM head at every layer) so the first E layers become a competent drafter; self-speculative decoding where draft and verify share weights AND the exit-layer KV cache is reused by verification.
papers.numbers: 2.16x on CNN/DM summarization, 1.82x on HumanEval coding, 2.0x on TOPv2 semantic parsing (Llama-2 variants); acceptance ~67-76% per external measurements.
papers.long_context_behavior: Not evaluated beyond ~4K. Draft/verify KV sharing means zero extra drafter memory — structurally the most long-context-friendly drafting design — but early-layer acceptance at 32K+ is unmeasured, and the training recipe (layer dropout + exit loss) has only been applied to short-context pretraining/finetuning mixes. No LayerSkip checkpoints exist for 128K-context models.

papers.title: Kangaroo: Lossless Self-Speculative Decoding for Accelerating LLMs via Double Early Exiting
papers.idea: Fixed shallow sub-network (early exit) as the self-drafter with a small trained adapter bridging to the full model's representations; second 'early exit' halts drafting mid-round when token confidence drops below a threshold to avoid wasted draft steps.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.04x wall-time on Spec-Bench; 88.7% fewer additional parameters than Medusa; adapter-only training.
papers.long_context_behavior: Short-context (Spec-Bench) only. Shallow sub-network shares the target's first-layers KV (no duplicate drafter KV), but adapter was trained on short data; confidence-threshold draft stopping has never been characterized when acceptance drifts with input length.

papers.title: EESD: Speculative Decoding via Early-exiting for Faster LLM Inference with Thompson Sampling Control Mechanism
papers.idea: Drafter = first N layers (recommended 5-10% of depth; 5 of 80 layers for 70B) plus one extra transformer layer trained by self-distillation on SlimPajama+self-generated text; Thompson sampling adaptively sets draft length per round.
papers.numbers: 2.29x GSM8K / 1.86x XSum on LLaMA-2-70B; 2.45x HumanEval on CodeLLaMA-13B; beats Medusa (1.73-1.97x) and Draft&Verify-style Self-SD (1.23-1.37x); 481M-1.12B trainable params.
papers.long_context_behavior: Output length capped at 512 tokens; all inputs short. TS draft-length control is the kind of mechanism long-context acceptance drift needs, but it was tuned/validated only in stationary short-context regimes.

papers.title: S3D: A Simple and Cost-Effective Self-Speculative Decoding Scheme for Low-Memory GPUs
papers.idea: Mid-layer skipping combined with simultaneous multi-token prediction as the self-draft path, targeting VRAM-constrained GPUs where a separate drafter or quantized big model would slow decoding up to 7x.
papers.numbers: Among top speedup-per-memory ratios (external survey lists 1.77-3.86x range); Phi-3-based SD model 1.4-2x faster than quantized EAGLE under memory limits.
papers.long_context_behavior: Short-context only; low-memory setting makes long context doubly hostile (KV competes with weights for VRAM) but this interaction is not studied.

papers.title: Draft on the Fly: Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding using Cosine Similarity (Metel et al.)
papers.idea: Training-free, per-input construction of the layer-skip draft model using simple rules on cosine similarity between successive layer hidden states — the first fully plug-and-play adaptive skip-set selector, precursor to CLaSp/KnapSpec.
papers.numbers: Competitive with SOTA self-speculative methods (no single headline multiplier in abstract).
papers.long_context_behavior: Not evaluated at long context; cosine-similarity layer redundancy profiles are computed on the current (short) input — whether they hold at 32K+ positions is exactly what KnapSpec later formalizes but still doesn't measure past 32K.

papers.title: SWIFT: On-the-Fly Self-Speculative Decoding for LLM Inference Acceleration
papers.idea: Two-phase plug-and-play layer skipping: an optimization phase runs interval Bayesian optimization + random search per input stream (using the LLM's own generated tokens as ground truth) to find the skip set, then an acceleration phase exploits it.
papers.numbers: 1.3-1.6x lossless; token acceptance 98-100% on LLaMA-2/CodeLLaMA; no training, no auxiliary model.
papers.long_context_behavior: Standard <4K benchmarks. Skip set is frozen after the optimization phase, so it goes stale over long generations; drafting attends over full KV, so gains shrink in KV-bound regimes. KnapSpec (ICML 2026) shows SWIFT reaches 1.33x vs its 1.47x on 16K-input GovReport with Llama3.1-70B.

papers.title: CLaSp: In-Context Layer Skip for Self-Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Training-free per-step dynamic programming over which layers to skip, using full hidden states of the last verification step as the DP objective, so the skip schedule adapts continuously during generation.
papers.numbers: 1.24-1.73x on LLaMA-3 series, lossless.
papers.long_context_behavior: Not evaluated at long context; the per-step DP adds overhead that grows with hidden-state work, and the drafter still pays full-KV attention. KnapSpec measures CLaSp at 1.22x on 16K GovReport (70B), below SWIFT — dynamic re-selection does not automatically win at longer inputs.

papers.title: DEL: Context-Aware Dynamic Exit Layer for Efficient Self-Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Plug-and-play controller that tracks, online, the would-be token acceptance rate of every candidate exit layer and heuristically picks exit layer + speculation length per sequence context (both are task- and context-dependent).
papers.numbers: 2.16-2.62x over AR decoding; up to +0.19x over best static self-spec baselines (peak 2.43x).
papers.long_context_behavior: Short-context evaluation; per-layer acceptance tracking is the right primitive for length-induced drift but was never run on 32K+ inputs. KnapSpec reports DEL 'fails to provide acceleration' on base (non-instruct) models in its long-input setting.

papers.title: PPSD: Pipeline Parallelism is All You Need for Optimized Early-Exit Based Self-Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Configures the model's layers as a pipeline so early-exit drafting of token t+1 executes concurrently with final-layer verification of token t (verify-while-draft), hiding drafting latency entirely at fixed acceptance/exit position.
papers.numbers: 2.01-3.81x across benchmarks; claims near-optimal acceleration for a given (acceptance rate, exit layer) pair.
papers.long_context_behavior: No long-context evaluation; pipelining changes the latency accounting but not the KV economics — both pipeline stages attend over the same growing cache, and stage balance shifts as attention time grows with context.

papers.title: CAS-Spec: Cascade Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Builds a HIERARCHY of self-drafters from dynamically switchable acceleration strategies (layer sparsity, activation quantization) inside one model; a Dynamic Tree Cascade algorithm routes among draft levels and assigns draft lengths from acceptance/latency predictions.
papers.numbers: 1.1-2.3x average over AR; DyTC +47%/+48% over cascade-based and tree-based baselines.
papers.long_context_behavior: Short-context; cascade routing assumes stationary per-level acceptance, precisely what breaks under context-length drift. First work to compose two internal-drafting axes (sparsity x quantization), but without any KV-side sparsity.

papers.title: DVI: Draft, Verify, and Improve — Toward Training-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Partitions the LLM into drafter (early exit) and verifier and turns deployment into continual learning: every verification outcome supervises the exit head online via a KL-then-RL schedule (online distillation + reward-masked CE + policy gradient).
papers.numbers: 2.16x on Spec-Bench, on par with EAGLE-2, with orders-of-magnitude less training data; lossless, single-model deployment.
papers.long_context_behavior: Short-context; but online drafter adaptation is the only published mechanism that could in principle track acceptance drift across a 100K-token generation — never tested there.

papers.title: Mirror Speculative Decoding: Breaking the Serial Barrier in LLM Inference (Mirror-SD, Apple)
papers.idea: Launches branch-complete rollouts from the target's own early-exit signals in parallel with the target's suffix computation, mapped across heterogeneous accelerators (draft on NPU, target on GPU), plus multi-token speculative streaming in the drafter — bidirectional speculation rather than serial draft-then-verify.
papers.numbers: 2.8-5.8x wall-time on SpecBench across 14B-66B models; +30% average over EAGLE-3.
papers.long_context_behavior: SpecBench is short-context; heterogeneous execution assumes the early-exit branch is compute-light, but at 32K+ both branches become KV-bandwidth-bound on their respective devices — NPU KV capacity for the draft branch is the unexamined constraint.

papers.title: Speculative Streaming: Fast LLM Inference without Auxiliary Models
papers.idea: Fuses drafting into the target by changing the finetuning objective to future n-gram prediction with multi-stream attention: extra speculative streams inside the same forward pass draft interdependent future tokens (unlike Medusa's independent heads); single model, tree drafting.
papers.numbers: On-par/higher speedups than Medusa-style approaches with ~10,000x fewer extra parameters; designed for resource-constrained/on-device deployment.
papers.long_context_behavior: Short-context finetuning and eval; speculative streams add per-stream attention over the shared cache, so stream cost grows with context; no 32K+ report.

papers.title: QuantSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding with Hierarchical Quantized KV Cache
papers.idea: Drafter = same architecture with W4 weights and the upper 4 bits of a hierarchical INT4/INT8 KV cache; target verification reconstructs INT8 KV from upper+lower nibbles — one shared KV representation, no duplicate drafter cache, custom quantized-attention kernels.
papers.numbers: Acceptance 91-94%; end-to-end 1.35x (4K) -> 2.08x (32K) -> 2.23x (64K) -> 2.49x (128K); ~1.3x memory reduction vs sparse-KV self-spec baselines; evaluated on Llama-2-7B-32K and LWM-Text-Chat-128K (PG19, Multi-LexSum, InfiniteBench-Sum) on 8x A6000.
papers.long_context_behavior: One of only two self-spec methods actually measured AT 128K: acceptance does NOT decay with length (92.18% at 64K, 94.31% at 128K) and speedup GROWS with context because the setting becomes KV-bandwidth-bound — direct counterexample to the assumption that all self-spec degrades with length. Drafter KV still grows linearly (at 4-bit); nothing beyond 128K.

papers.title: TriForce: Lossless Acceleration of Long Sequence Generation with Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Target model WITH retrieval-selected sparse KV (~4K budget) self-drafts against full-KV verification; a StreamingLLM-cache tiny model drafts for the sparse-KV middle level — established that at long context the target-with-sparse-KV beats a small model as drafter.
papers.numbers: 2.31x on A100 at 128K (Llama2-7B-128K); 7.78x with offloading on 2x RTX 4090; 0.226 s/token for 13B at 128K offloaded.
papers.long_context_behavior: The canonical 128K self-drafting result; retrieval KV selection keeps acceptance high at constant budget as context scales. Still the joint high-water mark (with QuantSpec) — nothing published at 256K+; SparseSpec (MLSys 2026) reports beating it by 1.76x on reasoning workloads where its static retrieval budget is stale.

papers.title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Analytical model + system showing decoding at long context/large batch is KV-bound, so a constant-KV (StreamingLLM) drafter — including the target itself with sparse KV — yields speedup that grows with batch size.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.51x for LLaMA-3.1-8B at batch 32-256 on 8K-32K+ sequences; closed-form drafting-strategy selector vs (batch, seqlen).
papers.long_context_behavior: Foundation of long-context self-drafting economics; but its static sink+window budget fails on reasoning workloads with shifting saliency — SparseSpec (MLSys 2026) measures MagicDec underperforming due to 'lack of adaptivity to high context dynamics in RLMs.'

papers.title: SpecPV: Improving Self-Speculative Decoding for Long-Context Generation via Partial Verification
papers.idea: Flips sparsity to the verification side of a (nominally self-) speculative loop: most verification steps run on a partial KV (sink + query-retrieved blocks + local window + buffer, budgets 2K/4K/8K), with full-KV verification triggered periodically (buffer overflow) to flush accumulated error. NOTE: the draft module is actually EAGLE-3, not layer skip.
papers.numbers: LLaMA-3.1-8B: 2.88x at 10K -> 6.29x at 60K (2K budget) vs 3.11x for EAGLE3-YARN at 60K; accepted length ~3.57 tokens/step, flat across budgets; evaluated 10K-60K on PG-19, LongBench v1/v2; Qwen3 4B/8B/14B.
papers.long_context_behavior: Shows verification, not drafting, dominates at long context — but it is NOT lossless: GovReport ROUGE-L falls 77.3 -> 56.1 (-27%) at 2K budget while QA stays within 1-3% of full verification; the 'minor degradation' claim is task-dependent, and the full-verify schedule is a fixed heuristic with no drift detector.

papers.title: SparseSpec: Accelerating Large-Scale Reasoning Model Inference with Sparse Self-Speculative Decoding (PillarAttn)
papers.idea: Target model drafts for itself using PillarAttn, a sparse attention that selects critical tokens by dumping attention scores from the verification pass via custom kernels (zero selection overhead); draft and target share weights and one KV cache; co-designed with unified batch scheduling, delayed verification (CPU/GPU overlap), dynamic KV management.
papers.numbers: Average accepted length 6.16 of 8 drafted tokens (k=8) on reasoning workloads where EAGLE-3 and n-gram accept <2; up to 2.13x throughput vs vLLM at batch up to 256; 1.36x over MagicDec, 1.56x over vLLM-NGram, 1.76x over TriForce; Qwen3-1.7B/8B/14B on H100s, outputs 10K-13K tokens (AIME/OlympiadBench/LiveCodeBench).
papers.long_context_behavior: Long-GENERATION native: KV growth comes from the model's own CoT; verification-recycled selection adapts to shifting saliency that breaks MagicDec/TriForce static budgets. The only serving-grade (batch 256, TP) self-spec system published. Input contexts are short; 100K+ inputs untested.

papers.title: Vegas: Self-Speculative Decoding with Verification-Guided Sparse Attention
papers.idea: Critical KV entries are identified for free from attention logits computed during the full-KV verification pass (averaged over first-draft + bonus token queries, then across heads; top-k), and drafting attends only over those entries; mask refreshes every verification step; same weights, one KV cache, lossless.
papers.numbers: 1.25-2.81x over default vLLM; 1.15-1.29x over SOTA sparse baselines (MagicDec-Stream/Quest, SpecExtend); ~7% drafting sparsity; Qwen3-4B/8B/30B and gpt-oss-20b; LongBench-v2 requests of 96K-120K tokens plus long-output AIME25 (~19.7K generated) and CodeElo.
papers.long_context_behavior: The longest-input self-spec evaluation published (96K-120K): verification-guided selection keeps draft acceptance above static-budget baselines at ~100K, and drafter-side KV traffic stays ~constant while full KV is touched only at verification. Nothing at 256K+; batch-scaling beyond vLLM defaults not mapped.

papers.title: KnapSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding via Adaptive Layer Selection as a Knapsack Problem
papers.idea: Skip-set selection as 0/1 knapsack over DECOUPLED attention and MLP sublayers, with each sublayer's hardware latency modeled as a function of the CURRENT context length; parallel DP re-solves every 64 steps (128 for >10B models, ~7.5% overhead); first proof that hidden-state cosine similarity is a sound proxy for token acceptance rate.
papers.numbers: Up to 1.47x (Llama3.1-70B GovReport, ~16K inputs) vs SWIFT 1.33x / CLaSp 1.22x; DEL fails on base models; acceptance 85-97% (93.5% AIME24 Qwen3-32B); cosine-sim proxy correlates 0.837 with throughput vs 0.538 for raw acceptance; reasoning generation up to 32K tokens (AIME24/25).
papers.long_context_behavior: The only layer-skip work that makes context length an explicit variable — in the LATENCY model (attention cost grows with context, so the optimal skip set shifts toward skipping attention sublayers as context grows).
