But acceptance-vs-context is still not measured beyond ~16K-input / 32K-generation, and even the context-aware optimum yields only 1.47x because retained layers still attend over full KV.

papers.title: ConfLayers: Adaptive Confidence-based Layer Skipping for Self-Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Training-free iterative skip-set construction from per-layer confidence scores against an adaptive threshold — no learned policy, no Bayesian optimization phase.
papers.numbers: Up to 1.4x over vanilla generation.
papers.long_context_behavior: No long-context claims or evaluation; inherits full-KV drafting cost.

papers.title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding (SparseSpec-L)
papers.idea: Drafts from a dynamically sparsified but RECALLABLE KV cache (sink + recent + top-mid by per-head attention statistics recycled from full-context verification; dense cache never discarded, evicted tokens can be reactivated), plus an entropy-EMA controller that picks per-step speculation length maximizing expected step-wise efficiency.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.79x (LongBench-v2, Llama-3.1-8B); 2.60x InfiniteBench; 1.55-2.79x across 3B-14B (Llama-3.1/3.2, Qwen2.5); acceptance 52-84.6%; avg accepted tokens/step 5.60-13.01 (adaptive: 11.26); ~10% KV ratio; contexts up to 64K; baselines include EAGLE-3, MagicDec, RAPID, LayerSkip.
papers.long_context_behavior: Long-context native to 64K; recallable eviction bounds the damage from stale importance estimates that permanently hurt eviction-based drafting. Lossless (full-KV verification). 128K+ unreported; controller has no drift guarantee.

papers.title: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding in Hybrid Language Models
papers.idea: Uses the SSM/linear-attention subgraphs of hybrid models as zero-cost internal drafters and shows the COMPOSITION PATTERN (parallel Mamba-2+attention per layer vs sequentially interleaved layers) — not the mere presence of linear components — determines self-speculation viability; perplexity-degradation ratio predicts alpha.
papers.numbers: Parallel hybrid (Falcon-H1): alpha=0.68 at k=2 greedy; sequential hybrid (Qwen3.5-style): alpha=0.038 — an 18x gap; LayerSkip-style early exit recovers ~12x acceptance for sequential hybrids; PPL-degradation 3.15x <-> alpha=0.37 (k=4) vs 81.96x <-> alpha=0.019; scale-invariant 0.5B->3B.
papers.long_context_behavior: No long-context evaluation, but it is the reference point for drafting on the hybrid architectures that dominate 2026 long-context model design; leaves open both LayerSkip-style training for hybrids and SSM-state rollback for rejected drafts.

papers.title: DEX: Depth Exploration for LLM Decoding
papers.idea: Instead of selecting one exit depth, explores multiple candidate depths in parallel via an expand-commit-collapse lattice, validating candidates against final-depth predictions and retaining only reusable branch states — sidesteps the exit-too-early (fallback cost) vs exit-too-late (wasted compute) tradeoff.
papers.numbers: Beats depth-selection baselines; competitive end-to-end throughput vs speculative and distributed decoding (no headline multiplier in abstract).
papers.long_context_behavior: No long-context evaluation; multi-depth branch states multiply activation/KV bookkeeping, cost at 32K+ unexamined.

papers.title: VeriCache: Turning Lossy KV Cache into Lossless LLM Inference
papers.idea: Same model on a compressed KV cache (dropping/quantization) is the drafter; full-KV verification runs against an off-GPU copy, overlapping HBM-bound compressed decoding with PCIe-bound full-KV swaps — bit-identical outputs.
papers.numbers: Up to 4x throughput over full-KV inference; 25-40 accepted tokens per verification round vs 2-3 for small-model drafters.
papers.long_context_behavior: Explicitly targets 32K-1M where full KV cannot fit in HBM (~327GB at 1M for the models discussed); long drafting horizons amortize each swap. The closest thing to a 1M-regime self-spec design, though headline evaluations remain far below 1M.

papers.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report (Multi-Token Prediction module used as self-drafter)
papers.idea: MTP module (one extra transformer block sharing the trunk and embedding/output head) trained during pretraining predicts token t+2; at inference it is repurposed as a shared-weight speculative drafter — production-scale proof that training-time self-drafting heads survive deployment.
papers.numbers: Acceptance of the second-token prediction 85-90% across generation topics; ~1.8x decoding TPS improvement.
papers.long_context_behavior: Model serves 128K contexts but the report gives no acceptance-vs-context breakdown; MTP head conditions on trunk hidden state (no separate drafter KV). Long-context MTP acceptance in production remains unpublished.

papers.title: OWL: Overcoming Window Length-Dependence in Speculative Decoding for Long-Context Inputs
papers.idea: (Context anchor for this theme) Documents that EAGLE-3 acceptance collapses beyond the trained window — the failure that motivates self-drafting at long context — and fixes it with an O(1)-state LSTM drafter conditioned on the final token's hidden state plus a [SPEC] token.
papers.numbers: EAGLE-3 drops to 0.81x of AR speed on long-context inputs; OWL ~5x higher acceptance length than EAGLE-3; introduces LongSpecBench.
papers.long_context_behavior: Establishes the quantitative baseline every 2026 long-context self-spec paper cites: trained-short draft heads go SUB-1x at 8K-100K+, whereas shared-weight self-drafters (QuantSpec/TriForce/Vegas) hold acceptance because the drafter IS the target.

evidence: QuantSpec (ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.10424): acceptance does NOT decay with context for weight/KV-quantized self-drafting — 91.64% at 16K, 90.99% at 32K, 92.18% at 64K, 94.31% at 128K on LWM-Text-Chat-128K; end-to-end speedup GROWS with context: 1.35x (4K) -> 2.08x (32K) -> 2.23x (64K) -> 2.49x (128K); draft and target share one hierarchical INT4/INT8 KV representation (draft reads upper 4 bits) so there is no duplicate drafter KV.

SpecPV (arXiv 2512.02337): partial-KV verification speedup scales with context — LLaMA-3.1-8B vs AR: 2.88x at 10K -> 6.29x at 60K with a 2K verification budget, vs EAGLE3-YARN 2.49x -> 3.11x; accepted length ~3.57 tokens/step flat across 2K/4K/8K budgets; BUT GovReport ROUGE-L drops 77.3 -> 56.1 (-27%) at 2K budget while QA stays within 1-3% — 'minor degradation' is task-dependent and unbounded. Its draft module is EAGLE-3, not layer skip.

Vegas (ICML 2026, arXiv 2602.07223): the longest-input self-spec evaluation to date — LongBench-v2 requests of 96K-120K tokens; 1.25-2.81x over default vLLM and 1.15-1.29x over MagicDec-Stream/Quest and SpecExtend at ~7% drafting sparsity; sparse mask = top-k over verification attention logits (averaged over first-draft+bonus queries, then across heads), refreshed every verification step at zero selection cost.

KnapSpec (ICML 2026, arXiv 2602.20217): first layer-skip selector that models per-sublayer (attention vs MLP) latency as a function of CONTEXT LENGTH; DP re-solves every 64 steps at ~7.5% overhead; proves cosine similarity of hidden states is a sound acceptance proxy (0.837 correlation with throughput vs 0.538 for acceptance rate alone); yet peak speedup is only 1.47x (Llama3.1-70B, ~16K GovReport) vs SWIFT 1.33x and CLaSp 1.22x, and evaluation stops at 16K inputs / 32K generations.

SparseSpec/PillarAttn (MLSys 2026, arXiv 2512.01278): on long-CoT reasoning workloads (10K-13K generated tokens), verification-recycled sparse self-drafting accepts 6.16 of 8 drafted tokens while EAGLE-3 and n-gram drafters accept <2; up to 2.13x throughput at batch sizes up to 256 (H100, TP1/2/4 for Qwen3-1.7B/8B/14B); beats MagicDec by 1.36x and TriForce by 1.76x because their static KV budgets cannot track 'high context dynamics' in reasoning traces.

Every published layer-skip/early-exit self-spec result is short-context: LayerSkip 2.16x CNN/DM, 1.82x code, 2.0x TOPv2 at <4K (ACL 2024, arXiv 2404.16710); Draft&Verify <=1.99x, ~92% acceptance at <4K (ACL 2024, arXiv 2309.08168); Kangaroo <=2.04x on Spec-Bench (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2404.18911); EESD 2.29x GSM8K-70B with drafter = first 5 of 80 layers + 1 trained layer, outputs capped at 512 tokens (arXiv 2406.03853); SWIFT 1.3-1.6x, acceptance 98-100% (ICLR 2025, arXiv 2410.06916); CLaSp 1.24-1.73x (ACL 2025, arXiv 2505.24196); DEL 2.16-2.62x (arXiv 2504.05598); ConfLayers <=1.4x (arXiv 2604.14612); PPSD 2.01-3.81x via verify-while-draft pipelining (arXiv 2509.19368); CAS-Spec 1.1-2.3x (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2510.26843). None reports an acceptance-vs-context curve.

SparseSpec-L (arXiv 2607.27735): train-free recallable-KV self-drafting reaches 2.79x on LongBench-v2 (Llama-3.1-8B) at contexts up to 64K with acceptance 52-84.6% and 5.60-13.01 accepted tokens/step (adaptive controller: 11.26) at ~10% KV ratio; dense KV is never discarded so importance-estimation errors are recoverable — unlike eviction-based sparse drafting whose acceptance collapse is permanent.

Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding (arXiv 2605.01106): hybrid-architecture self-drafting viability is determined by composition — parallel hybrids (Falcon-H1, Mamba-2+attention per layer) give alpha=0.68 at k=2 while sequential interleaved hybrids (Qwen3.5-style) give alpha=0.038 (18x gap); LayerSkip-style early exit recovers ~12x acceptance for sequential hybrids; perplexity-degradation ratio (3.15x vs 81.96x) predicts alpha; results scale-invariant 0.5B->3B.

Mirror-SD (Apple, arXiv 2510.13161): early-exit branch-complete rollouts executed on heterogeneous accelerators (draft on NPU, target suffix on GPU) give 2.8-5.8x on SpecBench across 14B-66B models, +30% average over EAGLE-3 — the strongest early-exit numbers published, but entirely short-context.

TriForce (COLM 2024, arXiv 2404.11912) and QuantSpec remain the only self-drafting results measured at 128K: TriForce 2.31x on A100 (Llama2-7B-128K, ~4K retrieval KV budget), 7.78x offloaded on 2x RTX 4090. Nothing in any family is measured at 256K-1M; VeriCache (arXiv 2605.17613) targets that regime architecturally (compressed-KV self-drafting + off-GPU full-KV verification, 25-40 accepted tokens/round, up to 4x) but does not report 1M evaluations.

DeepSeek-V3 (arXiv 2412.19437): production-scale shared-weight self-drafting — the pretraining MTP module reused as drafter yields 85-90% second-token acceptance and ~1.8x decoding TPS; no acceptance-vs-context-length breakdown has ever been published for it despite 128K serving.

OWL (arXiv 2510.07535): trained-short draft heads (EAGLE-3) fall to 0.81x of AR speed on long-context inputs — the quantitative motivation for shared-weight self-drafting at long context, since the self-drafter's 'training distribution' is by construction the target's own.

gaps.gap: No acceptance-vs-context curve exists for any layer-skip or early-exit self-drafter beyond ~16K inputs: whether early-layer hidden-state fidelity (KnapSpec's cosine-similarity acceptance proxy) degrades, holds, or improves at 64K-1M is unmeasured, and no LayerSkip-style (layer-dropout + early-exit loss) checkpoint exists for any 128K-context model.
gaps.why_open: Skip-set/exit-depth selection is calibrated on short streams because long-context calibration multiplies optimization cost (SWIFT's Bayesian phase, CLaSp's per-step DP, KnapSpec's 64-step re-solve all price per-token work, not per-context validity); meanwhile AdaSkip (AAAI 2025, arXiv 2501.02336) shows sublayer importance redistributes at long context for lossy skipping, implying short-context skip sets are miscalibrated at 32K+, but nobody has connected that redistribution to draft acceptance. The zero-extra-KV property that makes early exit uniquely attractive at 1M contexts is precisely the regime where it has never been tested.
gaps.closest_work: KnapSpec (ICML 2026, 2602.20217) models context-dependent sublayer LATENCY but measures acceptance only to ~16K-input/32K-generation; AdaSkip (2501.02336) measures long-context layer importance but for quality-lossy skipping, not speculative drafting; LayerSkip (2404.16710) has the training recipe but only short-context checkpoints.

gaps.gap: Layer-subset drafting and KV-subset drafting have never been composed: a layer-skip drafter pays full-KV attention in every retained layer (capping KnapSpec at 1.47x even with context-aware selection), while verification-guided sparse-KV self-drafters (Vegas, PillarAttn, SparseSpec-L) run ALL layers over ~7-10% of KV. Drafting with (subset of layers) x (subset of KV per retained layer) — with a joint acceptance/latency model — is untried.
gaps.why_open: The two selection signals live at different granularities and are owned by different communities: layer redundancy is estimated from hidden-state similarity (Draft-on-the-Fly, KnapSpec) while KV criticality is recycled from verification attention (Vegas, PillarAttn); composing them requires a 2D knapsack over sublayers x KV budget whose acceptance interaction is unmodeled — skipping layers changes the very attention distributions used to pick critical KV, a feedback loop no current selector accounts for.
gaps.closest_work: KnapSpec (layer axis with context-dependent latency), Vegas/SparseSpec-PillarAttn (KV axis with verification-recycled selection), CAS-Spec (composes sparsity with activation quantization but never touches the KV axis).

gaps.gap: Partial/sparse verification inside self-speculation has no error-accumulation control or certification: SpecPV's fixed buffer-overflow schedule for full verification hides a task-dependent quality cliff (-27% ROUGE-L on GovReport at 2K budget vs 1-3% on QA), and no method adaptively triggers full verification from an online divergence signal, nor bounds output divergence as a function of verification KV budget.
gaps.why_open: Between full-verify refreshes, the partially-verified prefix feeds back into both drafting and subsequent partial verification, so error compounds nonlinearly with the refresh interval and content distribution; the 2026 acceptance-certificate theory (2606.30265) characterizes rejection regions for relaxed/tree criteria but has no KV-sparsity axis, and measuring divergence online would seem to require the full-KV pass one is trying to avoid — an estimator from verification-side statistics (e.g., attention mass captured by the partial budget) has not been proposed.
gaps.closest_work: SpecPV (2512.02337, heuristic periodic refresh + the quantified failure case), Dustin (2606.24957, empirical 'negligible loss' at 32K), When Is a Draft Accepted (2606.30265, certificates without a KV-budget axis), VeriCache (2605.17613, sidesteps the problem by keeping full verification exact but off-GPU).

gaps.gap: Self-speculation for sequential hybrid (interleaved linear+full-attention) and SSM-bearing targets is broken and untrained: component-level self-drafting yields alpha=0.038 on sequential hybrids, LayerSkip-style exit recovers ~12x but no layer-dropout/early-exit TRAINING recipe has been applied to any hybrid checkpoint, and rolling back shared recurrent state for rejected draft tokens inside a self-spec loop (drafter and target share the SSM state that is overwritten in place) has no published solution.
gaps.why_open: Hybrids dominate 2026 long-context frontier models, but self-spec rejection semantics assume a cache you can truncate (KV) rather than a state you must checkpoint; per-draft-token SSM state checkpointing costs O(state x draft length) memory and its overhead at 100K contexts is uncharacterized, while SpecLA's accepted-state recovery machinery (1.70x ceiling) exists only for external drafters on pure linear-attention targets.
gaps.closest_work: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding (2605.01106) for the diagnosis; SpecLA (2607.16673) for state-recovery kernels with external drafters; LayerSkip (2404.16710) for the training recipe never ported to hybrids.

gaps.gap: Layer-skip/early-exit self-speculation has never run under continuous batching: every result (SWIFT, CLaSp, DEL, KnapSpec, ConfLayers, PPSD, Mirror-SD) is single-request, because per-request dynamic skip sets create heterogeneous execution graphs that break batched kernel homogeneity — there is no vLLM/SGLang integration and no measurement of layer-skip self-spec at batch 32+ where long-context serving actually operates.
gaps.why_open: A batch where each request wants a different layer subset requires either grouping requests by skip-set (fragmenting batches, hurting utilization) or imposing one shared skip-set whose per-request acceptance penalty nobody has quantified; PPSD's verify-while-draft pipelining assumes dedicated per-request pipeline stages, and the only serving-grade self-spec system (SparseSpec, MLSys 2026, batch 256) deliberately uses uniform-depth sparse-KV drafting to keep kernels homogeneous — evidence the community routed around the problem rather than solving it.
gaps.closest_work: SparseSpec/PillarAttn (2512.01278) for serving-grade self-spec without the layer axis; P-EAGLE (vLLM blog 2026) for what serving integration looks like in the draft-head family; MagicDec (2408.11049) for batch-scaling analysis that has no layer-skip counterpart.

gaps.gap: Draft-path staleness over ultra-long generations has no principled tracking: for 30K-100K-token reasoning traces the optimal exit depth/skip set/KV selection is non-stationary (SparseSpec shows MagicDec's static budget fails under 'high context dynamics'; SWIFT freezes its skip set after one optimization phase; KnapSpec re-solves every 64 steps for latency while assuming stationary acceptance), yet no method adapts the draft path from online acceptance feedback with any regret or drift guarantee over the generation.
gaps.why_open: Acceptance drift during generation is caused by the model's own output distribution shift (topic, entropy, self-generated KV), which invalidates the stationarity assumption behind every selector's calibration; the only online-learning self-spec (DVI, 2510.05421) updates the drafter HEAD, not the path selection, and was evaluated on short Spec-Bench; combining DEL-style per-layer acceptance tracking with KnapSpec-style re-solving under a drift model is unattempted, and no early-exit method except KnapSpec has even been evaluated on long-CoT generation.
gaps.closest_work: KnapSpec (2602.20217, periodic latency-driven re-solve), DVI (2510.05421, online drafter-head learning), SparseSpec (2512.01278, documents the non-stationarity), TokenSwift (100K-generation regime but n-gram drafting).

surveys.theme: Sparse/compressed KV drafting for long context: methods where the drafter is the same (or smaller) model running over a sparse, compressed, or retrieved KV cache, plus the emerging sparse-verification counterpart

papers.title: TriForce: Lossless Acceleration of Long Sequence Generation with Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Two-level hierarchy: target model self-drafts using a retrieval-selected sparse KV cache (context chunked, chunks scored by attention of the current query, top chunks kept) verified against full KV; a Llama-68M with StreamingLLM cache drafts for the sparse-KV middle layer.
papers.numbers: 2.31x on A100 for Llama2-7B-128K at 122K context; 7.78x (7B) / 7.94x (13B) with offloading on 2x RTX 4090 at 127K; 1.9x at batch=6 with 19K/sample; acceptance 0.9649 (PG-19) and 0.9878 (needle) at 120K with 4K retrieval budget vs StreamingLLM 0.9156/0.0519 and H2O 0.9179/0.0739; acceptance plateaus toward 1.0 at 4K budget; drops to ~0.29 per-token at temperature 1.0 (2.08x vs 2.31x speedup).
papers.long_context_behavior: Canonical 128K result. Drafter attends to constant ~4K retrieval-selected KV regardless of context; acceptance-vs-budget curve rises then plateaus at 4K. Relies on contextual locality: cache reuse effectiveness shows 'slowly decreasing trend' as generation proceeds (staleness). Batch scaling only shown to batch 6.

papers.title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Analytical model showing decoding becomes KV-bound as batch x seqlen grows, so a constant-KV drafter (self-speculation with StreamingLLM or SnapKV cache, budgets 256-2048) gives speedup that INCREASES with batch size beyond a hardware-dependent critical sequence length (~4K for Llama-3.1-8B on 8xA100).
papers.numbers: Llama-3.1-8B on 8xH100 with SnapKV drafting: 2.51x at 100K context/batch 41, 2.36x at 64K/batch 64, 2.01x at 32K/batch 128; StreamingLLM budget-512 on 8xA100: ~1.72x at 16K/batch 64, ~1.35x at 32K/batch 256; Mistral-7B 2.06x, Qwen-2.5-32B 1.34x. SnapKV-selected cache gives markedly higher acceptance than StreamingLLM at equal budget; self-speculation with sparse KV beats small full-KV drafters in acceptance.
papers.long_context_behavior: Long context is the premise: draft-to-target cost ratio shrinks as batch/context grow. Below S_inflection speedup decreases with batch; GQA models push S_inflection higher. Decode-only (prefill unaddressed); gains depend on high FLOPS-to-bandwidth GPUs. Max evaluated ~100K context.

papers.title: LongSpec: Long-Context Lossless Speculative Decoding with Efficient Drafting and Verification
papers.venue: ACL 2025 main (also listed ACL 2026 long); arXiv 2502.17421
papers.idea: Purpose-built drafter with constant memory: 512-token sliding-window self-attention plus cross-attention directly into the TARGET model's KV cache (no drafter copy), shared embeddings/LM head; Anchor-Offset position indices fix train-short/test-long mismatch; Hybrid Tree Attention = FlashAttention prefix + Triton masked tree suffix merged via log-sum-exp.
papers.numbers: Up to 3.26x over FlashAttention baselines (LongChat-13B, RepoBench-P); 2.25-2.34x wall-clock reduction on AIME24 long reasoning with QwQ-32B; mean accepted length tau 2.76-4.46 (summarization), 3.25-4.21 (code), 3.65-3.95 (QwQ math); ~2.5x average at T=1; attention latency -75% vs HuggingFace.
papers.long_context_behavior: Drafter KV is O(1) (512-token window) and cross-attention reads target KV so no duplicate long-context storage. Evaluated to ~32K inputs and 32K generated CoT; authors note modest degradation at 25-32K, single-GPU orientation, and that throughput advantage vs MagicDec shrinks at low batch.

papers.title: SpecExtend: A Drop-in Enhancement for Speculative Decoding of Long Sequences
papers.idea: Training-free retrofit: FlashAttention/Hybrid Tree Attention for prefill+verification, plus Cross-model Retrieval — target-model attention scores (free from verification) rank 32-token chunks and refresh the small drafter's ~1-2K working KV cache every 4-8 decoding steps.
papers.numbers: At 16K: vanilla SD 1.38-1.51x -> 2.65-2.81x with SpecExtend; EAGLE 1.57-1.61x -> 3.09-3.21x; up to 2.84x on 16K summarization, 3.86x on long reasoning; mean accepted length at 16K recovers from ~0.5-0.6 to ~1.7-2.1 tokens. Draft cache ~1K (Vicuna-68M) / ~2K (EAGLE), chunk 32, top-k 32-64.
papers.long_context_behavior: Directly documents early degradation: vanilla and EAGLE acceptance collapse by 8-16K. Evaluation stops at 16K; target attention extraction assumes full-KV verification; does not beat purpose-trained long-context drafters (LongSpec) per authors.

papers.title: RAPID: Long-Context Inference with Retrieval-Augmented Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: RAG drafter: same-scale (self-speculation) or LARGER LLM runs on a retrieval-shortened context (512-token chunks, BGE-M3, retrieval capped at 1/24 of input, 4-16K sweet spot) and speculates for the full-context target; 'upward speculation' transfers knowledge from a larger drafter, improving quality (deliberately lossy).
papers.numbers: 2.10x for LLaMA-3.1-8B and 2.69x for 70B at 120K contexts; speedup >1 only beyond ~32K (naive SD needs >64K); self-speculation acceptance 75-85%; 4K-8K retrieval nearly matches 16K speedup; upward speculation: InfiniteBench 42.83->49.98 (8B target + 70B drafter), 42.48->48.72 (Qwen2.5-7B + 72B) at ~0.93-1.14x speed.
papers.long_context_behavior: Drafter cost decoupled from context via retrieval; evaluated on InfiniteBench 100K+ and LongBench-v2 truncated to 128K. No gain below 32K; degrades when retrieval is unrelated and knowledge-transfer weight eta>20; requires per-task eta tuning and extra GPUs for upward mode.

papers.title: QuantSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding with Hierarchical Quantized KV Cache
papers.idea: Drafter = target architecture with 4-bit weights and hierarchical 4-bit quantized KV cache; full-precision KV verification; custom CUDA kernels for quantized-KV attention. Compression rather than sparsity keeps the entire context visible to the drafter.
papers.numbers: >90% acceptance; up to ~2.5x end-to-end; ~1.3x memory reduction vs sparse-KV self-spec alternatives; quantized attention kernel up to 2.88x vs FP16 FlashAttention.
papers.long_context_behavior: Drafter KV is 4x smaller but still grows linearly with context (unlike constant-budget sparse drafters); acceptance stays >90% at LongBench-scale (~32K); nothing shown at 128K+. Edge/long-context positioning.

papers.title: Vegas: Self-Speculative Decoding with Verification-Guided Sparse Attention
papers.idea: Self-speculation where the sparse drafting mask is a free byproduct of full-KV verification: attention logits of the first draft token + bonus token ('Collect-2-Query') are aggregated across heads and top-k KV entries retained for drafting the next chunk — no separate KV-selection pass, no separate drafter.
papers.numbers: 1.25-2.81x throughput over default vLLM; 1.15-1.29x over SOTA sparse self-spec (MagicDec-Stream/Quest variants, SpecExtend); ~6.1 accepted tokens/iteration at gamma=7 with 7% sparsity on LongBench-v2 (Qwen3-8B); evaluated at 96K-120K contexts, batch 4-128, Qwen3-4B/8B/30B + gpt-oss-20b on 2x H100 NVL with disaggregated prefill/decode.
papers.long_context_behavior: One of the only 2026 sparse-drafting evaluations near 128K. Query-aware verification-guided selection keeps acceptance flat across draft positions where single-query selection degrades. Authors note sparsity budget must GROW with context — fixed budgets underperform at extreme scale — and gains shrink on models with interleaved banded/dense attention (gpt-oss-20b).

papers.title: SparseSpec: Accelerating Large-Scale Reasoning Model Inference with Sparse Self-Speculative Decoding (PillarAttn)
papers.idea: Self-speculation for long-GENERATION reasoning: target drafts with PillarAttn — top-K KV tokens selected from attention scores dumped on-the-fly by custom kernels during the previous verification (every k=8 draft steps), averaged over draft tokens and query heads — co-designed with unified batch scheduling, delayed verification (CPU/GPU overlap), and dynamic KV management.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.13x throughput vs vLLM (Qwen3-8B, AIME); ~6.16 accepted of k=8 drafted vs <2 for N-gram and EAGLE-3 on reasoning traces; batch up to 256 on H100s (TP1/2/4 for 1.7B/8B/14B); Qwen3-14B generates avg 13,185 tokens on AIME.
papers.long_context_behavior: KV growth comes from the model's own CoT output; drafter reuses target KV sparsely so zero extra drafter memory. Explicitly no benefit for short-context compute-bound workloads. Importance refresh is a fixed k=8 heuristic; no staleness analysis over 10K+ generated tokens.

papers.title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding (SparseSpec-L)
papers.idea: Training-free self-speculation from a dynamically sparsified but RECALLABLE KV cache: budget = sink + recent + top-K_mid tokens ranked by per-head attention statistics recycled from full-context verification (dense KV never discarded, indices rebuilt each step); online entropy-based controller picks speculation length k* maximizing expected step-wise efficiency.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.79x over AR (LongBench-v2, Llama-3.1-8B); 1.95x/1.86x for Qwen2.5-7B on LongBench/InfiniteBench; acceptance 52-84.6%; optimal compression ratio ~10% of full KV; index gather 41.1 ms/iteration at 60K; contexts up to 64K (A40 ceiling), generation capped at 128 tokens; baselines: SpecInfer, EAGLE-3, MagicDec (Stream/SnapKV), RAPID, LayerSkip.
papers.long_context_behavior: Recallable eviction lets acceptance recover from importance-estimation errors that permanently hurt eviction-based drafters. But single A40 GPU caps evaluation at 64K, non-fused gather + dense verification kernels add overhead, and 128-token generations leave long-generation staleness untested.

papers.title: BudgetDraft: Acceptance-Aware Multi-View Training for Sparse-KV Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Trains a small drafter (Llama-68M) under multiple sampled KV budgets simultaneously: chunk-based sparse views (chunk s=8, top-floor(B/s) chunks by cumulative attention, B in {256,512,1024,2048}) each aligned to a shared full-cache teacher, with acceptance-aware loss on the full branch — one drafter robust across runtime budgets.
papers.numbers: Naive sparse drafting acceptance collapse: 55.4%/45.5%/29.7%/19.3% at 4K (B=256/512/1024/2048) -> 0.3%/0.4%/0.14%/0% at 8K -> ~0.1-0.5% at 16K. After multi-view training: 91.62% at 4K (all budgets), ~75% at 8K, ~18% at 16K. End-to-end 6.55x/4.46x/2.10x at 4K/8K/16K vs AR; at 8K gamma=5 on LWM: 2.54x vs TriForce 1.21x and EAGLE-3 1.64x. Drafter: llama-68m; verifier: YaRN-Llama-2-7B-128K.
papers.long_context_behavior: Best available acceptance-vs-budget-vs-length table. Training makes acceptance budget-invariant but NOT length-invariant: still falls to ~18% at 16K (drafter's native 2048 position-embedding limit). Greedy only; retraining needed per verifier; nothing beyond 16K.

papers.title: Dustin: Draft-Augmented Sparse Verification for Efficient Long-Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Sparsifies the VERIFICATION side: draft-model lookahead attention signals fused with target attention history form a global importance map; a fixed-size KV subset is selected per multi-step verification window, with importance scoring restricted to a minimal subset of attention heads to bound recomputation latency.
papers.numbers: 27.85x self-attention speedup and 9.17x end-to-end decoding speedup on Qwen2.5-72B at 32K (PG-19, LongBench) with 'negligible accuracy degradation'.
papers.long_context_behavior: Attacks the dominant cost (target KV loading at verification) but output is no longer bit-exact to full-KV target — losslessness traded away with only empirical accuracy checks at 32K; static eviction fails from saliency shift per their own motivation, yet no divergence certificate is provided.

papers.title: SpecPV: Improving Self-Speculative Decoding for Long-Context Generation via Partial Verification
papers.idea: Most verification steps use a partial KV (sink + block-level retrieval via max/min key summaries + local window + buffer; budgets 2K/4K/8K); full-KV verification runs periodically (buffer-triggered refresh) to bound error accumulation.
papers.numbers: Up to 6.29x at 60K context with 2K budget on LLaMA-3.1-8B vs 3.11x for EAGLE-3+YaRN; tested 10K-60K, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B/8B/14B; quality: GovReport ROUGE-L 56.1 vs 77.3 for full verification at 4K budget — the 'minor degradation' claim is contradicted by their own summarization numbers, though QA accuracy is comparable.
papers.long_context_behavior: Identifies verification, not drafting, as the long-context bottleneck. Errors from partial verification accumulate and outputs drift over long generations (admitted); fine-grained detail loss not captured by accuracy metrics; 128K support is architectural only, evaluation capped at 60K.

papers.title: VeriCache: Turning Lossy KV Cache into Lossless LLM Inference
papers.idea: Drafter = same model on a lossy compressed KV (uniform compressor interface: KVzip, KVzap, ExpectedAttention, SnapKV, KIVI, KVQuant, RotateKV); full KV lives on CPU/storage and full-KV verification is scheduled into interconnect idle windows — compressed-KV decoding is HBM-bound while full-KV swap is PCIe/network-bound, so they overlap.
papers.numbers: Up to 4x throughput over full-KV inference with bit-identical outputs (2x for remote prefix caching); 25-40 accepted tokens per verification round vs 2-3 for small-model drafters; 256 vs 102 tok/s on Llama-70B; Mistral-24B/Qwen-32B/Llama-70B on RTX PRO 6000 96GB and 2x H100 NVL PCIe 5.0.
papers.long_context_behavior: Targets contexts where full KV cannot fit in HBM (1M-class models); compressed-KV outputs stay close to full-KV so drafting horizons are 10x longer than model-based drafters, amortizing each swap. Costs: BOTH caches stored (GPU compressed + CPU full); fixed draft length per workload, not adaptive.

papers.title: STS: Efficient Sparse Attention with Speculative Token Sparsity
papers.idea: Training-free: the small draft model's attention scores predict target-model token importance, building a token-and-head-wise sparsity mask that prunes TARGET attention — the draft model accelerates both drafting and target attention inside a speculative decoding framework.
papers.numbers: 2.67x speedup at ~90% sparsity with negligible accuracy degradation; NarrativeQA long-document QA; positioned for multi-million-token sequences (aspirationally).
papers.long_context_behavior: Depends on draft-target attention-importance correlation, the same cross-model signal SpecExtend uses; its long-range stability is questioned by Attention Drift (2605.09992). No acceptance-vs-context curve; target attention is sparsified so output is not bit-exact.

papers.title: SSV: Sparse Speculative Verification for Efficient LLM Inference (v1: SpecSA)
papers.idea: Resolves the structural mismatch between multi-token speculative verification (cross-query commonality) and NSA-style query-specific dynamic sparse attention: overlap-aware grouped-query execution, refresh/reuse NSA kernel fusion, profile-guided prompt-adaptive orchestration to maximize KV-block reuse across verification queries.
papers.numbers: 3.49x end-to-end throughput over autoregressive NSA decoding; 6.86x kernel-level speedup on H100.
papers.long_context_behavior: For long-context NSA targets each verification query would otherwise trigger its own sparse selection; cross-query block reuse keeps sparse verification cost sublinear in draft width. Baseline is NSA (already sparse), so this composes speculation with natively-sparse targets rather than full-KV ones.

papers.title: Accelerate Speculative Decoding with Sparse Computation in Verification
papers.idea: Training-free sparsification of the verification pass across attention, FFN, and MoE experts, with inter-draft-token and inter-layer retrieval-reuse so draft tokens in one verification window share sparse index computation.
papers.numbers: Maintains stable acceptance length on summarization/QA/math; targeted at long-context inputs and MoE models (headline multipliers not in abstract).
papers.long_context_behavior: Part of the late-2025/2026 sparse-verification wave with Dustin/SpecPV/SSV; same caveat — sparse verification abandons bit-exactness with only empirical quality checks.

evidence: TriForce (COLM 2024, arXiv 2404.11912): acceptance at 120K context with 4K retrieval-cache budget is 0.9649 on PG-19 and 0.9878 on needle retrieval, vs StreamingLLM 0.9156/0.0519 and H2O 0.9179/0.0739 — eviction-based drafter caches collapse on retrieval tasks while attention-retrieval caches do not; acceptance rises with budget and plateaus at 4K.

TriForce speedups: 2.31x on A100 (Llama2-7B-128K, 122K context), 7.78x/7.94x offloading on 2x RTX 4090 (7B/13B at 127K), 1.9x at batch 6 with 19K/sample; per-token acceptance falls to ~0.29 at temperature 1.0 (speedup 2.08x vs 2.31x greedy); retrieval-cache reuse shows a slowly decreasing trend as generation proceeds (staleness).

MagicDec (ICLR 2025, arXiv 2408.11049): Llama-3.1-8B on 8xH100 with SnapKV-cache self-drafting reaches 2.51x at 100K/batch 41, 2.36x at 64K/batch 64, 2.01x at 32K/batch 128; StreamingLLM budget-512 on 8xA100 gives ~1.72x at 16K/batch 64; speedup grows with batch only beyond a critical sequence length (~4K for 8B on 8xA100, higher for GQA models); SnapKV selection yields higher acceptance than StreamingLLM at equal budget.

BudgetDraft (arXiv 2606.00144): naive sparse-KV drafting (llama-68m drafter, chunked top-attention selection) acceptance collapses from 55.4%/19.3% (budgets 256/2048) at 4K to 0.3%/0.0% at 8K and ~0.1-0.5% at 16K; multi-view budget training restores 91.62% at 4K, ~75% at 8K, but only ~18% at 16K — budget-robustness achieved, length-robustness not; end-to-end 6.55x/4.46x/2.10x at 4K/8K/16K.

SpecExtend (arXiv 2505.20776): vanilla SD mean accepted length drops to ~0.5-0.6 tokens at 16K; Cross-model Retrieval (target attention ranks 32-token chunks, drafter cache ~1-2K, refresh every 4-8 steps) restores ~1.7-2.1, lifting speedup from 1.38-1.51x to 2.65-2.81x (vanilla SD) and 1.57-1.61x to 3.09-3.21x (EAGLE) at 16K; evaluation stops at 16K.

LongSpec (ACL 2025, arXiv 2502.17421): drafter with 512-token sliding window + cross-attention into the TARGET's KV cache (zero duplicate long-context storage) reaches tau=2.76-4.46 accepted tokens and up to 3.26x over FlashAttention baselines; 2.25-2.34x on AIME24 with QwQ-32B; authors note degradation at 25-32K and weaker throughput than MagicDec at high batch.

RAPID (ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.20330): RAG drafter on <=1/24-of-input retrieval (4-16K sweet spot) achieves 2.10x (LLaMA-3.1-8B) and 2.69x (70B) at 120K contexts with 75-85% acceptance; speedup >1 only beyond ~32K; upward speculation (70B drafter for 8B target) raises InfiniteBench 42.83->49.98 at ~0.93-1.14x speed — quality-improving lossy speculation.

Vegas (ICML 2026, arXiv 2602.07223): verification-guided top-k selection from first-draft+bonus-token attention logits gives ~6.1 accepted tokens/iteration (gamma=7) at 7% sparsity on LongBench-v2 with Qwen3-8B; 1.25-2.81x over vLLM and 1.15-1.29x over MagicDec-Stream/Quest/SpecExtend at 96K-120K contexts, batch 4-128, 2x H100 NVL; authors state fixed sparsity budgets underperform at extreme context — budget must grow with length.

SparseSpec/PillarAttn (MLSys 2026, arXiv 2512.01278): verification-dumped attention scores (custom kernels, refresh every k=8 draft steps) select top-K KV for self-drafting on reasoning workloads; ~6.16 of 8 drafted tokens accepted vs <2 for N-gram and EAGLE-3; up to 2.13x throughput vs vLLM at batch up to 256; explicitly no gain in short-context compute-bound regimes.

SparseSpec-L (arXiv 2607.27735): train-free recallable sparse drafting (sink+recent+top-K_mid from verification attention, ~10% compression optimal) reaches up to 2.79x over AR (LongBench-v2, Llama-3.1-8B) with acceptance 52-84.6%; contexts capped at 64K by a single A40; generations capped at 128 tokens; index gather costs 41.1 ms/iteration at 60K.

Dustin (arXiv 2606.24957): sparse VERIFICATION via draft-lookahead + target attention history on a restricted head subset gives 27.85x self-attention and 9.17x end-to-end speedup on Qwen2.5-72B at 32K (PG-19/LongBench) — but output is no longer the target distribution; only 'negligible accuracy degradation' is claimed empirically.

SpecPV (arXiv 2512.02337): partial verification (sink+block-retrieval+local, budgets 2K-8K, periodic full-KV refresh) yields 6.29x at 60K on LLaMA-3.1-8B vs 3.11x for EAGLE-3+YaRN; its own tables show GovReport ROUGE-L 56.1 vs 77.3 under full verification — partial-verification error accumulation and output drift are admitted, contradicting 'minor degradation' for summarization.

VeriCache (arXiv 2605.17613): same-model drafting on lossy compressed KV (KVzip/SnapKV/KIVI/KVQuant etc.) sustains 25-40 accepted tokens per verification round vs 2-3 for small-model drafters; full-KV verification runs from CPU over PCIe overlapped with HBM-bound compressed decoding; up to 4x throughput with bit-identical outputs (256 vs 102 tok/s on Llama-70B); costs: double cache storage and fixed draft length.

QuantSpec (arXiv 2502.10424): 4-bit weight + hierarchical 4-bit KV self-drafter keeps acceptance >90% and gives up to ~2.5x end-to-end at LongBench-scale (~32K), with ~1.3x memory reduction vs sparse-KV self-spec alternatives — compression (all tokens, lower precision) is an acceptance-robust alternative to token sparsity, but drafter KV still grows linearly.

STS (arXiv 2605.15508): draft-model attention predicts target token importance well enough to run target attention at ~90% sparsity for 2.67x speedup with negligible degradation on NarrativeQA — cross-model attention-importance correlation is exploitable, but no context-scaling curve is given.

SSV (arXiv 2605.19893): composing multi-token verification with NSA-style query-specific sparse attention requires overlap-aware grouped-query execution and kernel fusion — 3.49x end-to-end over AR NSA decoding, 6.86x kernel-level on H100 — showing speculation and natively-sparse targets are non-trivially compatible.

gaps.gap: No measured budget-growth law B(L) for sparse-KV drafters: how the drafter's KV budget must scale with context length (and task) to hold acceptance constant from 128K to 1M tokens is unmapped, and nothing in the family is evaluated past ~128K.
gaps.why_open: Every method fixes its budget by ablation at one scale (TriForce plateaus at 4K budget at 120K; Vegas uses 7% sparsity at 96-120K and explicitly warns fixed budgets underperform at extreme scale; SparseSpec-L finds ~10% optimal but is hardware-capped at 64K on one A40; BudgetDraft stops at 16K). No paper publishes acceptance-vs-(budget, length) surfaces beyond 128K, and 256K-1M evaluation requires multi-node full-KV verification that current single/dual-GPU academic setups cannot run — yet 1M-context models are in production.
gaps.closest_work: TriForce (acceptance-vs-budget curve at 120K), Vegas (96-120K, notes budget must grow), BudgetDraft (budget x length acceptance table but only to 16K).

gaps.gap: Length-robust TRAINED sparse-KV drafting past ~16-32K is unproven: budget-robust training fixes the sparse/full mismatch across budgets but not across lengths — acceptance still collapses to ~18% at 16K after multi-view training.
gaps.why_open: BudgetDraft shows training equalizes acceptance across budgets (91.6% at 4K for all of B=256..2048) yet drops 91.6->75->18% as context goes 4K->8K->16K, bottlenecked by the tiny drafter's 2048-token native position range and per-verifier retraining; LongSpec avoids this only by architectural constant-window design (no sparse-selection training) and itself degrades at 25-32K. No work combines multi-budget sparse-view training with long-context position schemes (Anchor-Offset-style) and evaluates at 64K+.
gaps.closest_work: BudgetDraft (multi-view budget training, 16K ceiling); LongSpec (length-robust architecture, no budget-adaptive training).

gaps.gap: No principled staleness/refresh policy for verification-recycled importance signals over long generations: every 2025-26 sparse drafter reuses verification attention as its sparsity oracle with a fixed heuristic refresh interval, and nobody measures acceptance decay of stale indices over 10K+ generated tokens.
gaps.why_open: Refresh intervals are hand-set (SpecExtend: every 4-8 steps; PillarAttn: every k=8 draft steps; SparseSpec-L: every step at 41 ms/iteration gather cost at 60K; TriForce documented slow cache-reuse decay in 2024 but no successor quantified it). The methods best positioned to observe long-generation drift avoid it: SparseSpec-L caps generation at 128 tokens; SparseSpec/PillarAttn targets 13K-token CoT but never ablates refresh frequency vs acceptance. An acceptance-aware refresh controller (refresh when predicted acceptance drop exceeds gather cost) does not exist.
gaps.closest_work: SparseSpec-L (recallable eviction + entropy-based speculation-length controller — controls length, not refresh); TriForce (first documented staleness); SparseSpec/PillarAttn (fixed k=8 on long generations).

gaps.gap: Sparse verification has no divergence certification: Dustin/SpecPV/STS/2512.21911 abandon bit-exactness for 6-9x gains, but 'negligible degradation' is asserted from task metrics, and SpecPV's own GovReport numbers (ROUGE-L 56.1 vs 77.3 full) show the claims can hide large regressions; no bound connects KV-sparsity level to output-distribution divergence or certified acceptance.
gaps.why_open: The 2026 acceptance-region theory (When Is a Draft Accepted, arXiv 2606.30265) covers relaxed/top-m/tree criteria but takes draft and target distributions as given — nobody has modeled the target-under-sparse-KV as a perturbed distribution and derived per-token KL/TV certificates as a function of KV budget and attention mass dropped; empirically it requires full-KV references at exactly the scales being avoided. VeriCache sidesteps the problem (full verification off-GPU) rather than solving it.
gaps.closest_work: When Is a Draft Accepted (arXiv 2606.30265, acceptance certificates without KV-sparsity axis); SpecPV (only paper that measures and admits error accumulation); VeriCache (lossless alternative that avoids rather than certifies).

gaps.gap: Oracle circularity blocks composing sparse drafting with sparse verification: all verification-guided sparse drafters (Vegas, PillarAttn, SparseSpec-L, SpecExtend) source their importance signal from FULL-KV verification attention, so stacking them with sparse verification (Dustin, SpecPV, SSV, 2512.21911) destroys the signal they depend on — the combination that would attack both bottlenecks at once has never been built or even analyzed.
gaps.why_open: The dependency is structural: verification-time attention over the full cache is precisely what makes selection 'free' (Vegas Collect-2-Query, PillarAttn kernel dumps); under sparse verification, attention statistics exist only for the retained subset, so recall of dropped-but-relevant tokens becomes impossible without a third scoring pass. SpecPV's periodic full-refresh is the only partial mechanism, and it demonstrably accumulates error. No paper reports the interaction, and the 2-9x claims of each side are measured in isolation.
gaps.closest_work: SpecPV (periodic full verification as a crude signal-refresh); Vegas + Dustin (the two sides, never composed); SSV (composes speculation with natively-sparse NSA targets, but the target was trained sparse — different setting).

gaps.gap: No online controller sets the drafter KV budget jointly with speculation length across the (batch, context, load) surface: MagicDec's analytical model covers fixed drafting strategies vs (batch, seqlen), goodput schedulers (SmartSpec) cover load but not KV-boundedness, and no system adapts the sparse-KV budget per request at serving time even though acceptance-vs-budget curves are now known to be task- and length-dependent.
gaps.why_open: The required inputs only became available in 2026 — budget-robust drafters that tolerate runtime budget changes (BudgetDraft, trained; Vegas/SparseSpec-L, training-free) and acceptance-vs-budget measurements — but no work closes the loop: Vegas fixes sparsity per run, SparseSpec's scheduler batches drafting/verification without touching budgets, and BudgetDraft never deploys its budget-robustness in a serving stack; picking (budget, gamma) per request requires an acceptance predictor alpha(task, L, B) that does not exist.
gaps.closest_work: MagicDec (analytical speedup model over batch x seqlen for fixed strategies); BudgetDraft (runtime-adjustable budgets, no controller); SmartSpec/goodput line (load-aware gamma, KV-budget-blind); SparseSpec MLSys 2026 (serving co-design with fixed sparsity).

surveys.theme: KV-cache compression x speculative decoding interplay: compressed drafter KV (quantized/sparse/latent), compressed or sparse verification, paged/offloaded KV under draft-token pressure, and batch-level memory effects — who actually measures the combinations

papers.title: QuantSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding with Hierarchical Quantized KV Cache
papers.idea: Drafter = target architecture with 4-bit weights and a hierarchical INT4/INT8-switchable quantized KV cache; full-precision-KV verification. The only work that QUANTIZES the drafter's KV specifically and shows quantized drafter KV yields HIGHER draft-target agreement than sparse drafter KV.
papers.numbers: >90% acceptance rate; up to ~2.5x end-to-end; ~1.3x memory reduction vs other self-spec baselines; custom 4-bit attention kernel up to 2.88x vs FP16 FlashAttention
papers.long_context_behavior: Drafter KV is 4x smaller but still O(n); acceptance stays >90% at LongBench-scale (~32K). Nothing shown at 128K+; hierarchical INT4/INT8 switch avoids on-the-fly requantization cost.

papers.title: VeriCache: Turning Lossy KV Cache into Lossless LLM Inference
papers.idea: Drafter = same model on a compressed KV cache (token dropping OR quantization via a uniform compressor interface: SnapKV/KVzip/KVzap/ExpectedAttention, KIVI/KVQuant/RotateKV); verification against a full-KV copy held off-GPU, overlapping HBM-bound compressed decoding with PCIe-bound full-KV swaps. Bit-identical outputs.
papers.numbers: Up to 4x throughput vs full-KV (256 vs 102 tok/s on Llama-70B); at 4x compaction acceptance >0.8 at draft length 30; acceptance lengths ~19 (Qwen-32B) / ~23 (Llama-70B) vs EAGLE ~1-2/11 and small-drafter ~3-10; composes with EAGLE: 4.35x vs 3.50x alone; verification every 15-40 tokens
papers.long_context_behavior: Built for 32K-1M where full KV exceeds HBM (Llama-3.1-8B-1M: 0.6GB KV @5K -> 60GB @500K; decode 5ms -> 25ms). Key measurement: KL of compressed-KV vs full-KV output grows ~linearly in decode steps — ~6 nats after 250 steps at KVzip 4x, i.e. e^-6 ≈ 0.25% probability of emitting the full-KV sequence unverified — quantifying WHY unverified compressed-KV decoding fails at long generations.

papers.title: SpecKV: Adaptive Speculative Decoding with Compression-Aware Gamma Selection
papers.idea: Profiles spec decoding across 4 task categories x 4 speculation lengths x 3 TARGET-MODEL WEIGHT quantization levels (FP16 / BitsAndBytes INT8 / NF4) — NOT KV quantization despite the name — and builds a 0.34ms/step adaptive gamma controller from draft confidence/entropy. Explicitly states the compression x speculation interaction 'has not been studied'.
papers.numbers: 5,112 step-level records; +56.0% over fixed gamma=4; draft confidence/entropy predict acceptance with correlation ~0.56; optimal gamma shifts with precision (INT8's compute overhead favors longer speculation despite slightly lower acceptance; NF4 settles at 4-6)
papers.long_context_behavior: Context-length coverage modest; contribution is the first quantified precision-vs-gamma coupling. Because compression is weight-level, the KV-quantization analogue (KIVI/FP8-KV target + EAGLE) remains unmeasured.

papers.title: Lynx: Progressive Speculative Quantization for accelerating KV Transfer in Long-Context Inference
papers.idea: Disaggregated prefill/decode: splits KV cache into a high-priority Anchor bit-plane stream (MSBs) and low-priority Residual stream; decoding starts speculatively on Anchor bits while Residuals transfer, with verification guaranteeing full-precision equivalence — speculative decoding applied to KV PRECISION rather than tokens.
papers.numbers: Up to 1.43x faster TTFT than standard 8-bit KV quantization; 4-bit-equivalent latency at BF16-level accuracy; up to 5.1% accuracy gain over SOTA transfer-quantization
papers.long_context_behavior: Long-context transfer is the entire premise: KV transfer time scales with context so bit-plane streaming wins more at longer contexts; verification cost of the precision-speculation at 500K+ not broken out.

papers.title: Draft-based Approximate Inference for LLMs (SpecKV / SpecPC)
papers.idea: The INVERSE coupling: a small draft model's lookahead output and attention activations estimate future token/KV importance to drive KV-cache dropping (SpecKV) and prompt compression (SpecPC) — speculation used FOR compression rather than compression used inside speculation.
papers.numbers: Consistently higher accuracy than SnapKV/Ada-KV-class baselines at equal memory/latency budgets (per abstract; first method to use draft-model lookahead for KV dropping)
papers.long_context_behavior: Targets long-context prefill/decode budgets; draft generation itself adds prefill overhead that grows with context — the cost LookaheadKV later attacks.

papers.title: LookaheadKV: Fast and Accurate KV Cache Eviction by Glimpsing into the Future without Generation
papers.idea: Replaces draft-model-generation-based eviction (SpecKV-2506.08373-style) with learnable lookahead tokens + LoRA modules that predict future attention patterns directly — removing the drafter from draft-guided eviction because its generation cost dominates.
papers.numbers: <0.7% performance drop at 1K cache budget (~81% compression); eviction cost reduced up to 14.5x vs draft-generation-based eviction; faster TTFT
papers.long_context_behavior: Evidence that the draft-for-compression coupling is prefill-cost-bound at long context: the field's fix was to remove generation, not tune it.

papers.title: Beyond KV Reconstruction: Functional Reconstruction for MLA Draft Models in Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Converting MHA/GQA draft models to MLA (latent low-rank KV) for cache savings sharply reduces draft-token acceptance because low-rank factorization + RoPE handling introduce attention-function errors tolerable for standalone generation but fatal for draft-target agreement; fixes by calibrating each converted MLA module to reproduce the original post-output-projection attention response (no retraining).
papers.numbers: 192 configurations (Llama/Qwen pairs x TransMLA/MHA2MLA converters x HF/vLLM backends x 4 tasks); material acceptance improvement in 37/64 matched task cells, unchanged in 26, worse in 1
papers.long_context_behavior: First direct evidence that latent-KV compression of the DRAFTER degrades acceptance through attention-function error rather than output-distribution shift; long-context (32K+) acceptance of MLA drafters not evaluated.

papers.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report (MTP + MLA in production)
papers.idea: MTP module (one extra transformer layer, 14B params incl. MLA + MoE) drafts the next+1 token on top of a target whose entire KV is low-rank latent-compressed (MLA) — the production existence proof that latent KV compression and speculative decoding coexist at scale.
papers.numbers: 85-90% acceptance rate for the second-token prediction across topics; 1.8x TPS; SGLang MTP+EP+PD-disaggregation integration adds up to 60% output throughput
papers.long_context_behavior: MLA makes the target's KV ~an order smaller, shifting the KV-bound regime boundary that motivates sparse-drafter methods; no public acceptance-vs-context-length curves for MTP at 64K-128K.

papers.title: TriForce: Lossless Acceleration of Long Sequence Generation with Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Target model drafting with retrieval-selected sparse KV (~4K budget chunks picked by attention) verified against full KV; a StreamingLLM-cache tiny model drafts for the middle layer. Established that at long context the best 'compressed drafter' is the target itself with compressed KV.
papers.numbers: 2.31x on A100 for Llama2-7B-128K at 128K context; 7.78x with offloading on 2x RTX 4090; 0.226 s/token for 13B at 128K offloaded
papers.long_context_behavior: Canonical 128K result and still the high-water mark for evaluated context in this family; retrieval KV budget stays ~constant so acceptance holds as context scales.

papers.title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Analytical model + system showing long-context large-batch decoding is KV-bound, so a constant-KV (StreamingLLM sink+window) drafter — including self-drafting — gives speedup that GROWS with batch size; the draft/target cost ratio is governed by KV footprints, not parameter counts.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.51x for LLaMA-3.1-8B at batch 32-256 on 8K-32K+ sequences; provides closed-form optimal-drafting-strategy model over (batch, seqlen)
papers.long_context_behavior: The reference framework for batch x context x drafter-KV-budget reasoning — but its model has no axis for TARGET KV compression (FP8/eviction), which changes when decoding is KV-bound at all.

papers.title: BudgetDraft: Acceptance-Aware Multi-View Training for Sparse-KV Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Trains one drafter under multiple sampled KV budgets simultaneously (multi-view sparse branches aligned to a full-cache teacher with acceptance-aware loss) so acceptance survives whatever runtime budget memory pressure dictates.
papers.numbers: 6.55x / 4.46x / 2.10x vs AR at 4K / 8K / 16K (PG-19, LongBench, LWM); documents naive sparse-KV drafting acceptance collapsing to near-zero by 16K from the sparse/full mismatch
papers.long_context_behavior: The sparse/full mismatch it measures GROWS with context, yet evaluation stops at 16K — budget-robust drafting beyond 32K is unproven.

papers.title: SpecExtend: A Drop-in Enhancement for Speculative Decoding of Long Sequences
papers.idea: Cross-model Retrieval: the TARGET model's attention scores select which KV entries the small independent drafter keeps — drafter-KV eviction driven by target-side signals, training-free.
papers.numbers: 2.37x/2.22x over standard SD at 8K/16K; up to 2.84x on 16K summarization; 2.02-2.09x for EAGLE frameworks; documents vanilla SD degrading sharply at 8K already
papers.long_context_behavior: One of only two works (with BudgetDraft) that compress an independent drafter's OWN cache; evaluated to 16K only.

papers.title: Dustin: Draft-Augmented Sparse Verification for Efficient Long-Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Compresses the VERIFICATION-side KV: draft lookahead attention + target attention history build a global importance map selecting a fixed-size KV subset for verification, with scoring restricted to a few heads to bound overhead. Output no longer bit-exact to full-KV target.
papers.numbers: 27.85x self-attention speedup, 9.17x end-to-end decoding speedup on Qwen2.5-72B at 32K (PG-19, LongBench), 'negligible' accuracy degradation
papers.long_context_behavior: Evaluated at 32K on 72B; no divergence certificate for the compressed-verification output distribution and no report of how acceptance itself shifts when verification KV is compressed.

papers.title: SpecPV: Improving Self-Speculative Decoding for Long-Context Generation via Partial Verification
papers.idea: Most verification steps run on partial (compressed) KV; full-KV verification runs intermittently to bound error accumulation — an explicit accuracy/speed dial on the verification side.
papers.numbers: Up to 6x decoding acceleration vs AR on LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3; admits 'minor degradation' (not lossless)
papers.long_context_behavior: Identifies verification KV-loading, not drafting, as the binding constraint as context grows; the full-verification interval vs divergence tradeoff is heuristic, not certified.

papers.title: Vegas: Self-Speculative Decoding with Verification-Guided Sparse Attention
papers.idea: Critical-KV identification comes free from the attention computed during full-KV verification and is recycled as the drafter's sparse mask — compression signal generation costs zero because verification already computes it.
papers.numbers: 1.25-2.81x vs default vLLM; 1.15-1.29x over SOTA sparse-attention self-spec methods
papers.long_context_behavior: Drafter KV traffic ~constant, full cache touched only at verification; the design breaks if verification itself is sparsified (signal disappears) — a concrete composability conflict with Dustin/SpecPV.

papers.title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding (SparseSpec-L)
papers.idea: Drafts from a dynamically sparsified but RECALLABLE KV cache (dense cache retained, evicted tokens can be reactivated) using per-head attention statistics from verification; entropy-based controller adapts speculation length.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.79x end-to-end across long-context tasks and model scales
papers.long_context_behavior: Recallable eviction addresses saliency shift over long decodes that permanent-eviction drafters suffer; retaining the dense cache means NO memory saving — it trades none of the footprint for the bandwidth win.

papers.title: Accelerate Speculative Decoding with Sparse Computation in Verification
papers.idea: Jointly sparsifies attention, FFN, and MoE components during the verification pass, with inter-draft-token and inter-layer retrieval reuse — verification-side compression beyond KV alone, training-free.
papers.numbers: Claims favorable efficiency-accuracy tradeoffs with 'stable acceptance length' (no headline multiplier in abstract)
papers.long_context_behavior: Notable for claiming acceptance length is STABLE under verification sparsification — the counter-datapoint to assuming compressed verification must hurt acceptance; needs independent confirmation at 32K+.

papers.title: DeFT: Decoding with Flash Tree-attention for Efficient Tree-structured LLM Inference
papers.idea: KV-Guided Grouping + Flattened Tree KV Splitting: prefix-aware, load-balanced tree attention over paged (non-contiguous) KV so tree-structured speculative KV never needs materialization into one tensor; attacks the IO cost of tree verification over shared prefixes.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.23x end-to-end / 3.59x attention latency across three tree workloads (incl. speculative decoding); 73-99% KV cache IO reduction, ~100% partial-result IO eliminated
papers.long_context_behavior: Solves tree-verification IO on paged KV; does NOT account for the memory-allocation side (block-granular page waste for uncommitted tree branches) — that is TransKV's territory.

papers.title: Transactional KV Caching for Speculative Decoding under Paged KV Memory (TransKV)
papers.idea: Draft tokens force temporary KV growth that interacts pathologically with block-granular paged allocation and token-budget schedulers (uncommitted drafts consume whole pages and count against global token limits). Separates committed paged KV from a packed speculative buffer; only accepted prefixes commit — shrinking speculative KV pressure from block-sized pages to token-sized buffers.
papers.numbers: No peer-reviewed numbers extractable (403 on full text); qualitative claim: draft-token page consumption limits spec-decode speedups at high load
papers.long_context_behavior: The only work found that treats spec-decode draft-KV allocation under paged memory as a first-class problem; appears to handle linear draft buffers — tree-shaped branch commitment under paging unaddressed.

papers.title: BASS: Batched Attention-optimized Speculative Sampling
papers.idea: Variable per-sequence acceptance makes K/V tensors ragged across a batch; custom CUDA kernels handle ragged-tensor attention plus a per-step dynamic draft-length heuristic — the original batched-spec-decode KV-layout paper.
papers.numbers: 2.15x over optimized regular decoding at batch 8 (7.8B model, single A100); 5.8ms/token, ~1.1K tok/s
papers.long_context_behavior: Raggedness worsens with long variably-sized contexts; no long-context or compressed-KV evaluation.

papers.title: TETRIS: Optimal Draft Token Selection for Batch Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Under a shared verification-capacity budget, actively selects which draft tokens across ALL requests in the batch get verified, rather than fixed per-request speculation — batch-level allocation of the speculation budget.
papers.numbers: Consistently higher acceptance rate and capacity utilization vs baseline SD and dynamic per-request selection (relative gains; no single headline multiplier)
papers.long_context_behavior: Budget is compute/token slots, not KV bytes; no coupling to per-request KV footprint or context length — the memory-aware version of this scheduler does not exist.

papers.title: CXL-SpecKV: A Disaggregated FPGA Speculative KV-Cache for Datacenter LLM Serving
papers.idea: Speculative PREFETCH (not token speculation): predicts future tokens' KV entries and preloads them from CXL-attached FPGA memory, with an FPGA-hosted KV compression/decompression engine to cut link bandwidth.
papers.numbers: Up to 3.2x throughput vs GPU-only baselines; 2.8x memory cost reduction; compression cuts bandwidth up to 4x
papers.long_context_behavior: Extends the InfiniGen (OSDI'24) speculative-KV-prefetch line to CXL disaggregation; combining prefetch-speculation with token-speculation (whose drafts change which KV is needed) is unexplored.

papers.title: Striking the Right Balance between Compute and Copy: Improving LLM Inferencing Under Speculative Decoding (BMC)
papers.idea: Over-allocates KV tensor rows so in-place updates avoid KV copying; the redundant compute this creates is repurposed to run the drafter — an explicit KV-memory-layout x speculation co-design.
papers.numbers: 3.2x over HuggingFace baseline without SD; additional 1.39x when combined with SD; 1.36x vs vLLM, 2.29x vs DeepSpeed (CPU-focused, GPU-validated)
papers.long_context_behavior: Copy overhead grows with context length, so the repurposed-compute budget for drafting grows too; no long-context ablation given.

evidence: QuantSpec: 4-bit hierarchical DRAFTER KV keeps acceptance >90% with ~2.5x end-to-end speedup, ~1.3x memory reduction, and a 4-bit attention kernel 2.88x faster than FP16 FlashAttention; explicitly finds quantized drafter KV gives better draft-target agreement than sparse drafter KV (arXiv 2502.10424, ICML 2025).

VeriCache: at 4x KV compaction, acceptance stays >0.8 even at draft length 30; acceptance lengths ~19 (Qwen-32B) and ~23 (Llama-70B) per verification round vs ~1-2/11 for EAGLE and ~3-10 for a small draft model; up to 4x throughput vs full-KV (256 vs 102 tok/s on Llama-70B) with bit-identical outputs; composes with EAGLE for 4.35x vs 3.50x alone (arXiv 2605.17613).

VeriCache divergence measurement: KL between compressed-KV and full-KV decoding grows ~linearly in decode steps — ~6 nats after 250 steps with KVzip at 4x, i.e., probability e^-6 ≈ 2.5e-3 that unverified compressed-KV decoding emits the full-KV sequence — the quantitative case that lossy KV compression needs verification for long generations (arXiv 2605.17613).

VeriCache KV-footprint anchor: Llama-3.1-8B-1M decode step goes 5ms at 5K context (~0.6GB KV) to 25ms at 500K (~60GB KV); supported compressors span SnapKV/KVzip/KVzap/ExpectedAttention (dropping) and KIVI/KVQuant/RotateKV (quantization) behind one interface (arXiv 2605.17613).

SpecKV-gamma: across FP16/INT8/NF4 TARGET WEIGHT quantization (BitsAndBytes — not KV quantization despite the name), draft confidence/entropy predict acceptance with correlation ~0.56 over 5,112 step-level records; adaptive gamma gives +56.0% over fixed gamma=4 at 0.34ms/decision; the paper states the compression-speculation interaction 'has not been studied' (arXiv 2605.02888).

DeepSeek-V3: MTP draft head over a fully MLA (latent-KV) target achieves 85-90% second-token acceptance and 1.8x TPS in production — the existence proof that low-rank latent KV compression and speculative verification coexist at scale (arXiv 2412.19437; SGLang MTP integration adds up to 60% throughput, lmsys.org blog 2025-07-17).

MLA drafter conversion (2607.27269): converting MHA/GQA draft models to MLA 'can sharply reduce' draft-token acceptance due to low-rank factorization and RoPE attention-function errors; calibration-based functional reconstruction materially improves acceptance in 37 of 64 matched task cells across 192 configurations (Llama/Qwen x TransMLA/MHA2MLA x HF/vLLM).

Dustin: verifying with a compressed (importance-selected) target KV at 32K on Qwen2.5-72B yields 27.85x self-attention and 9.17x end-to-end speedup with claimed negligible accuracy loss — but no distributional certificate and no reported acceptance-rate shift from compressed verification (arXiv 2606.24957).

BudgetDraft: naive sparse-KV drafting acceptance collapses to near-zero by 16K context from the sparse/full mismatch; multi-view budget training restores 6.55x/4.46x/2.10x vs AR at 4K/8K/16K — evaluation stops at 16K (arXiv 2606.00144).

MagicDec: with a constant-KV (sink+window) drafter, spec-decode speedup GROWS with batch size — up to 2.51x for LLaMA-3.1-8B at batch 32-256 on 8K-32K+ sequences — because both draft and target costs become KV-loading-dominated; provides the (batch, seqlen) analytical model (arXiv 2408.11049, ICLR 2025).

TriForce: target-with-retrieval-sparse-KV (~4K budget) drafting at 128K context gives 2.31x on A100 (Llama2-7B-128K) and 7.78x with offloading on 2x RTX 4090 — still the longest-context drafter-KV-compression evaluation in the literature as of Aug 2026 (arXiv 2404.11912).

DeFT: tree attention over paged KV with KV-guided grouping cuts 73-99% of KV cache IO and ~100% of partial-result IO, for up to 2.23x end-to-end / 3.59x attention-latency speedup on tree workloads including speculative decoding (ICLR 2025, arXiv 2404.00242).

TransKV (TechRxiv Feb 2026): documents that uncommitted draft tokens consume block-granular KV pages and count toward token-budget schedulers in vLLM-style engines, limiting spec-decode speedups at high load; proposes transactional commit reducing speculative KV pressure from block-sized pages to token-sized buffers (DOI 10.36227/techrxiv.177101038.80960856).

BASS: batched spec decoding requires custom ragged-KV-tensor CUDA kernels; 2.15x over optimized regular decoding at batch 8 for a 7.8B model on one A100 (5.8ms/token, ~1.1K tok/s) (ACL Findings 2024, arXiv 2404.15778).

Target-KV quantization x spec decoding is quantified ONLY in grey literature: a dev.to engineering post claims mean accepted tokens/cycle drops 0.3-0.8 (FP8 E4M3) and 0.5-1.5 (INT8 per-token) with NO citable measurement source, referencing only vLLM issue #37618 (Qwen3.5 FP8-KV accuracy regression on B200); vLLM's own FP8-KV blog (2026-04-22, vllm-project.github.io) covers ITL slope (54% of BF16 for Llama-3.1-8B, break-even ~7K tokens) and 97-98% long-context AUC recovery but contains NO speculative-decoding section.

Lynx: bit-plane-split KV transfer (anchor MSBs + residual) lets decoding start speculatively on partial-precision KV with full-precision verification: up to 1.43x TTFT vs 8-bit KV quantization at BF16-level accuracy in disaggregated serving (arXiv 2607.01831).

LookaheadKV (ICLR 2026): draft-model-generation-guided KV eviction (the 2506.08373 SpecKV approach) is prefill-cost-bound, so learnable lookahead tokens replace the drafter — 14.5x cheaper eviction with <0.7% drop at 1K budget (~81% compression) (arXiv 2603.10899).

CXL-SpecKV: speculative KV prefetch into CXL/FPGA-disaggregated memory with hardware compression: 3.2x throughput vs GPU-only, 2.8x memory cost reduction, 4x bandwidth reduction — speculation applied to KV movement, disjoint from token speculation (arXiv 2512.11920).

gaps.gap: No published measurement of standard-drafter (EAGLE/MTP/independent) acceptance against a target whose KV is quantized or evicted — the exact configuration production stacks run (FP8-KV target + EAGLE-3 in vLLM/TRT-LLM).
gaps.why_open: SpecKV-gamma (2605.02888) states the compression-speculation interaction 'has not been studied' and then studies WEIGHT quantization (BitsAndBytes INT8/NF4), not KV; vLLM's FP8-KV blog (Apr 2026) has no spec-decode section; the only numbers anywhere are an uncited blog claim (0.3-1.5 accepted-token drop per cycle) and anecdotal vLLM issue #37618. The subtlety is contractual: verification against quantized-KV logits is 'lossless' relative to the wrong distribution, so acceptance drift and double-lossy compounding (drafter trained on BF16 features, target verifying in FP8-KV) are both unquantified.
gaps.closest_work: SpecKV-gamma (arXiv 2605.02888, weight-quant only); VeriCache (2605.17613, measures compressed-vs-full divergence but only with compressed KV as DRAFTER); dev.to/vLLM grey literature.

gaps.gap: Drafter-KV compression has no (compression-ratio x context-length x acceptance) scaling law — every point is a single fixed setting, and nothing exists past 128K.
gaps.why_open: QuantSpec fixes 4-bit and stops at ~32K; BudgetDraft sweeps budgets but stops at 16K; VeriCache reports one compaction ratio (4x) at ~100K; TriForce's 128K (2024) is still the max evaluated context. Nobody sweeps bits/budget against context to extend MagicDec's (batch, seqlen) analytical model with a compression axis — i.e., choose drafter KV precision/budget as a function of (batch, context, HBM) — even though QuantSpec (quantized beats sparse for acceptance) and BudgetDraft (sparse collapses at 16K) hint the frontier is nontrivial.
gaps.closest_work: MagicDec (2408.11049, model without compression axis); QuantSpec (2502.10424); BudgetDraft (2606.00144); VeriCache (2605.17613).

gaps.gap: Tree-shaped speculative KV under paged memory has no memory-side accounting: block-granular page waste, prefix-sharing interaction, and scheduler token-budget inflation for uncommitted tree branches are unmeasured at long context.
gaps.why_open: DeFT (ICLR'25) solved the IO/kernel side of tree attention over paged KV but not allocation; TransKV (TechRxiv Feb 2026, unreviewed, single preprint) is the only work treating uncommitted draft-KV pages as a first-class problem and appears to cover linear drafts, not trees; MineDraft (2603.18016) merely notes allocated-but-unwritten blocks in batch drafting. At 100K contexts with 64-node trees per request, per-branch page rounding times batch size is plausibly GBs of dead HBM, but no paper reports the number.
gaps.closest_work: TransKV (techrxiv 177101038); DeFT (2404.00242); Batch Speculative Decoding Done Right (2510.22876, correctness not memory).

gaps.gap: Compressed verification has no divergence certificate: Dustin/SpecPV/2512.21911 all claim 'negligible' or 'minor' degradation empirically, while the tooling to certify it exists separately and has never been connected.
gaps.why_open: VeriCache proved the needed measurement is tractable (KL to full-KV output grows ~linearly, ~6 nats/250 steps at 4x compaction) and the acceptance-theory framework (When Is a Draft Accepted, 2606.30265) provides exact KL-to-rejection certificates for relaxed criteria — but no work computes certified bounds for eviction/quantization-induced verification error, so 'negligible accuracy loss at 32K' (Dustin) is unfalsifiable at 128K or on tool-calling/code workloads where VeriCache shows compressed-KV divergence is catastrophic.
gaps.closest_work: VeriCache's KL-growth measurement (2605.17613); acceptance-region theory (2606.30265); Dustin (2606.24957) and SpecPV (2512.02337) as the uncertified claims.

gaps.gap: Latent-KV (MLA) targets and drafters lack any long-context or tree-speculation characterization: acceptance-vs-context curves for MTP-style heads on MLA targets, and compression of the drafter's own latent cache, do not exist.
gaps.why_open: DeepSeek-V3's 85-90% MTP acceptance is reported as a topic-level aggregate with no context-length axis; 2607.27269 shows MLA conversion of drafters breaks acceptance via attention-function error (a mechanism distinct from output-distribution shift, so existing acceptance theory doesn't cover it) but evaluates only short 200-prompt tasks; no work measures tree verification with absorbed-projection MLA kernels (FlashMLA-class) where the latent cache changes the arithmetic-intensity tradeoffs that motivated sparse drafting in the first place.
gaps.closest_work: DeepSeek-V3 (2412.19437); Functional Reconstruction for MLA Draft Models (2607.27269); SnapMLA (2602.10718, kernels only, no speculation).

gaps.gap: Batch-level scheduling that is jointly KV-compression-aware and speculation-aware does not exist: no scheduler models how target/drafter KV compression moves the batch-context boundary where speculation beats plain batching.
gaps.why_open: MagicDec's regime model assumes uncompressed target KV — FP8/4-bit target KV halves-to-quarters KV traffic and thus shifts the KV-bound crossover MagicDec relies on, invalidating its optimal-drafting prescriptions, yet no one has redone the analysis; SmartSpec's goodput control has no KV-byte term; TETRIS allocates verification compute, not KV bytes; BASS/TransKV handle layout, not policy. The needed artifact — a scheduler choosing (gamma, drafter budget, KV precision) per request under an HBM budget — has no paper.
gaps.closest_work: MagicDec (2408.11049); SmartSpec goodput (2406.14066); TETRIS (2502.15197); TransKV (techrxiv, mechanism without policy).

surveys.theme: Systems and theory of speculative decoding at long context: quantitative regime boundaries for when speculation pays off as context, batch size, and attention architecture (GQA/MLA) vary

papers.title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Roofline-style regime analysis: beyond a critical sequence length S_inflection decoding is KV-load-bound even at large batch, so a constant-KV (StreamingLLM sink+window) drafter — even self-speculation — gives speedup that GROWS with batch size; provides the analytical speedup model 1/Omega(gamma,alpha) * (gamma*T_D/T_T + T_V(gamma)/T_T) with Omega=(1-alpha^(gamma+1))/(1-alpha) for choosing drafting strategy vs (batch, seqlen).
papers.numbers: Up to 2.51x for Llama-3.1-8B at batch 32-256 (SnapKV-2048 drafter, 8xH100, 100K ctx); with StreamingLLM-512 on 8xA100: 0.95x @1K/b32, 1.13x @4K/b32, 1.32x @8K/b128, 1.72x @16K/b64, 1.69x @32K/b32; S_inflection ~= 4,000 tokens for Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-2-7B-32K on 8xA100 (lower on H100, higher on L40); drafter acceptance 0.84 @4K -> 0.79 @100K.
papers.long_context_behavior: Long context is the premise: draft-to-target cost ratio shrinks as batch*context grows because both are KV-dominated; drafter KV is O(1). GQA models have HIGHER S_inflection (lighter KV per token delays the memory-bound crossover), so GQA weakens the payoff regime — part-2 blog: Llama-2-7B (MHA) 2.0x vs Llama-3.1-8B (GQA) 1.84x at 32K on 8xA100, batches 32-128. Nothing evaluated past 100K, and the model ignores load/scheduling.

papers.title: SPIRe: Boosting LLM Inference Throughput with Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: MagicDec successor: draft model with static sparse (StreamingLLM-mask) KV, pruned initialization from the target, and feedback-memory (recurrent feedback transformer) trained so the drafter stays cheap at long context while keeping acceptance up.
papers.numbers: +100% modeled throughput of SD vs speculation with a much smaller vanilla draft model; +35% over MagicDec-style sparse self-speculation. Caveat: 'modeled' throughput, not full end-to-end serving numbers.
papers.long_context_behavior: Draft KV constant w.r.t. decode length by construction (StreamingLLM mask in training AND inference); explicitly targets the large-batch long-context KV-bound regime identified by MagicDec; claims gains are largest when context lengths vary across requests.

papers.title: Sequoia: Scalable, Robust, and Hardware-aware Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Dynamic programming computes the optimal draft-tree topology under a positional acceptance model; sampling-without-replacement verification robust across temperatures; a hardware-aware optimizer selects tree size/depth per platform (fits verification-cost curve per hardware).
papers.numbers: Up to 4.04x Llama2-7B / 3.73x Llama2-13B / 2.27x Vicuna-33B on A100 on-chip; Llama2-70B on one RTX-4090 at 0.57 s/token with offloading (~8x vs optimized offloading, ~9x vs DeepSpeed-Zero-Inference).
