papers.long_context_behavior: Tree optimizer models hardware (verification cost vs number of verified tokens) but NOT context length: verification cost per tree node grows with KV size at long context, so the DP's optimal tree should shrink with context — never re-solved with a context axis; experiments are short-context.

papers.title: Speculative Decoding Speed-of-Light: Optimal Lower Bounds via Branching Random Walks
papers.idea: Maps draft-tree token generation to branching random walks and proves tight bounds on any deterministic speculative algorithm: accepted tokens per iteration scale only LOGARITHMICALLY in verifier capacity P.
papers.numbers: E[X] <= (mu + mu_2) log(P)/mu^2 + O(1), mu = expected entropy of verifier output distribution, mu_2 = second log-moment; bound validated against well-optimized systems incl. EAGLE-3 — explains diminishing returns of giant trees (Sequoia/SpecExec regime).
papers.long_context_behavior: No explicit context axis, but the entropy parameter mu is context-dependent: grounded long contexts lower output entropy and raise the ceiling (consistent with PLD/SuffixDecoding), while drafter-alpha collapse beyond training windows is outside the model. Directly contradicts unbounded-tree-growth acceptance assumptions.

papers.title: A Theoretical Perspective for Speculative Decoding Algorithm
papers.idea: Markov-chain abstraction of decoding: exact formula for expected number of rejections in terms of draft-target TV distance; proves speculative decoding achieves the lower bound on expected rejections among unbiased rejection-based algorithms; extends to batch speculative decoding with rejection characterization.
papers.numbers: Closed-form expected rejections ~ sum of per-step TV distances; optimality proof; quality-vs-acceleration tradeoff curves for biased variants. No system numbers.
papers.long_context_behavior: Distributions are fixed inputs — no dependence of TV distance (hence alpha) on context length, KV budget, or position; the empirically observed long-context acceptance drift has no counterpart in this framework.

papers.title: Block Verification Accelerates Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Verifies the whole draft block jointly instead of token-by-token; provably optimal expected accepted tokens per iteration among lossless verifiers and never worse than token-level rejection sampling.
papers.numbers: Consistent 5-8% wall-clock speedup over standard token verification across tasks; zero cost, drop-in. Follow-up Greedy Multi-Path Block Verification (arXiv 2602.16961, Feb 2026) proves BV optimal even against verifiers using off-path probabilities and gains >30% block efficiency / >15% walltime over BV via multi-path generalization.
papers.long_context_behavior: Pure verification-rule theory; acceptance gain is distribution-level and context-free. Relevant at long context because each verification pass is expensive (KV-bound) so per-pass accepted-token optimality matters more, but no length-dependent analysis exists.

papers.title: Towards Optimal Multi-draft Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Computes the optimal acceptance rate for multi-draft speculation via the dual of the optimal transport problem (following SpecTr), discovering equivalence to a subset-selection problem, making the theoretical upper bound computable at realistic vocabulary sizes.
papers.numbers: First measurement of the MDSD theoretical upper bound for vocab sizes in the thousands; existing verification algorithms provably fall short of the bound; sampling WITHOUT replacement dominates with-replacement drafting.
papers.long_context_behavior: Context-free distribution-level theory; quantifies headroom for tree/multi-draft verification but the draft/target distributions' drift with context length is unmodeled.

papers.title: SpecDec++: Boosting Speculative Decoding via Adaptive Candidate Lengths
papers.idea: Formulates choice of candidate length K (gamma) as an MDP; proves the optimal policy is a threshold rule — stop speculating when predicted rejection probability exceeds a threshold — and implements it with a trained acceptance-prediction head.
papers.numbers: +7.2% (Alpaca), +11.1% (HumanEval), +9.4% (GSM8K) relative over best fixed-K speculative decoding (Llama-2-chat 7B draft / 70B target).
papers.long_context_behavior: The optimal-stopping theory is the principled version of draft-length control that long-context systems need (acceptance varies with position/context), but the acceptance predictor is trained and evaluated short-context; threshold calibration under long-context acceptance drift is unstudied.

papers.title: The Synergy of Speculative Decoding and Batching in Serving Large Language Models
papers.idea: First systematic characterization of speculation x batching: shows the optimal speculation length shrinks as batch size grows (compute saturation), and proposes adaptive per-batch speculation length.
papers.numbers: Characterization across LLMs/GPUs; adaptive scheme matches or beats best fixed speculation length; establishes that a fixed gamma is suboptimal across batch sizes.
papers.long_context_behavior: Pre-dates the KV-bound insight: analysis is compute-centric, short contexts; MagicDec later showed the batch conclusion inverts once context makes decoding KV-bound — the two regimes have never been unified in one model.

papers.title: Optimizing Speculative Decoding for Serving LLMs Using Goodput (SmartSpec; latest arXiv version renamed TurboSpec: Closed-loop Speculation Control System)
papers.idea: Under continuous batching, fixed-length speculation can increase latency at high request rates; picks per-request speculation length (0..n) by maximizing estimated goodput from observed system load and acceptance; closed-loop control in the renamed TurboSpec version.
papers.numbers: Up to 3.2x average request latency reduction vs non-speculative baselines across request rates, draft styles (draft-model, prompt-lookup, tree); basis for vLLM dynamic speculative decoding.
papers.long_context_behavior: Goodput model is load-aware but NOT length-aware: no KV-boundedness term, so it cannot predict the MagicDec inversion where speculation improves WITH batch at long context; combining goodput control with length-dependent cost/acceptance models is open.

papers.title: AdaServe: Accelerating Multi-SLO LLM Serving with SLO-Customized Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Multi-SLO serving as constrained optimization: hardware-aware algorithm builds a per-request speculation tree sized to each request's latency target; speculate-select-verify pipeline trades speculation quota across requests to maximize goodput.
papers.numbers: Up to 4.3x fewer SLO violations and up to 1.9x higher goodput vs best baselines (CMU/Princeton/EPFL/AWS/Purdue).
papers.long_context_behavior: Per-request tree sizing is the right control knob for heterogeneous contexts, but the cost model is not KV/context-aware and evaluation is not long-context; no interaction with context-dependent acceptance decay.

papers.title: FASER: Fine-Grained Phase Management for Speculative Decoding in Dynamic LLM Serving
papers.idea: Breaks the rigid batch-wide draft-then-verify serialization: per-request speculative length inside a continuous batch, early pruning of rejected tokens inside verification, and chunked verification frontiers overlapped with drafting via fine-grained spatial GPU multiplexing.
papers.numbers: vLLM prototype: up to +53% throughput and up to 1.92x latency reduction vs state-of-the-art SD serving systems.
papers.long_context_behavior: Load-adaptive, not length-adaptive; chunked verification overlap becomes more valuable as verification gets KV-bound at long context but no context-scaling study is reported.

papers.title: Batch Speculative Decoding Done Right (EQSPEC/EXSPEC)
papers.idea: Identifies the ragged-tensor problem in batched speculation (per-sequence accept counts corrupt position IDs, masks, KV state) and shows existing open-source batch implementations violate output equivalence — including sampling bonus tokens from the DRAFT distribution (DSD, Meta impl); EQSPEC guarantees equivalence, EXSPEC adds cross-batch same-length grouping.
papers.numbers: Correctness audit: BSP emits repetitive tokens, DSD emits unknown symbols; EXSPEC ~3x throughput at batch 8 vs batch 1 while maintaining 95% output equivalence.
papers.long_context_behavior: Raggedness worsens with long, variable-length contexts in a batch (more divergent accept counts, bigger realignment cost); no long-context or tree-mode evaluation — correct batched tree speculation over 32K+ ragged contexts remains undemonstrated.

papers.title: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Llama at Scale: Challenges and Solutions
papers.idea: Production deployment report of EAGLE-style speculation for Llama serving: GPU-efficient tree attention, multi-round speculative decoding, training and inference co-optimizations at fleet scale.
papers.numbers: ~4 ms/token at batch 1 on 8xH100 (claimed 10% faster than best known); 1.4x-2.0x speedup at large production batch sizes.
papers.long_context_behavior: Confirms speculation survives production batching but with compressed gains (1.4-2.0x vs 2-3x at batch 1); context-length-conditioned acceptance/speedup breakdowns are not published.

papers.title: EAGLE 3.1 + TorchSpec (vLLM/EAGLE team collaboration)
papers.idea: Fixes attention drift (drafter attention migrating from sink/prompt to its own generations as depth grows) via FC normalization of target hidden states + post-norm hidden states across decoding steps; TorchSpec provides scalable draft training; backward compatible with EAGLE-3 checkpoints (vLLM v0.22.0).
papers.numbers: Up to 2x longer acceptance length than EAGLE-3; Kimi K2.6 on GB200 (SPEED-Bench coding): 2.03x per-user throughput at concurrency 1, 1.71x at c=4, 1.66x at c=16.
papers.long_context_behavior: Explicitly markets 'stronger long-context robustness' and better train-to-inference extrapolation, but publishes no acceptance-vs-context curve beyond 32K; concurrency scaling still decays (2.03x -> 1.66x).

papers.title: P-EAGLE: Parallel-Drafting EAGLE with Scalable Training
papers.idea: Replaces EAGLE's sequential draft loop with a single forward pass: 4-layer head with learnable mask-token embeddings emits all K draft tokens at once; removes drafting latency from the critical path so deeper speculation (K=7) becomes optimal.
papers.numbers: Up to 1.69x over EAGLE-3 on B200; +55-69% throughput at concurrency 1 shrinking to +5-25% at concurrency 64; optimal K=7 vs K=3 for EAGLE-3; heads for GPT-OSS 120B/20B, Qwen3-Coder 30B.
papers.long_context_behavior: Training data median ~3.9K tokens (P90 10.8K); ecosystem consensus is EAGLE-family acceptance still decays beyond trained window (>32K); concurrency-64 numbers quantify how thin the speculation margin is in the throughput regime.

papers.title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
papers.idea: Semi-autoregressive drafter (parallel backbone + small sequential module for intra-block dependencies) plus confidence-scheduled verification: per-request verification length set from prefix survival probabilities AND current system throughput, treating speculation as a scheduling problem under concurrency.
papers.numbers: +60-85% per-user generation speed at MATCHED throughput vs production MTP-1 baseline in DeepSeek-V4 serving; mitigates verification waste at high concurrency.
papers.long_context_behavior: Runs in a 1M-context (hybrid sparse-attention) production stack but publishes no context-conditioned acceptance data; addresses acceptance decay across draft positions, not across context length.

papers.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report (MTP as speculative decoding under MLA)
papers.idea: Multi-Token Prediction module trained with the base model doubles as a self-contained drafter; combined with MLA's compressed KV this is the production reference point for speculation on latent-attention targets.
papers.numbers: Second-token acceptance 85-90% across topics; ~1.8x TPS from MTP speculation; SGLang/vLLM MTP integrations report 1.2-2.1x serving gains; acceptance drops sharply at draft positions beyond 1-2 (module trained for first-token prediction, reused autoregressively).
papers.long_context_behavior: MLA compresses KV ~93% vs MHA-equivalent, raising attention arithmetic intensity and weakening the KV-bound premise that long-context speculation payoff relies on; no public MTP acceptance-vs-context-length curve exists even for V4's 1M window.

papers.title: Hardware-Efficient Attention for Fast Decoding (GTA/GLA)
papers.idea: Designs attention variants by maximizing arithmetic intensity per byte of KV loaded: Grouped-Tied Attention (ties K/V, ~half GQA's KV) and Grouped Latent Attention (parallel-shardable latent attention); analyzes how multi-token (speculative) queries multiply arithmetic intensity.
papers.numbers: GLA kernel up to 2x faster than FlashMLA specifically in the speculative-decoding setting (query length > 1); up to 2x end-to-end online-serving gains from reduced per-device KV fetch.
papers.long_context_behavior: Provides the kernel-level mechanism for why verification of gamma tokens is nearly free when KV-bound — and why MLA-family attention (already high intensity) benefits differently; the interaction 'attention design x speculation payoff frontier' is analyzed at kernel level but not at end-to-end regime level.

papers.title: Rethinking LLM Inference Bottlenecks: Insights from Latent Attention and Mixture-of-Experts
papers.idea: Arithmetic-intensity analysis showing MLA's intensity is over two orders of magnitude higher than MHA, moving attention from memory-bound to compute-bound on modern GPUs, and that batched expert-parallel MoE reaches dense-layer-like intensity.
papers.numbers: MLA arithmetic intensity >100x MHA; attention becomes compute-bound under MLA (vs 1-8 FLOPs/byte memory-bound MHA decode).
papers.long_context_behavior: Directly undermines the universality of the MagicDec argument: if the target's attention is compute-bound (MLA), speculation's extra verification FLOPs are no longer free at long context — nobody has re-derived S_inflection or the speedup-grows-with-batch inversion for MLA/hybrid targets.

papers.title: StreamServe: Adaptive Speculative Flows for Low-Latency Disaggregated LLM Serving
papers.idea: First system co-adapting request routing and speculation depth inside a disaggregated prefill/decode architecture (StreamScheduler, FlowGuard metric-aware routing, SpecuStream runtime-adaptive speculation).
papers.numbers: Claims 11-18x latency reduction vs tensor-parallel vLLM baselines and up to 2,235 tok/s on summarization — but on only 4 GPUs, 80 queries/benchmark, short-context benchmarks (Alpaca/GSM8K/HumanEval/SUM); baseline strength questionable.
papers.long_context_behavior: No context lengths reported; demonstrates the disaggregation x speculation control problem exists but leaves KV-transfer interference, long-context prefill contention, and SLO-aware fallback unmeasured.

papers.title: Lossless but Not Free: An Empirical Anatomy of Speculative Decoding on Consumer Hardware
papers.idea: Backend-level audit showing speculation pays off only when verification executes with genuine batch parallelism and the draft/target latency gap is real; quantized Metal backends serialize 'parallel' verification, silently erasing the payoff regime.
papers.numbers: Best 1.61x at K=6; 3 of 5 draft/target configs DECELERATE; acceptance declines 69.7% (K=1) -> 37.8% at optimal config; distribution equivalence verified over ~9,200 tokens (chi^2=162.5, p=0.976).
papers.long_context_behavior: No context axis, but establishes that the memory-boundedness argument is hardware-implementation-contingent: where kernels serialize multi-token verification, the entire long-context speculation case collapses regardless of theory.

papers.title: Acceptance Dynamics Across Cognitive Domains in Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Empirical acceptance-length study across task domains and tree depths: task type dominates tree depth as the determinant of acceptance; identifies the 'efficiency inversion' tipping point where marginal drafting cost exceeds expected contribution.
papers.numbers: In the evaluated configuration only chat exceeds expected accepted length 1.0; acceptance probability shows a small positive trend with depth (context-commitment effect); entropy-acceptance correlations negative but weak.
papers.long_context_behavior: Domain/entropy structure of acceptance is the empirical input any context-length acceptance theory needs, but the study itself does not vary input context length.

papers.title: TensorRT-LLM speculative decoding (docs) + vLLM speculative decoding (docs)
papers.idea: Production engine constraint surface: TensorRT-LLM supports draft-model/EAGLE-3/ReDrafter/n-gram; vLLM V1 rebuilt spec decode around EAGLE/MTP/n-gram.
papers.numbers: TensorRT-LLM: dynamic draft-tree mode NOT supported for sliding-window-attention or MLA models (DeepSeek, gpt-oss); n-gram speculation 2-3x on code in production; vLLM: draft-model SD unsupported through v0.10.0, pipeline parallelism not composable with SD through v0.15.0.
papers.long_context_behavior: The engines that serve 128K-1M contexts cannot combine dynamic tree speculation with exactly the attention architectures (MLA, SWA/hybrid) those contexts are served with — the concrete serving-side long-context limitation as of mid-2026.

evidence: MagicDec regime boundary: S_inflection ~= 4,000 tokens for Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-2-7B-32K on 8xA100 — below it SD speedup decreases with batch size, above it speedup INCREASES with batch; up to 2.51x at batch 32-256; StreamingLLM-512 drafter acceptance 0.84 at 4K vs 0.79 at 100K context (arXiv 2408.11049, ICLR 2025).

GQA weakens the long-context speculation case: GQA models have higher S_inflection due to lighter KV footprint — MHA Llama-2-7B gets 2.0x vs GQA Llama-3.1-8B 1.84x at 32K, batches 32-128 on 8xA100 (MagicDec-part2, infini-ai-lab.github.io/MagicDec-part2).

MLA breaks the memory-boundedness premise: MLA arithmetic intensity is >2 orders of magnitude above MHA, shifting attention from memory-bound to compute-bound (arXiv 2507.15465); GLA kernels are 2x faster than FlashMLA specifically at query length >1, i.e., in speculative verification (arXiv 2505.21487).

Speed-of-light ceiling: for any deterministic speculative algorithm, E[accepted tokens/iter] <= (mu+mu_2)log(P)/mu^2 + O(1) — only logarithmic in verifier capacity P; bound empirically tight against EAGLE-3 (arXiv 2512.11718, EACL 2026).

Optimal verification rules: block verification is provably optimal per iteration and gives 5-8% free wall-clock over token-level rejection (arXiv 2403.10444, ICLR 2025); greedy multi-path BV adds >30% block efficiency and >15% walltime over BV (arXiv 2602.16961); existing multi-draft verifiers fall measurably short of the OT-dual optimal acceptance bound (arXiv 2502.18779, ICLR 2025).

Optimal draft length is a threshold policy: SpecDec++ proves the MDP-optimal stopping rule is 'stop when predicted rejection probability crosses a threshold', worth +7.2-11.1% over fixed gamma (arXiv 2405.19715, COLM 2025); optimal gamma also shifts with batch size (arXiv 2310.18813) and with system load — fixed-length speculation can INCREASE latency at high request rates, SmartSpec/TurboSpec goodput control recovers up to 3.2x latency (arXiv 2406.14066).

Batched speculation was silently wrong: open-source batch SD implementations violate output equivalence (bonus tokens sampled from the DRAFT distribution in DSD and Meta's implementation; corrupted KV alignment); EQSPEC restores exactness with ~3x throughput at batch 8 (arXiv 2510.22876).

Throughput-regime reality check from production: Meta reports 1.4-2.0x at production batch sizes (vs ~2-3x batch-1) and ~4 ms/token bs=1 on 8xH100 (arXiv 2508.08192); P-EAGLE gains fall from +55-69% at concurrency 1 to +5-25% at concurrency 64 (arXiv 2602.01469, vLLM blog); EAGLE 3.1 on Kimi K2.6/GB200 decays 2.03x (c=1) -> 1.66x (c=16) (vllm.ai blog 2026-05-26).

MLA-target production speculation: DeepSeek-V3 MTP second-token acceptance 85-90%, ~1.8x TPS, but acceptance collapses at draft positions >2 (arXiv 2412.19437); DeepSeek-V4's DSpark makes verification length a scheduling variable (prefix survival probability x system throughput) for +60-85% per-user speed at matched throughput vs MTP-1 (arXiv 2607.05147).

Serving-engine long-context constraint: TensorRT-LLM dynamic draft-tree mode is unsupported for MLA and sliding-window-attention models (DeepSeek, gpt-oss) as of 2026 (nvidia.github.io/TensorRT-LLM docs); vLLM had no draft-model SD through v0.10.0 and no PP+SD composition through v0.15.0 (docs.vllm.ai).

Counter-evidence on acceptance drift: MiniMax-M3 EAGLE-3 head reports acceptance length essentially FLAT from 1K to 32K prompt (AL 2.64 -> 2.63) on SPEED-Bench (huggingface.co/blog/lujangusface/tw-eagle3-minimax), while OWL measures EAGLE-3 collapsing to 0.81x on long inputs (arXiv 2510.07535) — acceptance-vs-context behavior is model/training-data dependent, not a law.

SLO/phase-level control gains: AdaServe cuts SLO violations up to 4.3x and lifts goodput 1.9x with per-request hardware-aware speculation trees (EuroSys 2026, arXiv 2501.12162); FASER's per-request lengths + intra-verification pruning + draft/verify overlap gives +53% throughput and 1.92x latency in vLLM (arXiv 2604.20503).

MagicDec successor economics: SPIRe (sparse-KV draft + pruned init + feedback memory) claims +100% modeled SD throughput vs small-drafter SD and +35% vs MagicDec-style self-speculation (arXiv 2504.06419, MatX).

Hardware contingency: on consumer/quantized backends 3 of 5 draft/target configs DECELERATE because verification is not genuinely batch-parallel; best case only 1.61x at K=6 with acceptance falling 69.7%->37.8% (arXiv 2607.17283).

gaps.gap: No unified payoff model coupling context length, batch/load, and attention architecture: MagicDec's analytical model has (batch, seqlen) but no load/SLO term; SmartSpec/TurboSpec's goodput has load but no KV-boundedness/context term; no published model predicts the speculation-payoff frontier for a given (batch, context, attention type, SLO) point, and none has been validated against a production engine.
gaps.why_open: The two model families were developed by disjoint communities (algorithms vs serving) and validated in incompatible settings — MagicDec on its own kernels at fixed request sets, goodput controllers on short-context traces; nobody has instrumented one engine across both axes.
gaps.closest_work: MagicDec (2408.11049) S_inflection analysis; TurboSpec/SmartSpec (2406.14066) goodput control; FASER (2604.20503) and AdaServe (2501.12162) add load-adaptivity but still no context axis.

gaps.gap: The regime analysis has not been re-derived for MLA/hybrid-attention targets: MagicDec-part2 only shows GQA raises S_inflection; with MLA attention compute-bound (>100x MHA intensity per 2507.15465) the 'verification is nearly free at long context' premise weakens or reverses, yet no paper computes S_inflection, optimal gamma, or speedup-vs-batch curves for DeepSeek-style MLA or 2026 hybrid SWA+compression targets at 128K-1M.
gaps.why_open: MLA-era frontier models (DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi) ship proprietary MTP heads and serving stacks; academic regime analyses still use Llama-class GQA/MHA models; TensorRT-LLM cannot even run dynamic tree speculation on MLA models, blocking measurement.
gaps.closest_work: MagicDec-part2 GQA observation; Rethinking LLM Inference Bottlenecks (2507.15465); GTA/GLA kernel analysis (2505.21487); DeepSeek-V3 MTP production numbers (2412.19437).

gaps.gap: Optimal tree shape as a function of context length is unsolved: Sequoia's DP takes hardware verification-cost curves at a FIXED context and position-independent acceptance; at 100K contexts per-node verification cost is dominated by KV loads and the BRW log(P) ceiling implies large trees waste bandwidth, so optimal trees should flatten/shrink with context — no one has published optimal (size, depth) vs context curves or a context-aware tree optimizer.
gaps.why_open: Requires joint modeling of KV-bound verification cost (grows with S) and context-dependent acceptance (drifts with S), plus ragged tree-attention kernels at long context which are themselves immature (LongSpec's hybrid attention is single-request).
gaps.closest_work: Sequoia (2402.12374) hardware-aware DP; Speed-of-Light BRW bound (2512.11718); AdaServe's SLO-sized trees (2501.12162) — none has a context axis.

gaps.gap: Acceptance theory has no context-length axis and the empirics are contradictory: OWL shows EAGLE-3 collapsing to 0.81x on long inputs while MiniMax-M3's head is flat 1K-32K (AL 2.64->2.63); no theory ties alpha (or the BRW entropy parameter mu) to context length, retrieval position, or drafter training-window coverage, so nobody can predict which drafter/model pairs drift — it must be measured per checkpoint.
gaps.why_open: All acceptance theory (Markov-chain 2411.00841, OT 2502.18779, level-set certificates 2606.30265, BRW 2512.11718) treats draft/target distributions as fixed inputs; connecting them requires a model of how distribution divergence evolves with context, which needs controlled long-context acceptance datasets that only started appearing (LongSpecBench, SPEED-Bench) and disagree.
gaps.closest_work: BRW bound's entropy dependence (2512.11718); OWL measurements (2510.07535); Attention Drift mechanism + EAGLE 3.1 norm fixes (2605.09992, vLLM blog 2026-05-26); Acceptance Dynamics (2604.14682) varies domain but not input length.

gaps.gap: Output-equivalent batched speculation at long context is undemonstrated: EQSPEC guarantees equivalence only for chain speculation at short contexts with scaling through batch 8; MagicDec runs batch 256 at 32K-100K but on bespoke kernels with StreamingLLM drafting and no equivalence audit under continuous batching; no system shows correct tree or chain speculation under continuous batching with ragged 32K-128K contexts, and production engines forbid the needed combinations (TRT-LLM: no dynamic tree with MLA/SWA; vLLM: no PP+SD through 0.15.0).
gaps.why_open: Raggedness (divergent accept counts) compounds with heterogeneous long contexts, corrupting position IDs/KV alignment exactly where realignment is most expensive; correctness audits (2510.22876) arrived only late 2025 and did not cover tree mode or long contexts.
gaps.closest_work: Batch Speculative Decoding Done Right (2510.22876); Meta's production report (2508.08192, no equivalence audit published); MagicDec large-batch experiments (2408.11049).

gaps.gap: Speculation control under disaggregated prefill/decode serving with long contexts is unmeasured: long-context serving is dominated by P/D disaggregation and KV transfer (Mooncake-style), but every speculation controller (SmartSpec, AdaServe, FASER, DSpark) assumes colocated engines; StreamServe is the only P/D+speculation system and it is 4 GPUs / 80 queries / short benchmarks with implausible 11-18x baselines — speculation's interaction with KV-transfer bandwidth, prefill interference, and per-request fallback at 100K+ contexts has no credible study.
gaps.why_open: Requires a production-scale disaggregated testbed plus per-request speculation control in the decode tier, and the KV-transfer cost of draft-side state (or sparse drafter caches) across tiers has no established design; academic groups lack the infrastructure and industrial systems (DeepSeek DSpark) don't publish context-conditioned data.
gaps.closest_work: StreamServe (2604.09562); DSpark load-aware verification in DeepSeek-V4 serving (2607.05147); AdaServe (EuroSys 2026) and FASER (2604.20503) for colocated control.

surveys.theme: Alternative drafters for long context: retrieval/n-gram/suffix-automaton drafting from the prompt, SSM/linear-attention drafters with O(1) state, cross-tokenizer/universal drafters, block-diffusion drafting, and cascade/hierarchical speculation — state size vs context length, acceptance on long inputs, and evidence (or absence) at 128K+

papers.title: Mamba Drafters for Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Uses Mamba (SSM) as a cross-model external drafter: linear-time drafting with a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing KV cache, plus a multi-armed-bandit test-time tree-search that adapts draft tree shape per input.
papers.numbers: Mamba-130M drafter ~2x throughput of Pythia-410M transformer drafter; 138.8 tok/s on XSum greedy vs 70.5 for Pythia-410M; MT-Bench 128.2 tok/s vs EAGLE 125.6 on Pythia-6.9B; acceptance length 2.1-5.4; MAB tree search +15.6% throughput on HumanEval; ~3x faster drafting than TriForce at 8K.
papers.long_context_behavior: Drafter state is O(1) by construction: decoding memory constant while Mistral/EAGLE drafter KV grows linearly (52GB vs 72GB peak at 8K). At 8K LongBench, Mamba acceptance 2.80-2.87 vs Mistral drafter's declining 2.21 and EAGLE's 2.64 (EAGLE even with YaRN extension). Maximum evaluated context is 8K — nothing at 32K/128K, so the regime where O(1) state should dominate is unmeasured.

papers.title: The Mamba in the Llama: Distilling and Accelerating Hybrid Models
papers.idea: Distills a transformer into a hybrid Mamba model reusing attention-layer weights, and introduces a hardware-aware multi-step speculative decoding algorithm that works on recurrent Mamba/hybrid targets (recomputing states for accepted prefixes efficiently).
papers.numbers: Distilled hybrid: 29.61 LC win rate AlpacaEval2, 7.35 MT-Bench; speculative decoding demonstrated on Mamba and hybrid targets (first to do so); no single headline multiplier in abstract.
papers.long_context_behavior: Distilled hybrid shows near-perfect needle-in-a-haystack at 20x the distillation length — evidence that SSM/hybrid targets extrapolate — but the speculative decoding contribution is evaluated at short generation lengths; no long-context speculation numbers.

papers.title: SpecLA: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Linear-Attention Models
papers.idea: Runtime for chain/tree speculation on stateful linear-attention (Gated DeltaNet) targets: topology-aware verification kernels respect recurrent dependencies and compact factors recover the accepted-state trajectory without full recomputation; drafter deliberately kept Transformer-style since short draft windows don't benefit from recurrence.
papers.numbers: Up to 1.70x end-to-end over autoregressive on GDN-1.3B target (H100) — well below transformer-target spec-decode multipliers.
papers.long_context_behavior: Target state is O(1) so memory never grows with context, but verification must serially respect recurrence, capping speedup; no context-length scaling study — the economics of speculating for O(1)-state targets at 128K remain uncharacterized.

papers.title: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding in Hybrid Language Models
papers.idea: Uses the SSM/linear-attention components of hybrid models as internal drafters; shows architectural composition (parallel Mamba-2+attention per layer vs sequential interleaving) determines speculative viability.
papers.numbers: Parallel hybrid (Falcon-H1): alpha=0.68 at k=2 greedy; sequential hybrid (Qwen3.5-style): alpha=0.038 — an 18x gap; LayerSkip-style early exit recovers ~12x acceptance for sequential hybrids; scale-invariant 0.5B-3B.
papers.long_context_behavior: No long-context evaluation, but it is the reference result for drafting on the hybrid architectures that dominate 2026 long-context frontier models; sequential hybrids — the common composition — are effectively un-draftable via component reuse.

papers.title: SAM Decoding: Speculative Decoding via Suffix Automaton
papers.idea: Builds a static suffix automaton over a text corpus and a dynamic suffix automaton over the prompt + generated text; finds the exact longest suffix match in amortized O(1) per step (vs O(n) n-gram scans), switching to an auxiliary drafter when match quality is low.
papers.numbers: 2.27x over AR on Spec-Bench combined with Token Recycling; 2.49x combined with EAGLE-2, surpassing prior approaches at publication; OWL's LongSpecBench measures SAMD at 3.18 acceptance length on 4K-64K inputs, and SAMD+Token-Recycling at 4.98 — beating EAGLE-3's 1.28.
papers.long_context_behavior: Automaton state grows O(n) in prompt+generation length but with tiny constants (pointers, no GPU memory); update/retrieval cost is length-independent. Acceptance on long grounded inputs holds up (3.18-4.98 on 4K-64K) with zero drafter KV; never evaluated at 128K+.

papers.title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight (arXiv 2411.04975; Snowflake, shipped in vLLM via ArcticInference)
papers.idea: Model-free drafting from two suffix trees — a global tree over prior outputs and a per-request tree over the current prompt/output — with adaptive speculation length that extends to hundreds of tokens when patterns repeat (agentic pipelines, SQL, self-refine).
papers.numbers: 5.3x on AgenticSQL, 2.5x on SWE-Bench vs vanilla; 2.8x faster than EAGLE-2/3, 1.9x faster than Token Recycling, 1.3-3x over PLD end-to-end in vLLM; accepts up to hundreds of tokens per step; tree ops ~4us update / ~12us lookup.
papers.long_context_behavior: Suffix-tree state is ~10.75 bytes/token in CPU RAM (6.15GB per ~572M tokens; 144GB CPU RAM caches ~31 days of generation) — linear but off-GPU and 3-4 orders cheaper than KV; drafting cost is context-length-independent, verification still pays full target KV. No explicit 128K+ input ablation; OWL measures its acceptance at 3.41 on 4K-64K LongSpecBench.

papers.title: Turning Trash into Treasure: Token Recycling
papers.idea: Stores top-k candidate tokens from past decoding steps in a vocabulary-indexed adjacency matrix and BFS-builds a draft tree from them — recycling logits the model already computed, with <2MB of state.
papers.numbers: ~2x speedup across model sizes, ~30% over prior train-free methods; <2MB storage; OWL measures 3.16 acceptance length on 4K-64K inputs (vs EAGLE-3 1.28).
papers.long_context_behavior: State is O(vocab), strictly constant in context length — one of the only drafters whose memory is independent of both prompt and generation length; long-context acceptance (3.16 at up to 64K) held up in OWL's third-party benchmark without any long-context tuning.

papers.title: DReSD: Dense Retrieval for Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Replaces REST-style exact suffix matching with approximate nearest-neighbor search over contextualized token embeddings, retrieving semantically (not lexically) matched continuations for drafting.
papers.numbers: +87% acceptance rate, +65% accepted tokens, +19% generation speed vs sparse (exact-match) retrieval on average; up to 4.64x in optimal configuration.
papers.long_context_behavior: Datastore is external and embedding index grows with corpus, not context; retrieval latency depends on index size not prompt length. No long-context input evaluation — semantic retrieval FROM the 128K prompt itself (dense analog of PLD) is untried.

papers.title: NEST: Nearest Neighbor Speculative Decoding for LLM Generation and Attribution
papers.idea: Semi-parametric kNN-LM mixture proposes real corpus spans; an approximate (relaxed) speculative procedure accepts a prefix of the retrieved span — deliberately lossy, trading strict distribution preservation for attribution and factuality gains.
papers.numbers: 1.8x inference speedup on Llama-2-Chat-70B; improves generation quality and attribution over base LM and kNN-LM on knowledge-intensive tasks.
papers.long_context_behavior: Precursor of the RAPID-style 'quality-improving speculation' line; retrieval state lives in an external index, not context; no long-context input study.

papers.title: LogitSpec: Accelerating Retrieval-based Speculative Decoding via Next Next Token Speculation
papers.idea: Uses the last step's logits to predict not just the next but the next-next token, using both as retrieval anchors to expand and better rank model-free draft candidates.
papers.numbers: 2.61x average speedup reported (2.58x avg in comparisons vs 2.40x Token Recycling, 2.34x SAM-Decoding on Spec-Bench).
papers.long_context_behavior: Same O(vocab)/pointer-scale state as its model-free base; no long-context evaluation.

papers.title: Accelerating LLM Inference with Lossless Speculative Decoding Algorithms for Heterogeneous Vocabularies
papers.venue: ICML 2025 Oral (arXiv 2502.05202; Weizmann/Intel — Timor et al.)
papers.idea: Three lossless algorithms (string-level exact match, token-level intersection, and a rejection-sampling variant) that let a drafter with a DIFFERENT tokenizer/vocabulary speculate for any target with provable distribution preservation, using off-the-shelf models with no training.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.8x over autoregressive decoding on summarization, programming, and long-context tasks.
papers.long_context_behavior: Explicitly includes long-context tasks in evaluation (one of very few cross-tokenizer works to do so) but reports no acceptance-vs-context-length curve; cross-vocab re-tokenization drift over long copied spans is unquantified.

papers.title: OmniDraft: A Cross-vocabulary, Online Adaptive Drafter for On-device Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: One 68M drafter serves any target: an online n-gram cache translates between drafter and target vocabularies while hybrid distillation fine-tuning adapts the drafter to user data on the fly ('one drafter for all').
papers.numbers: 1.5-2x speedup pairing Llama-68M with Vicuna-7B, Qwen2-7B, Llama3-8B targets.
papers.long_context_behavior: On-device short-context focus; the online n-gram translation cache grows with observed text but is small; no long-context evaluation.

papers.title: TokenTiming: A Dynamic Alignment Method for Universal Speculative Decoding Model Pairs
papers.idea: Re-encodes the draft token sequence into the target's vocabulary and uses Dynamic Time Warping to build a probability-mass mapping between mismatched token sequences, enabling speculative sampling across arbitrary model pairs without retraining.
papers.numbers: 1.57x speedup across tasks with off-the-shelf mismatched-vocabulary pairs.
papers.long_context_behavior: No long-context evaluation; DTW alignment cost scales with draft length, not context, so drafting side is length-safe but unproven on long inputs.

papers.title: DFlash: Block Diffusion for Flash Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: 5-layer block-diffusion drafter generates a 16-token block in one forward pass, conditioned on target-model features from 5 uniformly-selected layers injected into the K/V projections of every draft layer ('the target knows the context best').
papers.numbers: Up to 6.1x on Qwen3-8B, ~2.5x faster than EAGLE-3; LMSYS: acceptance/speedup 4.2/3.3x GSM8K, 4.0/3.2x HumanEval, 3.0/2.2x MT-Bench vs EAGLE-3 (5-layer) 2.1-2.2x; >4.3x throughput on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.
papers.long_context_behavior: The only diffusion drafter with a published context-length curve (Table 4, LongBench): zero-shot acceptance decays 4.91-5.27 at 1K -> 3.93-5.17 at 4K -> 3.32-4.46 at 8K -> 2.67-3.61 at 16K -> 2.09 at 32K; light fine-tuning (1.6K LongAlign samples, 3 epochs) recovers to 3.81-6.05 at 16K and 3.56 at 32K. Nothing beyond 32K; per-block re-encoding cost vs context growth not analyzed.

papers.title: DeLS-Spec: Decoupled Long-Short Contexts for Parallel Speculative Drafting
papers.idea: Treats a frozen DFlash drafter as a long-context expert and adds an independently-trained lightweight local head as a short-context expert; combines their logits at inference — modular, no joint training with target or DFlash backbone.
papers.numbers: Consistent speedup and acceptance-length gains over DFlash on Qwen3 across math/code/dialogue (no single headline multiplier in abstract).
papers.long_context_behavior: Despite the long/short-context expert framing, evaluation is on standard math/code/dialogue benchmarks — the decomposition is about global (target-feature) vs local (recent-token) conditioning, not 32K+ inputs; long-input behavior untested.

papers.title: Fail Fast, Win Big: Rethinking the Drafting Strategy in Speculative Decoding via Diffusion LLMs (FailFast)
papers.idea: Off-the-shelf diffusion LLM as drafter without fine-tuning; since dLLM drafting cost is roughly independent of draft length, dynamically shortens drafts in hard regions and extends aggressively in easy ones.
papers.numbers: Up to 4.9x over AR, 1.7x over naive dLLM drafting, 1.7x faster than EAGLE-3; accepts up to 70 tokens in one round.
papers.long_context_behavior: Standard short-context benchmarks; the dLLM drafter's bidirectional attention over the full context makes its drafting cost grow quadratically with input length — exactly the regime never measured.

papers.title: SpecDiff-2: Scaling Diffusion Drafter Alignment for Faster Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Calibration techniques aligning a discrete-diffusion drafter's non-autoregressive distribution with the AR verifier, attacking both drafting parallelism and misalignment rejections.
papers.numbers: Up to +55% tokens/sec over previous SOTA baselines; up to 5.5x over standard decoding, lossless.
papers.long_context_behavior: Reasoning/coding/math benchmarks only; no drafter-KV or context-scaling analysis — diffusion drafter re-encodes block context per pass.

papers.title: Cascade Speculative Drafting for Even Faster LLM Inference
papers.idea: Two cascades: Vertical (each drafter's draft is reviewed by the next-larger model, bottoming out in a statistical/max-gram LM so no neural model ever decodes autoregressively) and Horizontal (larger drafters draft early high-value tokens, smaller ones draft the tail).
papers.numbers: Up to 81% additional speedup over standard speculative decoding while preserving the target distribution.
papers.long_context_behavior: Short-context only; every neural cascade level still carries its own full KV over the context, so the cascade's cost structure degrades with length — never re-evaluated in KV-bound regimes.

papers.title: Faster Cascades via Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Unifies model cascades (which defer only hard tokens for quality/cost) with speculative decoding (which verifies everything) via speculative cascading — a deferral rule decides token-by-token whether to accept the small model's output or defer to the large model, interpolating lossless and lossy operation.
papers.numbers: Better cost-quality tradeoffs than both plain cascades and plain speculative decoding on T5/PaLM-2 benchmark suites (gains reported as tradeoff curves, not one multiplier).
papers.long_context_behavior: No context-length axis; relevant as the theoretical bridge between lossless verification and RAPID-style quality-blurring speculation, which long-context sparse verification (Dustin/SpecPV) now needs.

papers.title: CAS-Spec: Cascade Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Builds a cascade of draft models on the fly from dynamically switchable acceleration strategies (layer sparsity, activation quantization) of the target itself; Dynamic Tree Cascade (DyTC) routes among levels and assigns draft lengths via acceptance-rate and latency heuristics.
papers.numbers: 1.1-2.3x over AR across LLMs/datasets; DyTC +47% avg speedup over cascade-based and +48% over tree-based baselines.
papers.long_context_behavior: No long-context discussion; self-drafters here attend over full KV, so every cascade level's drafting cost grows with context — untested where TriForce showed hierarchy matters most.

papers.title: Fast Inference via Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
papers.idea: Formalizes stacking drafters into a hierarchy where each model verifies the smaller one's proposals; derives a closed-form expected-latency expression for any hierarchy and a polynomial-time algorithm to select the latency-optimal stack.
papers.numbers: Up to 1.2x over the best single-draft baseline empirically; optimal hierarchy selection in polynomial time.
papers.long_context_behavior: The latency model has no context-length or KV-boundedness term — costs are treated as fixed per model, which is exactly what breaks at 128K where level costs become KV-load-dominated; extending this theory to length-dependent costs is open.

papers.title: Recurrent Drafter for Fast Speculative Decoding (ReDrafter)
papers.idea: Lightweight RNN drafter conditioned on the target's last hidden state with beam search plus dynamic tree attention to dedupe candidate prefixes; trained by distillation. The architectural ancestor of OWL's context-length-invariant LSTM drafter.
papers.numbers: Up to 2.8x on Vicuna MT-Bench (PyTorch, H100); 2.5x in TensorRT-LLM; 2.3x on Apple Silicon MLX.
papers.long_context_behavior: RNN drafter state is O(1) in context (conditions only on current hidden state + recurrent state) — inherently length-robust drafter memory — but was never evaluated on long-context inputs; OWL later showed this drafter shape is the right one for 8K-100K.

papers.title: OWL: Overcoming Window Length-Dependence in Speculative Decoding for Long-Context Inputs
papers.idea: LSTM drafter conditioned only on the final token's hidden state (zero drafter KV growth), a [SPEC] token enriching verifier representations, and hybrid model-based + SAM/n-gram drafting (HOWL); releases LongSpecBench (200 samples, 4K-64K inputs).
papers.numbers: On LongSpecBench: EAGLE-3 acceptance 1.28 (0.81x — a slowdown), PLD 2.75, Token Recycling 3.16, SAMD 3.18, SuffixDecoding 3.41, SAMD+TR 4.98; OWL 4.00 (Llama-3.1-8B) / 4.27 (Llama-3.3-70B, 2.35x speedup); HOWL 6.14 acceptance, 3.08x speedup.
papers.long_context_behavior: The definitive third-party measurement that model-free prompt-retrieval drafters (PLD/SAMD/SuffixDecoding, 2.75-3.41) all BEAT the trained EAGLE-3 head (1.28) on 4K-64K inputs, and that combining retrieval with an O(1)-state learned drafter (HOWL 6.14) is the current long-context acceptance frontier — but the benchmark stops at 64K.

evidence: OWL/LongSpecBench (arXiv 2510.07535): on 4K-64K-token inputs, EAGLE-3 acceptance length collapses to 1.28 (0.81x speed, i.e., slower than AR) while zero-KV model-free drafters hold up — PLD 2.75, Token Recycling 3.16, SAM-Decoding 3.18, SuffixDecoding 3.41, SAMD+TokenRecycling 4.98; OWL's O(1)-state LSTM drafter reaches 4.00/4.27 (2.35x on Llama-3.3-70B) and hybrid HOWL 6.14 acceptance / 3.08x.

Mamba Drafters (arXiv 2506.01206, EMNLP-F 2025): Mamba drafter keeps constant decoding memory while transformer-drafter KV grows linearly — peak memory 52GB vs EAGLE's 72GB at 8K; acceptance at 8K LongBench 2.80-2.87 vs Mistral-7B drafter 2.21 and EAGLE(+YaRN) 2.64; drafting ~3x faster than TriForce at 8K; maximum context evaluated is only 8K.

DFlash (arXiv 2602.06036) Table 4 — first context-length curve for a block-diffusion drafter: zero-shot acceptance decays 4.91-5.27 @1K -> 3.32-4.46 @8K -> 2.67-3.61 @16K -> 2.09 @32K; fine-tuning on 1.6K LongAlign samples for 3 epochs recovers 3.81-6.05 @16K and 3.56 @32K; headline 6.1x on Qwen3-8B, ~2.5x over EAGLE-3; no data beyond 32K.

SuffixDecoding (arXiv 2411.04975, NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight): suffix-tree drafter state costs ~10.75 bytes/token in CPU RAM (6.15GB for ~572M tokens; ~4us updates, ~12us lookups) vs megabytes-per-token GPU KV for model drafters; 5.3x on AgenticSQL, 2.5x on SWE-Bench, 2.8x faster than EAGLE-2/3, 1.9x over Token Recycling.

Token Recycling (arXiv 2408.08696): <2MB total drafter state (vocab-indexed adjacency matrix), strictly constant in context length, ~2x speedup across model sizes and +30% over prior train-free methods; third-party long-context acceptance 3.16 on 4K-64K (OWL).

Heterogeneous-vocabulary lossless SD (arXiv 2502.05202, ICML 2025 Oral): three provably lossless cross-tokenizer algorithms reach up to 2.8x over AR using off-the-shelf drafter/target pairs on summarization, programming, and long-context tasks — the only cross-vocab work touching long context, and it reports no acceptance-vs-length curve.

TokenTiming (arXiv 2510.15545, ACL 2026): DTW-based probability transfer across mismatched vocabularies gives 1.57x with any off-the-shelf pair; OmniDraft (arXiv 2507.02659, NeurIPS 2025) gets 1.5-2x with one 68M drafter serving Vicuna-7B/Qwen2-7B/Llama3-8B via an online n-gram translation cache — both short-context only.

DReSD (arXiv 2502.15572, ACL-F 2025): replacing exact suffix matching with dense (ANN, contextualized-embedding) retrieval yields +87% acceptance rate, +65% longer accepted spans, +19% faster generation vs sparse retrieval, up to 4.64x total — semantic retrieval drafting works, but only from an external datastore, never from the long prompt itself.

SpecLA (arXiv 2607.16673): speculative decoding on O(1)-state linear-attention targets (GDN-1.3B) tops out at 1.70x because tree verification must respect recurrent state dependencies — far below the 3-6x of transformer-target pipelines; Component-Aware Self-Spec (arXiv 2605.01106): parallel hybrids draft at alpha=0.68 vs alpha=0.038 for sequential hybrids (18x gap).

Cascade/hierarchical line: Cascade Speculative Drafting (arXiv 2312.11462, NeurIPS 2024) +81% over standard SD via vertical+horizontal cascades ending in a statistical LM; CAS-Spec (arXiv 2510.26843, NeurIPS 2025) 1.1-2.3x with Dynamic Tree Cascade +47%/+48% over cascade/tree baselines; Hierarchical SD theory (arXiv 2510.19705) selects the latency-optimal drafter hierarchy in polynomial time but yields only ~1.2x over best single drafter and models no context-length dependence.

ReDrafter (arXiv 2403.09919, Apple): RNN drafter conditioned on the target's last hidden state — O(1) drafter state — reaches 2.8x (PyTorch H100), 2.5x (TensorRT-LLM), 2.3x (MLX/Apple Silicon); NEST (arXiv 2405.19325, NeurIPS 2024): lossy retrieval-span speculation gives 1.8x on Llama-2-Chat-70B while improving attribution.

Absence evidence (searched Aug 2026): no published paper uses an RWKV or hybrid attention+SSM model as a drafter for a transformer target; no SSM/linear-attention drafter evaluation exists beyond 8K context; no cross-tokenizer speculation evaluation reports acceptance vs context length; no alternative-drafter family (retrieval, SSM, diffusion, cascade) has any published 128K+ acceptance curve — TriForce's 2024 sparse-KV self-drafting result at 128K remains the only 128K datapoint in the literature.

gaps.gap: SSM/linear-attention drafters have never been measured beyond 8K context — the regime where their O(1) state should pay off most. No acceptance-vs-context curve exists for a Mamba/GDN/RWKV drafter at 32K/128K/1M against a long-context transformer target, and no serving stack (vLLM/SGLang) has a recurrent-drafter path.
gaps.why_open: Mamba Drafters stops at LongBench 8K (acceptance 2.80 at 8K); the core scientific question — whether a fixed-size recurrent state can compress a 128K prompt well enough to keep alpha useful, i.e., the acceptance-vs-state-capacity curve — is unmeasured; and hybrid long-context targets change the cost model (Component-Aware shows sequential hybrids draft at alpha=0.038). TriForce/MagicDec don't cover this: they use the target itself with sparse KV, not an O(1)-state external drafter.
gaps.closest_work: Mamba Drafters for Speculative Decoding (2506.01206, 8K max); OWL (2510.07535) has an O(1)-state LSTM drafter but conditions on target hidden state and stops at 64K; ReDrafter (2403.09919) is the O(1)-state ancestor with zero long-context data.

gaps.gap: Cross-tokenizer/universal speculation has no context-length axis: nobody reports acceptance or re-tokenization drift vs input length for heterogeneous-vocabulary drafting, even though the natural long-context use case is pairing a strong small model from another family with a 1M-context target.
gaps.why_open: Token-boundary misalignment compounds over long accepted spans (string-level verification must re-tokenize growing text), and long grounded contexts produce exactly the long copied spans where alignment algorithms (exact-match, DTW) are most stressed; the ICML 2025 oral includes 'long-context tasks' in its 2.8x headline but publishes no per-length breakdown, and TokenTiming/OmniDraft are short-context on-device settings.
gaps.closest_work: Lossless SD for Heterogeneous Vocabularies (2502.05202, ICML 2025 Oral); TokenTiming (2510.15545, ACL 2026); OmniDraft (2507.02659, NeurIPS 2025).

gaps.gap: Prompt-retrieval drafting (PLD/SAM/suffix-tree) is unmeasured past 64K, and there is no principled per-step router between retrieval drafting and model drafting with an acceptance model as a function of context length, match position, and task groundedness — despite retrieval drafters being the only family that IMPROVES with more copyable context at zero GPU state.
gaps.why_open: OWL's LongSpecBench (the only third-party long-context comparison) tops out at 64K, where retrieval drafters already beat EAGLE-3 (3.18-4.98 vs 1.28 acceptance); at 128K-1M, match-search quality, suffix-automaton memory locality, and the retrieval-vs-model tradeoff are all unquantified, and existing hybrids (HOWL, SAM-Decoding's switching, AdaPLD) use static heuristics, not a policy derived from an acceptance model. Dense (semantic) retrieval drafting from the prompt itself — DReSD's mechanism applied to the 128K context instead of an external corpus — has never been tried.
gaps.closest_work: OWL/HOWL + LongSpecBench (2510.07535, 6.14 acceptance at <=64K); SAM-Decoding (2411.10666); SuffixDecoding (2411.04975); DReSD (2502.15572, external-corpus only).

gaps.gap: Block-diffusion drafters are uncharacterized beyond 32K, and their per-block context re-encoding economics are unanalyzed: DFlash-style KV-injection of target features avoids drafter prefill, but nobody has measured how per-block drafting cost, feature-injection bandwidth, and acceptance scale from 32K to 128K+, nor whether diffusion drafting composes with sparse target attention.
gaps.why_open: DFlash's own Table 4 (the only data) shows zero-shot acceptance falling 5.2 -> 2.09 from 1K to 32K, patched by 1.6K-sample fine-tuning to 3.56 at 32K — a band-aid whose scaling to 128K is unknown; FailFast's off-the-shelf dLLM drafter pays bidirectional attention over the full prompt (quadratic in input length), and DeLS-Spec's 'long-context expert' framing was never actually tested on long inputs.

gaps.gap: Cascade/hierarchy theory has no length-dependent cost model: the polynomial-time optimal-hierarchy result and all cascade systems (CS-Drafting, CAS-Spec) assume fixed per-model costs, but at 128K+ every level's cost is dominated by KV loading that scales with context and differs by drafter type (O(1)-state RNN/SSM, O(n)-CPU suffix tree, sparse-KV self-draft) — so the latency-optimal hierarchy at 4K is provably not the one at 128K, and nobody can compute the right one.
gaps.why_open: TriForce's 128K two-level hierarchy was hand-designed in 2024 and never generalized; extending Mohri et al.'s expected-latency expression to costs c_i(L, batch, KV-budget) and heterogeneous drafter families requires acceptance-vs-length models that don't exist (the theory-has-no-context-axis problem instantiated at the hierarchy level).
gaps.closest_work: Fast Inference via Hierarchical Speculative Decoding (2510.19705); TriForce (2404.11912); CAS-Spec (2510.26843); MagicDec's analytical model (batch/length-aware but single-level).

gaps.gap: Drafting FOR long-context O(1)-state and hybrid targets is unsolved: linear-attention targets cap at 1.70x (vs 3-6x for transformers) because tree verification must respect recurrence, and sequential hybrids — the dominant 2026 long-context architecture — have no viable drafter at all (alpha=0.038 self-spec); no work combines an O(1)-state target with any alternative drafter family (retrieval, diffusion, cascade) at long context, where the KV-bound argument for speculation (MagicDec) no longer applies and a new speedup rationale is needed.
gaps.why_open: The entire speculative-decoding economics literature assumes verification is KV-load-bound, which is false for O(1)-state targets — so what makes speculation profitable there (pure FLOP parallelism vs state-recovery cost) must be re-derived; SpecLA's compact-factor state recovery is a first step but scales poorly to trees, and nobody has evaluated any of it at 128K contexts where these architectures are actually deployed.
gaps.closest_work: SpecLA (2607.16673, 1.70x on GDN-1.3B); Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding (2605.01106); The Mamba in the Llama (2408.15237, hardware-aware multi-step speculation for hybrids).

claims.claim: H1: Long-context speculative decoding is fundamentally limited by KV-cache memory/bandwidth.
claims.strongest_evidence_for: For MHA/GQA transformers the decode step is KV-bandwidth bound and the gap widens with context: VeriCache (arXiv 2605.17613, verified) anchors Llama-3.1-8B-1M at 5ms/step @5K (~0.6GB KV) vs 25ms @500K (~60GB KV); MagicDec (ICLR 2025, arXiv 2408.11049, verified) gives the analytical (batch, seqlen) model showing both draft and target become KV-loading dominated; TriForce (COLM 2024, arXiv 2404.11912) built its whole hierarchical design on the target-KV bottleneck at 128K. GQA already measurably weakens speculation gains because it lightens KV: MagicDec-part2 (infini-ai-lab.github.io/MagicDec-part2, verified) reports self-speculation at 32K/batch-128 on 8xA100 of 1.63x for MHA Llama-2-7B vs 1.47x for GQA Llama-3.1-8B, with critical sequence length explicitly higher for GQA — i.e., the KV footprint really is the control variable.
claims.strongest_evidence_against: The claim inverts the sign and overstates universality. (a) KV memory-boundedness is the OPPORTUNITY, not the limit: MagicDec shows speedup INCREASES with batch and context beyond S_inflection (~4K for 8B on 8xA100), up to 2.51x at batch 32-256 (verified); QuantSpec (ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.10424, verified) speedup GROWS with context 1.35x@4K -> 2.49x@128K; SpecPV (arXiv 2512.02337, verified) 2.88x@10K -> 6.29x@60K. The regime the hypothesis calls 'fundamentally limited' is where speculation pays best. (b) The premise is architecture-contingent, not fundamental: MLA arithmetic intensity is >2 orders of magnitude above MHA, moving decode attention toward compute-bound (arXiv 2507.15465, verified: 'over two orders of magnitude higher... toward a compute-bound regime'); GLA kernels are 2x faster than FlashMLA specifically at query length >1 (arXiv 2505.21487); DeepSeek-V3's MLA+MTP runs 85-90% second-token acceptance and ~1.8x TPS in 128K production (arXiv 2412.19437). (c) The binding ceiling at high acceptance is informational, not memory: E[accepted/iter] <= (mu+mu_2)log(P)/mu^2 + O(1), logarithmic in verifier capacity, empirically tight vs EAGLE-3 (arXiv 2512.11718, EACL 2026, verified). (d) At production load the limiter becomes scheduling/verification compute, not KV: Meta 1.4-2.0x at production batch vs 2-3x at bs=1 (arXiv 2508.08192); EAGLE 3.1 on GB200 decays 2.03x (c=1) -> 1.66x (c=16) (vllm blog 2026-05-26).

claims.claim: H2: An additional independent drafter model makes long-context speculation WORSE, because the drafter's own KV cache also grows with context.
claims.strongest_evidence_for: Steelman: naive independent transformer drafters do fail at long context, and drafter state does cost real memory/scheduler budget. OWL/LongSpecBench (arXiv 2510.07535, verified): EAGLE-3 acceptance length collapses to 1.28 and generation runs at 0.81x — slower than plain AR — on 4K-64K inputs. SpecExtend (arXiv 2505.20776): vanilla SD mean accepted length drops to ~0.5-0.6 tokens at 16K. BudgetDraft (arXiv 2606.00144, verified): llama-68m sparse-KV drafter acceptance collapses from 55.4% @4K to ~0% @8-16K. Mamba Drafters (arXiv 2506.01206, verified paper): transformer-drafter KV grows linearly — EAGLE peaks at 72GB vs 52GB at 8K. TransKV (TechRxiv 2026): uncommitted draft tokens consume block-granular KV pages and count against vLLM token budgets, capping SD gains at high load. So the failure mode H2 describes exists — for full-attention drafters trained short.
claims.strongest_evidence_against: The causal premise ('drafter KV grows with context') is false for entire drafter classes, and the conclusion is false even for some growing-KV drafters. (a) Constant-KV independent drafting is exactly how MagicDec (verified) achieves speedup that GROWS with batch and context — StreamingLLM/SnapKV-cache drafters, up to 2.51x for Llama-3.1-8B at batch 32-256; StreamingLLM-512 acceptance degrades only 0.84@4K -> 0.79@100K. (b) LongSpec (ACL 2025, arXiv 2502.17421, verified): constant-sized drafter KV (512-token window + cross-attention into the TARGET's cache, zero duplicated long-context storage), up to 3.26x. (c) O(1)-state non-transformer drafters: OWL's LSTM drafter 2.35x on Llama-3.3-70B with acceptance 4.00-4.27 where EAGLE-3 gets 1.28; Mamba drafters hold acceptance 2.80-2.87 at 8K vs EAGLE+YaRN 2.64 with constant decoding memory; ReDrafter RNN (arXiv 2403.09919) 2.3-2.8x. (d) Zero-KV model-free drafters: SuffixDecoding (NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight, arXiv 2411.04975) ~10.75 bytes/token in CPU RAM, 2.8x faster than EAGLE-2/3; Token Recycling <2MB total state, acceptance 3.16 on 4K-64K. (e) Even a LARGER independent drafter helps at 120K: RAPID (ICML 2025 Spotlight, arXiv 2502.20330, verified) RAG drafter on <=1/24 of the input reaches 75-85% acceptance, 2.10x (8B) / 2.69x (70B target) — and upward speculation IMPROVES quality (InfiniteBench 42.83 -> 49.98). The real long-context failure driver for independent drafters is acceptance/distribution mismatch (OWL, BudgetDraft), not drafter KV growth — H2 gets the mechanism wrong and the direction wrong.

claims.claim: H3: The only viable directions are self-speculation, early exit, and sparse-attention drafting, or a combination of them.
claims.strongest_evidence_for: Steelman: everything actually measured at 96K-128K+ IS self-speculation over sparse/compressed target KV. TriForce 2.31x@122K (A100) with acceptance 0.9649-0.9878 at a 4K retrieval budget; QuantSpec (verified) 2.49x@128K with >90% acceptance via shared hierarchical INT4/INT8 KV; Vegas (ICML 2026, arXiv 2602.07223, verified) 1.25-2.81x over vLLM on 96K-120K LongBench-v2 requests via verification-guided sparse drafting; SpecPV (verified) 6.29x@60K; SparseSpec/PillarAttn (MLSys 2026, arXiv 2512.01278, verified) 2.13x at batch up to 256 where EAGLE-3 and n-gram accept <2 of 8 tokens; VeriCache (verified) up to 4x bit-identical via compressed-KV self-drafting. Meanwhile learned independent draft heads collapse (OWL: EAGLE-3 at 0.81x), and no alternative-drafter family (retrieval, SSM, diffusion, cascade, cross-tokenizer) has ANY published 128K+ acceptance curve as of Aug 2026 — TriForce-style sparse-KV self-drafting remains the only 128K datapoint family.
claims.strongest_evidence_against: 'Only' fails on at least four published counterexamples outside the H3 triad, and one member of the triad (early exit) is the LEAST supported direction at long context. (a) Retrieval/suffix/n-gram drafting with zero or O(1) state: SuffixDecoding 5.3x on AgenticSQL, 2.8x over EAGLE-2/3; OWL's model-free baselines hold 2.75-3.41 acceptance on 4K-64K inputs and hybrid HOWL reaches 6.14 acceptance / 3.08x — none is self-speculation, early exit, or sparse-attention drafting. (b) RAG drafting: RAPID (verified) 2.10-2.69x at 120K with an independent (even larger) drafter. (c) Block-diffusion drafting: DFlash (ICML 2026, arXiv 2602.06036, verified) >6x lossless, up to 2.5x over EAGLE-3, with a context curve — zero-shot acceptance decays to 2.09@32K but 1.6K LongAlign fine-tuning samples recover 3.56@32K. (d) O(1)-state SSM/RNN drafters (Mamba drafters, ReDrafter, OWL-LSTM). (e) Compressed-KV drafting (QuantSpec, VeriCache) is compression, not sparsity — QuantSpec explicitly finds quantized drafter KV beats sparse drafter KV on draft-target agreement. Conversely, early exit — which H3 includes — has NO long-context evidence at all: every layer-skip/early-exit result is <4K-16K (LayerSkip 2.16x, SWIFT 1.3-1.6x, CLaSp 1.24-1.73x, KnapSpec peaks at 1.47x and stops at 16K inputs), so H3 simultaneously excludes directions proven at 64-120K and includes one proven nowhere beyond 16K. Corrected claim that survives: at >=96K, published wins come from drafting against the target's own (sparse, compressed, or retrieved) state rather than from short-trained independent transformer drafters — but that class includes retrieval, RAG, diffusion, and O(1)-state drafters that H3's 'only' excludes.

claims.claim: Hidden assumption: draft-token acceptance rates hold up (or fail) uniformly as context grows to 32K-1M.
claims.strongest_evidence_for: Acceptance is length-robust when the draft state is a lossless-ish view of the target's own state: QuantSpec (verified) acceptance is flat-to-rising with context — 91.64%@16K, 90.99%@32K, 92.18%@64K, 94.31%@128K; TriForce retrieval-cache acceptance 0.9649 (PG-19) / 0.9878 (needle) at 120K; MagicDec StreamingLLM-512 only 0.84@4K -> 0.79@100K; VeriCache sustains 25-40 accepted tokens/round at 4x KV compaction; SparseSpec-L (arXiv 2607.27735, verified) 52-84.6% acceptance up to 64K because dense KV is never discarded, making importance-estimation errors recoverable.
claims.strongest_evidence_against: Acceptance collapses catastrophically for other draft-state constructions, so no uniform law exists: BudgetDraft (verified) naive sparse-KV drafting falls 55.4%@4K -> 0.3%@8K -> ~0.1-0.5%@16K, and even multi-view training recovers only ~18%@16K — budget-robust but not length-robust; TriForce shows eviction-based caches (StreamingLLM 0.0519, H2O 0.0739 acceptance on 120K needle retrieval) collapse where retrieval caches (0.9878) do not; OWL (verified) shows short-trained EAGLE-3 heads collapse to acceptance length 1.28 (0.81x, slower than AR) on long inputs; DFlash zero-shot diffusion drafting decays 4.91-5.27@1K -> 2.09@32K; LongSpec's own authors report degradation at 25-32K; TriForce acceptance also drops with temperature (~0.29 per-token at T=1.0) and retrieval-cache staleness grows with generation length. Caveat on the one 'flat acceptance' counter-anecdote: the MiniMax-M3 EAGLE-3 blog (huggingface.co/blog/lujangusface/tw-eagle3-minimax) exists but the fetched content contains no acceptance-vs-prompt-length table, so the 'AL 2.64@1K vs 2.63@32K' figure could not be re-verified and should not be load-bearing. Net finding: acceptance-vs-context is a property of how the draft state is built — shared/quantized/attention-retrieved target state holds to 128K; evicted, budget-mismatched, or short-context-trained draft states collapse by 8-32K — and NOTHING in any family has a published acceptance curve at 256K-1M (VeriCache targets the regime architecturally but reports no 1M evaluation; DeepSeek-V3 serves 128K with no published acceptance-vs-length breakdown).

gaps.gap: 1. Acceptance-vs-context curve for layer-skip/early-exit self-drafting beyond ~16K; LayerSkip-style training for 128K-context models
gaps.closest_work: KnapSpec (arXiv 2602.20217, ICML 2026, github.com/kaist-flexml-lab/knapspec) remains the frontier: context-dependent attention/MLP latency modeling, up to 1.47x on Qwen3/Llama3, evaluation confirmed to span only 'context lengths up to 32K' (input ~16K). New negative evidence: 'The Diminishing Returns of Early-Exit Decoding in Modern LLMs' (arXiv 2603.23701) shows newer pretraining recipes reduce layer redundancy (dense > MoE/SSM for early exit; 20B+ and base models exit best) but does NOT evaluate 32K+ contexts. ConfLayers (2604.14612) and DEL (2504.05598, 2.16-2.62x) stay short-context. LayerSkip (2404.16710) checkpoints remain Llama2/Llama3/CodeLlama short-context only — no 128K-context LayerSkip-recipe checkpoint found anywhere (HF blog, facebookresearch/LayerSkip repo, 2026 search).
gaps.remaining_delta: Still fully novel: (a) measured acceptance/hidden-state-fidelity curves for any layer-skip or early-exit self-drafter at 64K-1M input; (b) connecting AdaSkip-style (2501.02336) long-context sublayer-importance redistribution to draft acceptance; (c) any layer-dropout+early-exit-loss training run on a 128K model. 2603.23701 adds a caveat to motivation: layer redundancy is shrinking in modern checkpoints, so the paper should measure on 2025-26 architectures, not Llama2.

gaps.gap: 2. Composing layer-subset drafting with per-layer KV-subset drafting (2D sublayer x KV-budget knapsack)
gaps.closest_work: No composition found in any 2025-26 search. The two axes remain siloed: KnapSpec (2602.20217) = layer axis with full KV per retained layer; Vegas (ICML 2026 poster, verification-guided sparse attention, icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/60880), SparseSpec/PillarAttn (2512.01278, up to 2.13x throughput), SparseSpec-L ('A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole', arXiv 2607.27735, up to 2.79x, all-layers sparse-KV recallable drafting + entropy-based speculation-length control) = KV axis with all layers. QuantSpec (2502.10424) = KV-precision axis, all layers. S3D (2405.20314) = layer axis + multi-token, no KV sparsity. DFlash/Spec-V2 (LMSYS blog 2026-06-15) injects target hidden states into a small draft's KV — a different decomposition, not sublayer x KV-budget selection inside the target.
gaps.remaining_delta: Entire gap intact: joint (layers x KV-budget) drafter with a coupled acceptance/latency model, including the feedback loop that skipping layers changes the attention distributions used for KV selection. KnapSpec's DP machinery plus Vegas/PillarAttn's free verification-attention signal are the ready-made ingredients; nobody has built the 2D knapsack.

gaps.gap: 3. Error-accumulation control / adaptive full-verification triggering for partial (sparse-KV) verification in self-speculation
gaps.closest_work: SpecPV (2512.02337) is still the only method that measures and admits error accumulation (periodic full verification to flush errors; the GovReport ROUGE-L 56.1 vs 77.3 cliff). New: 'Revisiting Lossy Verification in Speculative Decoding: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Failure Modes' (arXiv 2607.26627, July 2026, Fast-HSD repo) — taxonomy of truncation-based vs collaborative lossy verification and their distributional-distortion failure modes, but no KV-sparsity axis, no divergence bounds, no adaptive full-verify trigger. Dustin (2606.24957) improves the sparse-verification signal (draft-lookahead + target-historical attention, maximizing Attention Recovery Rate) but keeps fixed heuristics. When Is a Draft Accepted (2606.30265) unchanged: certificates without KV-budget axis.
gaps.remaining_delta: Unclaimed: an online divergence estimator from verification-side statistics (e.g., captured attention mass) that triggers full verification adaptively, plus any bound linking verification KV budget to output divergence with refresh-interval dependence. 2607.26627 strengthens motivation by documenting failure modes without offering control.

gaps.gap: 4. Self-speculation for sequential hybrid / SSM-bearing targets: training recipe + shared-state rollback
gaps.closest_work: The rollback-engineering sub-problem is being solved in serving stacks: ReplaySSM (vLLM RFC #47572, SGLang RFC #28511, 2026) caches recent SSM layer INPUTS instead of checkpointing state — rollback becomes an O(1) ring-buffer pointer move vs O(T), eliminating per-draft-token state storage for Mamba2/GDN, targeted at standard and speculative decode (Qwen GDN/KDA-class hybrids). vLLM/llama.cpp already run MTP spec decode on hybrid SSM targets (NemotronH — vllm#39809 crash reports; Qwen3.5-MoE hybrid fix llama.cpp#20075), so hybrids + external/MTP drafting is production reality with active bugfixing. SpecMamba (2509.19873) has FPGA-side memory-aware hybrid backtracking. Component-Aware Self-Spec (2605.01106) still holds the diagnosis: alpha=0.68 (parallel hybrids, k=2 greedy) vs alpha=0.038 (sequential), an 18x gap.
gaps.remaining_delta: Still novel: (a) LayerSkip-style layer-dropout + early-exit-loss training applied to any hybrid checkpoint (nothing found); (b) self-speculation semantics where drafter and target share the recurrent state (ReplaySSM handles rejection rollback for a separate draft path, not a shared-state self-drafter); (c) characterizing checkpoint/replay overhead at 100K contexts inside a self-spec loop. Cite ReplaySSM as concurrent infrastructure, not as the answer.

gaps.gap: 5. Layer-skip/early-exit self-speculation under continuous batching (batch 32+, vLLM/SGLang)
gaps.closest_work: Nothing found that batches heterogeneous skip-sets. 'Batch Speculative Decoding Done Right' (2510.22876) fixes ragged-tensor correctness for standard batched drafters only. SparseSpec (2512.01278) remains the only serving-grade self-spec (unified draft/verify scheduler, delayed verification, dynamic KV management, up to 2.13x throughput) and stays uniform-depth sparse-KV precisely to keep kernels homogeneous. P-EAGLE (vLLM blog 2026-03-13, in vLLM v0.16.0 PR#32887, 1.69x over EAGLE-3 on B200) and EAGLE-3.1 (vLLM blog 2026-05-26) show serving integration only for draft-head methods. Nightjar (2512.22420) and FASER (2604.20503) adapt speculation length per batch/request but with fixed drafters. All layer-skip works (SWIFT 2410.06916, CLaSp 2505.24196 ACL 2025 1.3-1.7x, DEL, ConfLayers, KnapSpec) remain batch-1.
gaps.remaining_delta: Entire gap intact: shared-skip-set vs skip-set-grouped batching trade-off unquantified; no vLLM/SGLang layer-skip self-spec integration; no batch-32+ measurement. SparseSpec's design choice is citable evidence the community routed around it.

gaps.gap: 6. Principled draft-path adaptation under acceptance drift over 30K-100K-token generations (regret/drift guarantees)
gaps.closest_work: The regret machinery now exists, but not for path selection at long generation: BanditSpec (ICML 2025, 2505.15141) — UCBSpec/EXP3Spec with stopping-time regret bounds for training-free hyperparameter/drafter choice; 'Not-a-Bandit' (2510.20064) — provably no-regret drafter selection; OnlineSpec 'When Drafts Evolve' (2603.12617) — dynamic-regret-grounded online drafter evolution with a formal link between regret and acceleration, up to 24% over static SD; Nightjar (2512.22420) — contextual-bandit speculation length under serving drift; DEL (2504.05598) — online per-layer acceptance tracking for exit-layer+gamma, heuristic, short-context. All evaluated on short benchmarks; none select layer-subsets/KV budgets; none run on 30K-100K reasoning traces.
gaps.remaining_delta: Novel remainder: applying no-regret/drift-aware selection to the combinatorial self-spec draft path (skip set / exit depth / KV budget) with non-stationarity induced by the model's own generation, evaluated on long-CoT (TokenSwift-regime lengths). Framing must position against BanditSpec/OnlineSpec explicitly — 'no regret guarantee exists' is no longer true generically, only for path selection.

gaps.gap: 7. Budget-growth law B(L) for sparse-KV drafters, 128K-1M
gaps.closest_work: Windowed-MTP (arXiv 2607.21535, July 2026) breaks the 128K evaluation ceiling: StreamingLLM-style sink+sliding-window on the DRAFT attention only, lossless full-attention verification, evaluated to 1M tokens on a single GPU via SGLang on Qwen GDN-MoE 35B/122B and Mamba2-hybrid NoPE 120B; drops ~99% of draft KV at 1M at matched acceptance, +28-44% per-step draft-cost reduction (draft KV was 7.7-11% of total KV at 1M). This is a existence proof that a constant local window suffices at 1M for MTP-style drafters. Otherwise unchanged: TriForce (4K budget plateau at 120K), Vegas (7% at 96-120K, warns fixed budgets fail at extreme scale), BudgetDraft (2606.00144, budget x length table to 16K), SparseSpec-L (2607.27735, 64K hardware cap).
gaps.remaining_delta: Still novel: acceptance-vs-(budget, length) SURFACES for retrieval/verification-recycled sparse drafters (not window-local MTP heads) at 256K-1M, and reconciling Windowed-MTP's 'constant window suffices' with Vegas's 'budget must grow' — likely task- and drafter-family-dependent. A B(L) law paper must now include Windowed-MTP as a baseline/counterpoint.

gaps.gap: 8. Length-robust TRAINED sparse-KV drafting past 16-32K (multi-budget training x long-position schemes)
gaps.closest_work: BudgetDraft (2606.00144) unchanged: multi-view budget training holds acceptance across budgets (91.6% at 4K for B=256-2048) but collapses 91.6->75->18% at 4K->8K->16K ('16K collapse', speedup <=1x). LongSpec now ACL 2026 (aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.83, arXiv 2502.17421v4) with anchor-offset random offsets 0-15K/0-30K — architectural length robustness, no budget-adaptive sparse training. New adjacent: 'Attention Drift' (2605.09992) diagnoses drafter attention shifting off the prompt with chain depth and fixes it with post-norm/RMSNorm on drafter states (1.18x on long-context tasks, generalizes shorter train-time depths to longer draft chains) — but this addresses chain-depth drift in hidden-state drafters, not context-length collapse of sparse-KV drafters.
gaps.remaining_delta: Intact: no work combines multi-budget sparse-view training with long-context position schemes and evaluates at 64K+. Attention Drift's normalization fixes are a plausible ingredient to cite/compose, not a solution.

gaps.gap: 9. Staleness/refresh policy for verification-recycled importance signals over 10K+ generated tokens
gaps.closest_work: No acceptance-aware refresh controller found. SparseSpec-L (2607.27735) refreshes per-head sparse indices from each full-context verification pass and adds an entropy-based speculation-LENGTH controller (controls gamma, not refresh economics; generation capped ~128 tokens). SparseSpec/PillarAttn (2512.01278) keeps fixed k=8 refresh on ~13K-token CoT with no refresh-vs-acceptance ablation published. SpecExtend (4-8 steps) and TriForce (2404.11912, original staleness observation) unchanged. Dustin (2606.24957) blends draft-lookahead with historical target attention — implicitly mitigates staleness but never measures decay.
gaps.remaining_delta: Intact: measure acceptance decay of stale indices over 10K+ generated tokens, and build a controller that refreshes when predicted acceptance loss exceeds gather cost. Dustin's lookahead signal and SparseSpec-L's entropy statistics are available estimator ingredients.

gaps.gap: 10. Divergence certification for sparse verification (KV-budget -> output-distribution bound)
gaps.closest_work: When Is a Draft Accepted (2606.30265) still the only theory, still no KV-sparsity axis. 'Revisiting Lossy Verification' (2607.26627, July 2026) is the closest new work: empirically characterizes distributional distortion of truncation-based lossy verification and overshoot control for collaborative verification, but it is a mechanisms/failure-modes study of RELAXED ACCEPTANCE criteria — no formal bounds, no modeling of target-under-sparse-KV as a perturbed distribution. SpecPV (2512.02337) remains the only quantified failure case on the KV axis; SSV/SpecSA (2605.19893) verifies sparsely only against natively-sparse NSA targets (3.49x over AR-NSA, 6.86x kernel, H100) where sparse IS the reference distribution — sidestepping certification. VeriCache (2605.17613) sidesteps via off-GPU exact verification.
gaps.remaining_delta: Intact and strengthened: per-token KL/TV certificates as a function of KV budget / dropped attention mass, composed with 2606.30265-style acceptance regions. 2607.26627 provides the empirical failure taxonomy such a theory should explain.

gaps.gap: 11. Composing verification-recycled sparse drafting with sparse verification (oracle circularity)
