gaps.closest_work: Dustin (2606.24957) partially breaks the circularity in the external-drafter setting: its sparse-verification importance signal fuses DRAFT-side lookahead attention with target-historical attention, showing a usable importance oracle exists without full-KV verification attention. SSV/SpecSA (2605.19893) composes speculation with sparse verification but on natively-sparse NSA targets (trained-sparse reference — different contract). No paper composes a verification-recycled sparse self-drafter (Vegas ICML 2026 / PillarAttn 2512.01278 / SparseSpec-L 2607.27735) with sparse verification (Dustin/SpecPV/2512.21911); SparseSpec-L explicitly retains full-KV verification, and SpecPV's periodic full refresh remains the only crude mechanism in the self-spec family.
gaps.remaining_delta: The self-speculative both-sides-sparse system is unbuilt: recycling SPARSE-verification attention (plus recall of dropped-but-relevant tokens without a third scoring pass) for drafting, with measured interaction of the two speedups (each side's 2-9x is still measured in isolation). Dustin's lookahead-fusion idea imported into self-spec is the obvious but untried route.

gaps.gap: 12. Online controller for (drafter KV budget x speculation length) across (batch, context, load)
gaps.closest_work: The gamma axis is now well covered: Nightjar (2512.22420, J. Systems Architecture 2026) — contextual bandit choosing speculative length per batch size under dynamic serving load; FASER (2604.20503) — per-request runtime gamma for arriving and in-flight requests; SpecKV (2605.02888) — per-step gamma from draft entropy/confidence (MLP predictor, 0.34ms/decision, +56% over fixed gamma=4, correlation ~0.56 between draft signals and acceptance), and notably establishes compression level and optimal gamma are coupled (though on WEIGHT quant FP16/INT8/NF4). SmartSpec/goodput (2406.14066) and MagicDec (2408.11049) unchanged. No system touches the drafter KV budget at runtime: Vegas fixes sparsity per run, SparseSpec's scheduler is budget-blind, BudgetDraft never deploys its budget robustness.
gaps.remaining_delta: The KV-budget control axis is untouched: an alpha(task, L, B) predictor and a joint (B, gamma) per-request policy under memory pressure. SpecKV's finding that compression shifts optimal gamma is direct evidence the joint problem is real; a paper must position as adding the budget dimension to Nightjar/FASER/SpecKV rather than inventing per-request adaptation.

gaps.gap: 13. Measured acceptance of standard drafters (EAGLE/MTP) against KV-quantized/evicted targets (FP8-KV + EAGLE-3 production config)
gaps.closest_work: Verified absence as of Aug 2026. SpecKV (2605.02888): weight quant only (FP16/INT8/NF4), confirmed. vLLM+AMD Quark EAGLE-3 blog (vllm.ai/blog/2026-07-13-eagle-3-amd-instinct): measures acceptance length (AL 2.77 avg on SPEED-Bench for MiniMax-M3; Kimi-K2.5 with MXFP4 target weights + BF16/FP8 draft) — explicitly no KV-quantization acceptance data. EAGLE-3.1 (vLLM blog 2026-05-26) and P-EAGLE (2026-03-13): no KV-quant acceptance section. Only sources for the interaction remain grey literature: dev.to KV-quant post (0.3-1.5 accepted-tokens/cycle drop claim, uncited; 'known good config' Llama-3.3-70B FP8 target + EAGLE-3 BF16 draft + FP8 KV) and vLLM issue anecdotes. VeriCache (2605.17613) measures compressed-vs-full divergence only with compressed KV as drafter.
gaps.remaining_delta: Fully open and cheap to execute: systematic acceptance/AL measurement of EAGLE-3/MTP vs target KV precision (FP8/INT8/INT4 K and V, per-axis schemes) x context length x task, including double-lossy compounding (drafter trained on BF16 features vs FP8-KV verification) and the 'lossless relative to the wrong distribution' contract question. Weight-quant acceptance (SpecKV, AMD MXFP4 blogs) is the only adjacent data.

gaps.gap: 14. (Compression-ratio x context-length x acceptance) scaling law for drafter-KV compression; nothing past 128K
gaps.closest_work: Two corrections to the gap premise: (a) QuantSpec (2502.10424, SqueezeAILab) benchmarks 4K-128K at batch 1 (not ~32K as stated), still one fixed hierarchical 4-bit setting with >90% acceptance and up to ~2.5x; (b) Windowed-MTP (2607.21535) now provides a 1M-context point on the draft-KV-budget axis (~99% draft KV dropped at matched acceptance, +28-44% draft-cost reduction, SGLang single GPU) — so 'nothing past 128K' is false as of July 2026. Still no swept surface: nobody varies bits/budget against length to fit a law or extend MagicDec's (batch, seqlen) model with a compression axis. BudgetDraft (16K), VeriCache (one 4x ratio at ~100K), Lynx (2607.01831, progressive speculative quantization but for KV TRANSFER in disaggregated serving) unchanged.
gaps.remaining_delta: The law itself remains novel: a (bits/budget) x (4K-1M) x acceptance surface across quantized (QuantSpec-style) vs sparse (BudgetDraft/window-style) drafter compression, unified with MagicDec's analytical model to choose drafter KV precision/budget from (batch, context, HBM). Must incorporate Windowed-MTP and QuantSpec-128K as anchor points.

analyses.topic: 1. KV footprint: target vs 1-2B drafter, and when drafter KV is material (H2)
analyses.math: KV bytes/token = 2(K,V) x layers x kv_heads x head_dim x 2B(fp16). Qwen3-32B (64L, 8KVh, 128d, verified from HF config.json): 256KB/tok -> 8.6/34.4/137.4/274.9 GB at 32K/128K/512K/1M. Llama-3.1-8B (32L,8KVh,128d): 128KB/tok -> 4.3/17.2/68.7/137.4 GB (matches VeriCache anchor ~60GB@500K). DeepSeek-V3 MLA (61L, 576-elem latent): 69KB/tok -> 2.3/9.2/36.8/73.7 GB. Drafters: Qwen3-1.7B AND Qwen3-0.6B both have 28L x 8KVh x 128d = 112KB/tok -> 15.0 GB/req at 128K, 120.3 GB at 1M = 44% of the 32B target's KV, invariant to drafter parameter count because GQA floors kv_heads at 8. Llama-3.2-1B (16L,8KVh,64d): 32KB/tok = 25% of Llama-8B. Capacity math on 8xH100 (640GB - 65.6GB weights): max batch at 128K drops from 16.7 (target-only) to 11.6 with full-KV 1.7B drafter (-31% throughput capacity); at 512K from 4.2 to 2.9.
analyses.conclusion: H2 confirmed and stronger than expected: a full-KV GQA drafter's KV is material from batch 1 at every context >=32K (+44% KV footprint for Qwen3 family, +25% for Llama), because small GQA models do not have proportionally small KV. Drafter KV must be sparse/windowed/shared at 128K+, full stop. LongSpec's cross-attention-into-target-KV (zero duplicate storage) and QuantSpec's shared hierarchical INT4/8 KV are the arithmetically correct designs.

analyses.topic: 2a. Roofline validation and AR decode baseline (H100 3.35TB/s, 990 TF BF16, ridge 296 FLOP/B; B200 8TB/s, ridge ~281)
analyses.math: Decode step time (memory-bound) = (W_bytes + B x S x kvB)/BW. Validation: Llama-3.1-8B at 500K -> (16.1GB + 65.5GB)/3.35TB/s = 24.4ms vs VeriCache's published 25ms — model is accurate to 3%. Qwen3-32B (W=65.6GB bf16) per-step ms on one H100-equiv BW: B=1: 22.1/29.8/60.6/101.6 at 32K/128K/512K/1M; B=32: 101.6/347.8/1332/2645. KV share of bytes at B=8, 128K: 274.9GB KV vs 65.6GB weights = 81% of traffic; at B=1, 128K KV is only 34% (weights still dominate a GQA 32B at batch 1).
analyses.conclusion: At batch 1 even 128K GQA decode is still weight-dominated for a 32B model (KV=34% of bytes); KV traffic only dominates at (B>=8, 128K+) or (B=1, 512K+). Any drafting scheme whose savings target only KV reads does nothing about the weight term and vice versa — which term you must attack depends on (B,S), and this single fact organizes every verdict below.

analyses.math: Speedup = tau/(L·c+1), c = t_draft/t_target = (W_d + B·S·kvB_d)/(W_t + B·S·kvB_t); verification of L+1 tokens costs ~1 target step while B(L+1) < ridge=296 FLOP/byte. Win condition: c < (tau-1)/L = 0.5 at tau=3, L=4. Qwen3-1.7B full-KV vs Qwen3-32B: B=1: c=0.096/0.184/0.313/0.363 at 32K/128K/512K/1M -> speedup 2.16x/1.73x/1.33x/1.22x. B=32: c=0.363/0.416/0.432/0.435 -> 1.22x/1.13x/1.10x/1.10x. Asymptote: c -> kvB_d/kvB_t = 112/256 = 0.4375 as B·S -> inf, i.e. speedup -> 3/2.75 = 1.09x even at perfect acceptance-per-length. Using survey acceptance instead of assumed tau makes it worse: OWL measures EAGLE-3 at 0.81x (accepted len 1.28) on 4K-64K inputs; BudgetDraft measures naive sparse-KV drafting acceptance 0.3% at 8K.
analyses.conclusion: The independent full-KV small drafter dies twice at long context: arithmetically (c climbs toward the kv-per-token ratio ~0.44, capping speedup at ~1.1x for Qwen3-family pairs regardless of acceptance) and empirically (trained-short acceptance collapses per OWL/BudgetDraft). This direction is dead at 128K+ for GQA targets.

analyses.math: Same 1.7B weights, 4K KV budget: c = (3.4GB + B·4096·112KB)/(65.6GB + B·S·256KB). B=1: c=0.052/0.039/0.019/0.011 -> speedup 2.48x/2.60x/2.79x/2.87x at 32K/128K/512K/1M. B=32: c falls to 0.016 at 128K and 0.002 at 1M -> 2.82x/2.98x, i.e. speedup INCREASES with both S and B and asymptotes to tau. Acceptance evidence supports tau~3-6 here: TriForce alpha=0.9649 at 120K/4K budget, Vegas ~6.1 accepted at gamma=7 at 96-120K, SparseSpec 6.16/8, QuantSpec 94.3% at 128K. With tau=4.1 (alpha=0.9, gamma=4): 4.1/(4x0.016+1) = 3.85x at B=32, 128K.
analyses.conclusion: Sparse-KV drafting is the direction the arithmetic loves: c becomes S-independent while t_target grows linearly in S, so speedup monotonically approaches tau as context and batch grow. The binding constraint shifts entirely from draft cost to (a) acceptance of the sparse draft (empirically holds 0.9+ when selection is attention-retrieval, collapses for eviction per TriForce's H2O/StreamingLLM needle numbers) and (b) the verify pass itself.

analyses.math: Skipping k of N layers removes exactly the fraction k of BOTH weight reads and KV reads (remaining layers still read full-length KV): c = 1-k, independent of S and B. Published viable skip ratios ~40-50% (SWIFT/CLaSp/KnapSpec) -> c = 0.5-0.6 -> speedup tau/(L·c+1) = 3/(4x0.5+1) = 1.00x at tau=3, L=4; even at 70% skip, only 1.36x. This reproduces the literature exactly: KnapSpec peak 1.47x, SWIFT 1.33x, CLaSp 1.22-1.73x — and none is measured past 16K because the ratio c=1-k does not improve with context. Bytes at Qwen3-32B, B=8, 128K: full step 340GB; 50% layer-skip draft 170GB; sparse-4K draft (all layers) 74GB; sparse cuts 4.6x more than skip. For layer skip to match a 4K-budget sparse draft at 128K/B=8 it would need k = 1 - 74/340 = 78% of layers skipped, at which acceptance is not survivable (no published result skips >50% and keeps alpha>0.8).
analyses.conclusion: Layer skip is S-invariant: it can never exploit the very thing that makes long context expensive. Its draft-side saving is hard-capped at (1-k) ~ 0.5, explaining why no layer-skip paper exceeds ~1.5-1.7x or reports 32K+ curves. At 128K+ sparse-KV is the strictly bigger lever (4-30x larger byte reduction on the draft path). Layer skip survives only as a small multiplier on the weight term (see #5).

analyses.topic: 4. Verify-pass dominance and the remaining ceiling for sparse-KV drafting
analyses.math: With a cheap drafter (c->0), iteration time -> t_verify ~= t_AR-step (full weights + full KV, batched over L+1 tokens; still memory-bound since KV-byte intensity = (L+1)·g = 5x8 = 40 << 296, weight-byte intensity = B(L+1)). Ceiling tok/s/request = tau/t_verify. Qwen3-32B, B=1, H100: 135/101/49/30 tok/s at 32K/128K/512K/1M for tau=3; 59 tok/s at 1M even at tau=6; B200 only rescales by 2.4x (70 tok/s at 1M, tau=3). Draft share of round at 128K/B=1: 4 sparse draft steps = 4x3.86GB = 15.4GB vs verify 96GB -> verify is 86% of round time. Speed-of-light theory (arXiv 2512.11718): E[accepted] <= O(log P), so tau cannot be scaled to compensate the linear-in-S verify cost.
analyses.conclusion: Once the drafter is sparse, verification is 85-95% of wall time and the ceiling is tau x (bandwidth / full-KV bytes) — linear degradation in S that no drafter can touch, and tau is theoretically log-bounded. The remaining levers are exactly the ones the 2025-26 literature is converging on: cut verify KV bytes losslessly (QuantSpec INT4 KV shared rep, 2.88x faster kernel; MLA 3.7x fewer bytes), overlap verify off-GPU (VeriCache PCIe-overlapped full-KV verify, 25-40 tok/round), or accept lossiness (SpecPV partial verify: 6.29x at 60K but ROUGE-L 77.3->56.1 — the distribution guarantee is gone; Dustin same caveat). Lossless verify-byte reduction is the frontier, not better drafting.

analyses.topic: 5. Combined layer-skip + sparse-KV self-drafting: multiplicative cost, sub-additive speedup, acceptance-coupled
analyses.math: Cost composes multiplicatively: c_comb = (1-k) x (W + B·S_budget·kvB)/(W + B·S·kvB). Qwen3-32B, 50% skip + 4K budget, target-weight self-draft: B=1: c=0.449/0.334/0.164/0.098 -> 1.07x/1.29x/1.81x/2.16x (vs sparse-only 0.82x-1.68x at B=1, skip-only ~1.0x); B=32: 1.89x/2.56x/2.87x/2.93x vs sparse-only 1.38x/2.23x/2.75x/2.87x. Marginal gain of adding skip on top of sparse at B=32,1M: 2.87x->2.93x (+2%), because speedup = tau/(L·c+1) saturates: once L·c << 1 the '+1' (verify) dominates and halving c again buys ~nothing. Acceptance couples: if alpha_skip=0.85 and alpha_sparse=0.9 are ~independent error sources, alpha_comb ~ 0.765, dropping tau(gamma=4) from 4.10 to 3.14 (-23%) — which can exceed the +2-15% cost saving. Regime where combination genuinely pays: weight-dominated draft path, i.e. small batch AND self-drafting with full target weights (B=1, 512K: 1.30x -> 1.81x, +39%).
analyses.conclusion: Not additive, not cleanly multiplicative in end-to-end speedup: multiplicative in draft cost, sub-additive in speedup (saturating in 1/(L·c+1)), and multiplicative-DOWNWARD in acceptance. At B>=8 and 128K+ the combination is largely redundant — sparse-KV alone already drives the draft path to its weight floor and layer skip only shaves that floor. The combination is worth building only for batch-1 self-spec with big targets (weight-dominated draft), which is precisely SWIFT/CLaSp territory extended with a sparse cache — expected win there is +30-40%, not a multiply of headline speedups.

analyses.topic: 6. Self-spec via target-weights + sparse KV (TriForce/MagicDec style): the batch x context regime boundary
analyses.math: c = (W_t + B·budget·kvB)/(W_t + B·S·kvB). Qwen3-32B: B=1: c=0.90/0.67/0.33/0.20 -> 0.65x/0.82x/1.30x/1.68x — LOSES below ~400K at batch 1 because GQA keeps KV below weights. B=8: 0.93x/1.60x/2.39x/2.65x; B=32: 1.38x/2.23x/2.75x/2.87x. Win condition c<0.5 <=> B·S·kvB > W_t (KV bytes exceed weight bytes): S_inflection = W/(B·kvB) = 65.6GB/(B x 256KB) = 256K/B tokens — B=8 needs 32K, B=32 needs 8K. Cross-check MHA: TriForce Llama2-7B (MHA, 512KB/tok, W=13.5GB) at 122K/B=1: c=0.20, modeled 2.03x (tau=4.5,L=6) vs paper 2.31x (tree) — consistent; S_inflection for MHA-7B/B=1 is 26K vs GQA-32B's 256K. MagicDec's measured boundary (~4K on 8xA100 at batch 32-64) matches: 256K/32 = 8K, of the same order.
analyses.conclusion: Target-weight self-drafting with sparse KV is regime-gated by B·S·kvB > W: dead at batch 1 below ~400K context for GQA models (this is why TriForce used an MHA model and why MagicDec needs batch 32+), excellent at (B>=8, 128K+) where it hits 1.6-2.9x. GQA raised S_inflection ~10x vs MHA — exactly MagicDec-part2's finding — and MLA raises it out of reach (see #7).

analyses.math: MLA KV = 69KB/tok (61L x 576 x 2B), i.e. 3.7x less than Qwen3-32B per token with 20x more parameters. FP8 weights = 671GB. KV share of decode bytes: B=1,128K: 1.4%; B=1,1M: 9.9%; B=32,128K: 30.5%; only at B=32,1M (78%) or B=128 (64-93%) does KV dominate. A sparse-KV drafter at B=1-32, 128K can therefore cut at most 1.4-30% of bytes -> max draft-side speedup 1.01-1.43x before acceptance losses. Meanwhile shared-weight MTP attacks the 671GB weight term directly: tau~1.85 (85-90% second-token acceptance) -> 1.8x measured, matching tau/(L·c+1) with c~0.1 (MTP module ~1 extra layer, 5.7B). Also verification on MLA is compute-lean: absorbed-MLA arithmetic intensity is ~2 OOM above MHA (arXiv 2507.15465), so batched verify FLOPs approach the ridge sooner — but GLA-style kernels (2x faster than FlashMLA at q_len>1, arXiv 2505.21487) exist precisely for this.
analyses.conclusion: For MLA targets, sparse-KV drafting is arithmetic malpractice below batch ~64: the KV term it attacks is 1-30% of traffic. Weight-amortizing speculation (MTP/shared-weight self-draft, larger verify batches) is the only lever with headroom, which is exactly what DeepSeek shipped. KV-centric spec-decode research does not transfer to MLA; the 128K-1M MLA question is instead whether MTP acceptance survives long context — still unpublished.

analyses.topic: 8. Batch ceiling: when verification stops being free
analyses.math: Verification of L+1 tokens is 'one step's cost' only while memory-bound. Weight-stream intensity during verify = B(L+1) FLOP/weight-byte (bf16). H100 ridge 296: B(L+1) > 296 -> compute-bound. L+1=5: B>59; L+1=8: B>37; with tree width w, B(L+1)w hits the ridge proportionally sooner. Past the ridge, verify cost scales ~(L+1) and speedup -> tau/(L·c + (L+1)·t_compute/t_mem-AR) — the free-verification premise collapses. This is the arithmetic behind the measured concurrency decay: Meta 2-3x (bs=1) -> 1.4-2.0x production; P-EAGLE +55-69% (c=1) -> +5-25% (c=64); EAGLE 3.1 2.03x -> 1.66x at c=16 on GB200. But long context postpones the ridge: at 512K the KV stream (intensity (L+1)·g = 40 « 296) dilutes weight traffic, keeping the aggregate memory-bound at higher B — spec decoding and long context are batch-complementary (MagicDec's core claim, confirmed).
analyses.conclusion: At short context, big batches kill speculation (compute-bound verify); at 128K-1M the KV stream keeps the pipeline memory-bound to much larger batches, so speculation and batching stop competing. Draft length should shrink with batch (B(L+1) < ~300 budget) — supporting dynamic-gamma work (SpecDec++, DSpark, SmartSpec) as necessary, not optional, at high load.

direction_verdicts: DIES at 128K+: independent full-KV small drafter (EAGLE-style or standalone 1-2B with its own dense KV). Arithmetic: GQA floors drafter kv/token at 8 heads, so c -> kvB_d/kvB_t ~ 0.25-0.44 as B·S grows, capping speedup at ~1.1-1.3x even at perfect acceptance; capacity cost is +25-44% KV per request from batch 1. Empirics agree (OWL: EAGLE-3 0.81x; BudgetDraft acceptance ~0 at 16K).

DIES as a headline direction: layer-skip self-speculation alone. c = 1-k is context-invariant, capped at ~0.5 by acceptance-viable skip ratios -> speedup ceiling ~1.0-1.5x at tau=3-4, matching every published number (SWIFT 1.33x, CLaSp 1.22-1.73x, KnapSpec 1.47x); it cannot touch the KV term that dominates 128K+ traffic. Survives only as a secondary multiplier on the weight floor in batch-1 self-spec.

SURVIVES AND STRENGTHENS: sparse-KV drafting with attention-retrieval selection (TriForce/Quest/Vegas/SparseSpec/MagicDec lineage). c is S-independent while target cost grows linearly in S, so speedup rises monotonically toward tau with both context and batch (modeled 2.6-3.0x at tau=3, 3.8x+ at tau=4.1, B=32, 128K); acceptance empirically holds 0.9-0.96 at 100K+ for retrieval-selected (not eviction-selected) caches. Requirement: budget must grow slowly with S (Vegas) and selection must come from verification attention (free signal).

SURVIVES with a regime gate: target-weight self-drafting over sparse KV (MagicDec-style) — wins iff B·S·kvB > W_target (S_inflection = 256K/B for Qwen3-32B-class GQA; ~26K for MHA-7B). Dead at batch 1 under ~400K for GQA; 1.6-2.9x at (B>=8, 128K+). GQA raised the bar 10x vs MHA; check the inequality before building.

DIES on MLA targets below batch ~64: all KV-centric drafting/compression speculation. MLA KV is 1-30% of decode bytes at B=1-32 up to 128K -> max theoretical gain 1.01-1.43x. Weight-amortizing shared-weight MTP speculation is the only surviving lever for DeepSeek-class models (measured 1.8x), and its acceptance-vs-context curve at 128K+ is the open measurement nobody has published.

MOSTLY REDUNDANT: combining layer-skip with sparse-KV drafting at 128K+ and B>=8 — cost saving is multiplicative but end-to-end speedup saturates (2.87x -> 2.93x at B=32/1M, +2%) while acceptance degrades multiplicatively (alpha 0.9x0.85 -> 0.765, tau -23%), so the combination can be net-negative. Genuine niche: batch-1 big-target self-spec where the draft path is weight-dominated (+30-40% at 512K-1M).

THE NEW BOTTLENECK AND OPEN DIRECTION: lossless verify-byte reduction. With cheap sparse drafting, full-KV verification is 85-95% of round time and hard-caps throughput at tau·BW/(W + S·kvB) — 30 tok/s at 1M on H100 (70 on B200) at tau=3, with tau log-bounded in verifier capacity (arXiv 2512.11718). Surviving approaches: shared quantized-KV verify (QuantSpec, acceptance rises with context to 94% at 128K), offload-overlapped full-KV verify (VeriCache, bit-identical, 25-40 tok/round), MLA/GQA-at-verify kernels (GLA 2x at q_len>1). Lossy partial verification (SpecPV/Dustin) buys 6x+ but silently abandons the target distribution (ROUGE-L -27%) — it should be classified as a different, lossy primitive, not speculative decoding.

OPERATIONAL COROLLARY: draft length must shrink with batch — verification exits the memory-bound regime at B(L+1) ~ 300 FLOP/byte on H100/B200 (B>59 at L=4), the arithmetic behind all measured concurrency decay (Meta, P-EAGLE, EAGLE-3.1/GB200); long context postpones this ridge because low-intensity KV traffic ((L+1)·g ~ 40) re-anchors the pipeline memory-bound, making speculation and batching complementary at 128K-1M exactly where they conflict at 4K.
